- Contrast. Web: Title text/primary; body text/secondary 6.4:1; pill text #3D2600 on #FAAF39 7.6:1. Confirmation text/action on the gradient is about 2.4:1 in light; lime in dark. Android: Same tokens.
- State. Web: "notified" swaps the button for text with a check icon, so not colour alone; role=status announces it. Android: Same, announced through the polite live region.
- Motion. Web: Static. Android: Static.

Known accessibility gaps:
- Notify pill is 32 px / 32 dp high with no 48 dp target (SystemStatus.tsx, SystemStatus.kt).
- After Notify is tapped the button unmounts and keyboard focus is lost; move focus to the confirmation (SystemStatus.tsx).
- Notified confirmation uses text/action #00B140 on gradient/status-card (about 2.4:1) in light (SystemStatus.tsx, SystemStatus.kt).
- Compose title has no semantics { heading() } (SystemStatus.kt).

Example: Unavailable
```tsx
<SystemStatusCard onNotify={subscribeToRecovery} />
```
```kotlin
SystemStatusCard(state = SystemStatusState.Unavailable, onNotifyClick = {})
```

Example: Notify requested
```tsx
<SystemStatusCard state="notified" />
```
```kotlin
// The confirmation is not tappable, so onNotifyClick is never called in this state
SystemStatusCard(state = SystemStatusState.Notified, onNotifyClick = {})
```

Example: In the Chats header
```tsx
<HomeHeader assistantOn={on} status={down ? <SystemStatusCard state={notify} onNotify={subscribe} /> : undefined} />
```
```kotlin
var on by remember { mutableStateOf(true) }
var notify by remember { mutableStateOf(SystemStatusState.Unavailable) }
val down = true
HomeHeader(
    assistantOn = on,
    onAssistantChange = { on = it },
    status = if (down) {
        { SystemStatusCard(state = notify, onNotifyClick = { notify = SystemStatusState.Notified }) }
    } else {
        null
    },
)
```

entries.name: whats-new-card
entries.title: What's New card
entries.summary: A dismissible announcement card with the NEW FEATURE badge, a heading, body copy and one CTA. Built in three layers: a flat fill, a blurred circle in the bottom-right corner, and the illustration on top of the circle.
entries.text:
# What's New card (`whats-new-card`)
Group: Cards

A dismissible announcement card with the NEW FEATURE badge, a heading, body copy and one CTA. Built in three layers: a flat fill, a blurred circle in the bottom-right corner, and the illustration on top of the circle.

- React: `import { WhatsNewCard } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `WhatsNewCard`
- Tokens: `whats-new/bg`, `whats-new/glow`, `badge/new-feature-stroke`, `text/action`, `text/secondary`, `text/placeholder`, `button/primary`
- Source: §22 What's New Card

Do: Keep the body to about two lines and one CTA that goes straight to the feature. Always offer onDismiss on the Chats list so the card can go away.

Don't: Don't stack more than one What's New card at a time. Don't add a second button; the card has a single commit.

Anatomy:
1. Card: Flat green-tint card with clipped layers. (width 322 · min height 172 · radius 20 · whats-new/bg · padding 18 16 18 18)
2. Glow: Blurred circle bottom-right. (150 circle blur 32 (web) / 230 dp radial gradient (Compose) · whats-new/glow)
3. Illustration: Robot art on the right. (125 · right 4 · top 35)
4. Feature badge: NEW FEATURE pill. (24 high · bg/surface · 1 px badge/new-feature-stroke · ⭐ 11 · badge text/secondary)
5. Heading: What the feature is. (18/24 Bold · text/action)
6. Body: About two lines. (caption Regular · text/secondary)
7. CTA: One filled button. (Button md 36 high · leading icon · button/primary · text/on-action)
8. Close: Optional dismiss. (32 · icon 22 · text/placeholder · top 8 right 8)

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: Heading is an <h3>; CTA and close are <button>s; illustration and glow are decorative (alt="", aria-hidden). Android: Heading is plain text (no heading()); CTA EqualButton Role.Button; close Box Role.Button.
- Name. Web: CTA from its label; close aria-label "Dismiss". Android: CTA from its label; close icon contentDescription "Close".
- Keyboard. Web: Tab to the CTA, then Dismiss; Enter/Space activates. Android: TalkBack: swipe to CTA and Close.
- Touch target. Web: CTA is a 36 px md button with no eq-touch; close is 32 px with eq-touch (48 px). Android: CTA uses minimumInteractiveComponentSize (48 dp); close is 32 dp plain clickable.
- Contrast. Web: Body text/secondary 6.9:1. Heading text/action on #EAFBE6 is 2.6:1 and close #AAAAAA 2.15:1 in light; in dark lime heading is 11.9:1. CTA text white on #00B140 2.85:1 (black on lime in dark 17:1). Android: Same tokens.
- State. Web: No state. Android: No state.
- Motion. Web: Static; button press scale goes to 0 ms under reduced motion. Android: Static.

Known accessibility gaps:
- Heading text/action #00B140 on whats-new/bg is 2.6:1 in light, below 4.5:1 for 18 px text (WhatsNewCard.tsx, Cards.kt).
- Close icon text/placeholder #AAAAAA on whats-new/bg is 2.15:1, below 3:1 (WhatsNewCard.tsx, Cards.kt).
- CTA Button md is 36 px high with no eq-touch, below 48 px (Button.tsx / WhatsNewCard.tsx).
- Close button is 32 dp with no minimumInteractiveComponentSize (Cards.kt).
- Compose heading has no semantics { heading() } (Cards.kt).
- Primary button label white on #00B140 is 2.85:1 in light (Button.css, Buttons.kt).

Example: Default
```tsx
<WhatsNewCard width="100%" heading="Language Preference"
  body="Set your preferred language and choose how your assistant sounds"
  ctaLabel="Try Voices" ctaIcon="translate" onCta={openVoices} onDismiss={dismiss} />
```
```kotlin
WhatsNewCard(
    title = "Language Preference",
    body = "Set your preferred language and choose how your assistant sounds",
    buttonLabel = "Try Voices",
    buttonIcon = EqualIcons.Translate,
    onButtonClick = {},
    onCloseClick = {},
)
```

Example: Custom badge and icon, not dismissible
```tsx
<WhatsNewCard width="100%" badge="Just added" heading="Instructions"
  body="Tell your assistant how to handle deliveries, sales calls and more."
  ctaLabel="Add instruction" ctaIcon="add" />
```
```kotlin
WhatsNewCard(
    badgeText = "Just added",
    title = "Instructions",
    body = "Tell your assistant how to handle deliveries, sales calls and more.",
    buttonLabel = "Add instruction",
    buttonIcon = EqualIcons.Add,
    onButtonClick = {},
    onCloseClick = null, // null hides the close (X)
)
```

entries.name: ai-panel
entries.title: AI panel
entries.summary: The assistant's bottom panel inside a conversation: a suggestion from the orb, large action chips and a composer; AiSuggestion is the avatar-plus-prompt line on its own.
entries.text:
# AI panel (`ai-panel`)
Group: Chat

The assistant's bottom panel inside a conversation: a suggestion from the orb, large action chips and a composer; AiSuggestion is the avatar-plus-prompt line on its own.

- React: `import { AiChatPanel, AiSuggestion } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `AiChatPanel`, `AiSuggestion`
- Tokens: `bg/surface`, `text/secondary`, `text/primary`, `gradient/chip-large`, `action/stroke/unread`
- Source: §12b AI Chat — Within other conversation · §16 AI Suggestion

Do: Phrase the prompt as a question the user can answer with one chip ("Want me to send Amit a quick reply on WhatsApp?"). Offer at most two or three emoji chips, the most likely one first. Hide the composer (composer={false}) when only a quick decision makes sense, like during a live call.

Don't: Don't put a filled Button in the panel; the actions are large chips. Don't write the prompt in green; the assistant's words are text/secondary here.

Anatomy:
1. Panel: Bottom sheet-like panel with rounded top corners. (bg/surface · radius 24 24 0 0 · padding 20 16 16 · shadow 0 -4 16)
2. Suggestion: Equal orb and the assistant's prompt. (AiAvatar 36 · gap 12 · body1 text/secondary)
3. Action chips: Horizontally scrolling row of large emoji chips. (margin-top 20 (web) / 24 (Compose) · gap 6 · LargeActionChip 40 high · gradient/chip-large · 1 px action/stroke/unread · button text/primary)
4. Composer: Message input with the send button. (margin-top 16 (web) / 20 (Compose) · input 45 high radius full · send 45 circle)
5. AiSuggestion: line: Avatar plus prompt on its own. (AiAvatar 36 · gap 12 · body1 · tone primary or secondary (web))

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: Panel is a <section>; chips are <button>s; composer is a <form> with an <input> and a submit <button>. Android: Column; chips clickable(role = Role.Button); VoiceInputBar is a BasicTextField plus a Role.Button send.
- Name. Web: Orb role=img "Equal AI"; chips from their label (emoji is aria-hidden); input aria-label "Message"; send aria-label "Send". Android: AiAvatar "Equal AI"; chips read label and the emoji glyph; send contentDescription "Send"; the text field has no label beyond the placeholder.
- Keyboard. Web: Tab through chips, input and send; Enter submits; send is disabled while the input is empty. Android: TalkBack: swipe to chips, field and send; IME Send action submits.
- Touch target. Web: Chips are 40 px high with no eq-touch; send is 45 px. Android: Chips use minimumInteractiveComponentSize (48 dp); send is 45 dp.
- Contrast. Web: Prompt text/secondary 7.5:1 on white; chip text text/primary; placeholder text/tertiary 5.1:1. Chip border #9DDDB4 is 1.56:1 but the text marks the control. Android: Same tokens.
- State. Web: Send uses the native disabled attribute when empty. Android: Send clickable enabled = false when empty; disabled chips draw at 45% and ignore taps.
- Motion. Web: eq-pressable press scale and composer border transitions go to 0 ms under reduced motion. Android: Press feedback only.

Known accessibility gaps:
- LargeActionChip is 40 px high with no eq-touch (ActionChip.css), below the 48 px target on web.
- Compose LargeActionChip draws the emoji with EmojiGlyph, which TalkBack reads aloud; web hides it (ActionChips.kt).
- VoiceInputBar text field has no accessible label, only placeholder text (Composer.kt).

Example: After a call
```tsx
<AiChatPanel
  prompt="Want me to send Amit a quick reply on WhatsApp?"
  actions={[
    { label: 'Reply on WhatsApp', emoji: '💬' },
    { label: 'Add to Calendar', emoji: '🗓️' },
  ]}
  composer={{ onSend: send }} />
```
```kotlin
var draft by remember { mutableStateOf("") }

AiChatPanel(
    prompt = "Want me to send Amit a quick reply on WhatsApp?",
    actions = listOf(
        ActionChipData("Reply on WhatsApp", "💬"),
        ActionChipData("Add to Calendar", "🗓️"),
    ),
    onActionClick = {},
    composerValue = draft,
    onComposerValueChange = { draft = it },
    onSend = {},
)
```

Example: During a live call, no composer
```tsx
<AiChatPanel
  prompt="Arnav is at the gate with a parcel. Want to take over?"
  actions={[
    { label: 'Takeover', emoji: '📞' },
    { label: 'Ask to reschedule', emoji: '🗓️' },
  ]}
  composer={false} />
```
```kotlin
var draft by remember { mutableStateOf("") }

// Compose: AiChatPanel always shows the composer; there is no composer = false.
AiChatPanel(
    prompt = "Arnav is at the gate with a parcel. Want to take over?",
    actions = listOf(
        ActionChipData("Takeover", "📞"),
        ActionChipData("Ask to reschedule", "🗓️"),
    ),
    onActionClick = {},
    composerValue = draft,
    onComposerValueChange = { draft = it },
    onSend = {},
)
```

Example: AI suggestion
```tsx
<AiSuggestion>Want me to send Amit a quick reply on WhatsApp?</AiSuggestion>
<AiSuggestion tone="secondary">I can also add Sunday dinner to your calendar.</AiSuggestion>
```
```kotlin
Column(verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(16.dp)) {
    AiSuggestion("Want me to send Amit a quick reply on WhatsApp?")
    // Compose: no `tone`; AiSuggestion is always text/primary.
    AiSuggestion("I can also add Sunday dinner to your calendar.")
}
```

entries.name: call-status
entries.title: Call status
entries.summary: Centred thread markers: the day divider, call start/end events, and a notice when the thread switches to the assistant.
entries.text:
# Call status (`call-status`)
Group: Chat

Centred thread markers: the day divider, call start/end events, and a notice when the thread switches to the assistant.

- React: `import { DayDivider, ThreadEvent, ThreadNotice } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `DayDivider`, `ThreadEvent`, `ThreadNotice`
- Tokens: `bg/surface`, `stroke/subtle`, `text/primary`, `text/secondary`, `notice/bg`
- Source: §21 Call Status Indicators

Props of `DayDivider`:
- `label`: `string`. "Today", "12 July".

Props of `ThreadEvent`:
- `label`: `string`. "Call Started 03:31", "Call Ended 03:31".

Props of `ThreadNotice`:
- `children`: `ReactNode`. Notice text (captionWrap, centred, max width 240).

Do: Bracket every call with Call Started / Call Ended events. Use a ThreadNotice when the conversation changes hands ("You are now talking to your AI assistant").

Don't: Don't use a ThreadNotice for ordinary messages; it is for system state changes only. Don't style these as bubbles; they are centred pills without avatars.

Anatomy:
1. DayDivider: Centred pill naming the day. (24 high (web) / 22 dp (Compose) · padding 0 14 · radius 8 · bg/surface · 1 px stroke/subtle · micro text/primary)
2. ThreadEvent: Same pill for call start and end. (micro · text/secondary)
3. ThreadNotice: Centred note when the thread changes hands. (max width 240 (web) / 232 dp (Compose) · padding 8 16 · radius 8 · notice/bg · captionWrap text/secondary centred)

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: Plain divs and spans with text; no separator or status role. Android: Plain Box + EqualText; no extra semantics.
- Name. Web: Read as their visible text ("Today", "Call Started 03:31"). Android: Read as their visible text.
- Keyboard. Web: Not focusable; read in order when browsing. Android: TalkBack: swipe to each as plain text.
- Contrast. Web: DayDivider text/primary on white; ThreadEvent text/secondary 7.5:1; notice text/secondary on notice/bg 7.2:1 (dark 7.5:1). Android: Same tokens.
- State. Web: No state. Android: No state.
- Motion. Web: No animation. Android: No animation.

Example: All indicators
```tsx
<MessageList>
  <DayDivider label="Today" />
  <ThreadEvent label="Call Started 03:31" />
  <ThreadEvent label="Call Ended 03:31" />
  <ThreadNotice>Call has ended. You are now talking to your AI assistant.</ThreadNotice>
</MessageList>
```
```kotlin
Column(
    Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    horizontalAlignment = Alignment.CenterHorizontally,
    verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(12.dp),
) {
    DayDivider("Today")
    ThreadEvent("Call Started 03:31")
    ThreadEvent("Call Ended 03:31")
    ThreadNotice("Call has ended. You are now talking to your AI assistant.")
}
```

Example: In a thread
```tsx
<ChatWallpaper>
  <MessageList>
    <DayDivider label="12 July" />
    <ThreadEvent label="Call Started 18:02" />
    <ChatBubble kind="outgoing" sender="Equal AI" time="18:02">Hi, who is this?</ChatBubble>
    …
    <ThreadEvent label="Call Ended 18:04" />
    <ThreadNotice>Call has ended. You are now talking to your AI assistant.</ThreadNotice>
  </MessageList>
</ChatWallpaper>
```
```kotlin
ChatWallpaper {
    Column(
        Modifier.fillMaxWidth().padding(vertical = 16.dp),
        horizontalAlignment = Alignment.CenterHorizontally,
        verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(12.dp),
    ) {
        DayDivider("12 July")
        ThreadEvent("Call Started 18:02")
        ChatBubble(type = ChatBubbleType.Outgoing, sender = "Equal AI", timestamp = "18:02", message = "Hi, who is this?")
        ChatBubble(type = ChatBubbleType.Incoming, incomingCategory = EqualCategory.NA, sender = "Amit Nanda",
            timestamp = "18:02", message = "It's Amit. Dinner at mine this Sunday, 8 PM?")
        ThreadEvent("Call Ended 18:04")
        ThreadNotice("Call has ended. You are now talking to your AI assistant.")
    }
}
```

entries.name: call-summary
entries.title: Call summary
entries.summary: The post-call card in a thread: a recording player with a coded waveform and speed pill, the assistant's summary, and an optional share footer or "Instruction Applied" tag.
entries.text:
# Call summary (`call-summary`)
Group: Chat

The post-call card in a thread: a recording player with a coded waveform and speed pill, the assistant's summary, and an optional share footer or "Instruction Applied" tag.

- React: `import { CallSummary, VoicePlayer } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `CallSummaryBubble`, `VoiceNotePlayer`
- Tokens: `bg/surface`, `voice/player-bg`, `stroke/subtle`, `waveform/bar`, `waveform/bar-played`, `playback/pill-bg`, `text/on-dark`, `text/tertiary`, `text/primary`, `text/action`
- Source: §11 Chat Bubbles · Voice note + Call Summary bubble

Do: Write the summary as the outcome for the user ("Amit invited you to dinner… confirm by tonight"), not a transcript. Tag the card 🪄 "Instruction Applied" when one of the user's instructions handled the call. Keep the same `seed` for a recording so its waveform is stable.

Don't: Don't use an image for the waveform; it is coded. Don't show the player for calls without a recording; use `noRecording`.

Anatomy:
1. Card: White card that holds the recording, the summary and the footer. (width 268 · bg/surface · radius lg (16) · overflow hidden)
2. Voice player: Recording box with play, waveform, speed pill and times. (8 margin · voice/player-bg · radius md (12) · padding 10 / 10 / 6)
3. Play / pause: Toggles playback. (icon 22 · text/secondary · gap 8)
4. Waveform: Coded bars that fill as the recording plays. (28 bars (web) · 3 wide, gap 2, 24 high · waveform/bar · waveform/bar-played)
5. Speed pill: Cycles 1x → 1.2x → 1.5x → 2x. (22 high · padding 0 8 · radius full · playback/pill-bg · caption tabular · text/on-dark)
6. Label and summary: "Call Summary" caption over the summary text. (caption text/tertiary · body1 text/primary · padding 0 10 6)
7. Tag and time: Optional pill (e.g. 🪄 Instruction Applied) and the timestamp. (tag 24 high · padding 0 10 · 1 px stroke/subtle · caption text/secondary · time micro text/tertiary)
8. Share footer: Divider and a centred Share action. (divider stroke/subtle · row 44 · TextButton share icon 18 · button text/action)

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: Play and speed are native <button>s; the waveform is aria-hidden; Share is a <button>. Android: Play: clickable(role = Role.Button); speed: Role.Button with onClickLabel "Change speed"; Share row: Role.Button.
- Name. Web: Play button aria-label switches "Play" / "Pause"; speed aria-label "Playback speed 1x"; Share from its visible text. Android: Play icon contentDescription "Play" / "Pause"; speed reads its label ("1x"); Share reads "Share".
- Keyboard. Web: Tab reaches play, speed and Share; Enter/Space activates. No seek control. Android: TalkBack: swipe to play, speed, Share; double-tap to activate.
- Touch target. Web: Play and speed use eq-touch for a 48 px hit area around the 22 px visuals; Share is a TextButton with eq-touch in a 44 px row. Android: Play is a 22 dp box and the speed pill 22 dp high with plain clickable (no minimumInteractiveComponentSize; only pointer hit-testing expands); Share row 44 dp.
- Contrast. Web: Summary text/primary; label/time text/tertiary 5.1:1; speed text white on #555555 7.5:1; unplayed bars #8A8A8A on #F2F2F2 3.1:1. Share is text/action: In light, text/action #00B140 on white is 2.85:1, below 4.5:1 for text; in dark it is lime #BAFF29 (13:1 on bg/surface #222222). Android: Same tokens.
- State. Web: Play/pause is told by the label, not colour; progress shows by bar colour and by the elapsed time text. Locked audio is aria-hidden behind an Unlock Audio pill. Android: Same; the locked player uses clearAndSetSemantics {} under UnlockAudioPill.
- Motion. Web: Bar colour transition (duration-fast) goes to 0 ms under prefers-reduced-motion via base.css. Android: Waveform progress is driven by the caller; no extra animation.

Known accessibility gaps:
- Share action uses text/action #00B140 on white (2.85:1), below 4.5:1 in light (VoiceNote.tsx, VoiceNote.kt).
- VoiceNotePlayer play button and speed pill are 22 dp with plain clickable and no minimumInteractiveComponentSize (VoiceNote.kt); Share row is 44 dp.
- Playback progress is not exposed to assistive tech (no progressbar/slider or stateDescription) in VoicePlayer (VoiceNote.tsx) or EqualWaveform (VoiceNote.kt).
- CallSummaryBubble tag emoji is drawn with EmojiGlyph, which TalkBack reads aloud ("magic wand"); web hides it (VoiceNote.kt).

Example: With recording and share
```tsx
<CallSummary
  summary="Amit invited you to dinner this Sunday, 8 PM at his place. He asked you to confirm by tonight."
  time="03:21" onShare={share} />
```
```kotlin
var playing by remember { mutableStateOf(false) }
var speed by remember { mutableStateOf(PlaybackSpeed.X1) }

CallSummaryBubble(
    summary = "Amit invited you to dinner this Sunday, 8 PM at his place. He asked you to confirm by tonight.",
    timestamp = "03:21",
    voiceNote = {
        // Compose: the player is controlled; drive progress/elapsed from your media player.
        VoiceNotePlayer(isPlaying = playing, onPlayPauseClick = { playing = !playing },
            progress = 0f, elapsed = "0:00", total = "2:37",
            speed = speed, onSpeedChange = { speed = it })
    },
    onShareClick = {},
)
```

Example: Instruction applied
```tsx
<CallSummary
  summary="Priya from Dr. Mehta's clinic confirmed your appointment for tomorrow at 10 AM. Bring your previous reports."
  time="03:32" tag={{ emoji: '🪄', label: 'Instruction Applied' }} />
```
```kotlin
CallSummaryBubble(
    summary = "Priya from Dr. Mehta's clinic confirmed your appointment for tomorrow at 10 AM. Bring your previous reports.",
    timestamp = "03:32",
    tag = CallSummaryTag(label = "Instruction Applied", emoji = "🪄"),
    modifier = Modifier.width(264.dp),
)
```

Example: Summary only
```tsx
<CallSummary noRecording
  summary="Vijay from NoBroker called with an offer on a 2BHK flat in Sector 12. You said you were not interested and ended the call."
  time="03:21" />
```
```kotlin
// No voiceNote slot = no recording player.
CallSummaryBubble(
    summary = "Vijay from NoBroker called with an offer on a 2BHK flat in Sector 12. You said you were not interested and ended the call.",
    timestamp = "03:21",
)
```

Example: Voice player
```tsx
<VoicePlayer duration={94} seed={7} />
```
```kotlin
var playing by remember { mutableStateOf(false) }
var speed by remember { mutableStateOf(PlaybackSpeed.X1) }

// Compose: no `seed`; pass `samples` for a recording-specific waveform (defaults are fixed).
VoiceNotePlayer(
    isPlaying = playing,
    onPlayPauseClick = { playing = !playing },
    progress = 0f,
    elapsed = "0:00",
    total = "1:34",
    speed = speed,
    onSpeedChange = { speed = it },
)
```

entries.name: chat-bubble
entries.title: Chat bubble
entries.summary: Message bubbles for a call thread: outgoing (Equal AI or you on the call), incoming (the caller) and assistant (Equal AI talking to you), stacked with MessageList.
entries.text:
# Chat bubble (`chat-bubble`)
Group: Chat

Message bubbles for a call thread: outgoing (Equal AI or you on the call), incoming (the caller) and assistant (Equal AI talking to you), stacked with MessageList.

- React: `import { ChatBubble, MessageList } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `ChatBubble`
- Tokens: `chat-bubble/user-bg`, `chat-bubble/user-title`, `chat-bubble/other-bg`, `chat-bubble/contact-title`, `bg/surface`, `text/action`, `text/primary`, `text/tertiary`
- Source: §11 Chat Bubbles

Do: Use `outgoing` with sender "Equal AI" when the assistant speaks for the user on a call, and "You" after a takeover. Use `assistant` only when Equal AI is talking to the user, not to the caller. Set first={false} on consecutive bubbles from the same sender.

Don't: Don't mix up outgoing and assistant; the green byline means Equal AI is addressing you. Don't put custom cards inside a padded bubble; use `bare`.

Anatomy:
1. Avatar: Caller category art (incoming) or the Equal orb (assistant), shown on the first bubble of a group only. (CategoryAvatar 28 dp · AiAvatar 24 dp · 28 dp column, gap 8 · outgoing has none)
2. Bubble container: Rounded fill whose colour and side tell outgoing, incoming and assistant apart. (max width 264 · radius md (12) · padding 8 / 10 / 6 · chat-bubble/user-bg · chat-bubble/other-bg · bg/surface)
3. Tail: Optional notch on the top outer corner of the first bubble. (tail + first · 10 × 12 notch · square top-outer corner (web) · 8 dp gutter (Compose))
4. Sender line: Who is speaking, on the first bubble of a group. (body2 · chat-bubble/user-title (outgoing) · chat-bubble/contact-title (incoming) · text/action (assistant))
5. Message: The message text, or custom content with bare. (body1 · text/primary · bare removes padding)
6. Timestamp: Time of the message, right-aligned. (micro · text/tertiary · 2 dp above)
7. MessageList: stack: Vertical list that applies the group rhythm. (gap 4 · 8 dp extra before a new group · padding 12)

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: Plain divs; the orb is role=img and the category avatar is an img with alt. MessageList is a plain div, not role=log. Android: Plain Row/Column of texts; no mergeDescendants, so sender, message and time are separate TalkBack stops.
- Name. Web: Content is read as text: avatar name ("Equal AI" or the category label), sender, message, time. Android: AiAvatar contentDescription "Equal AI"; CategoryAvatar uses category.label; texts read as written.
- Keyboard. Web: Not interactive; screen readers reach it in reading order. Android: TalkBack: swipe through sender, message and time one by one; should be one merged stop per bubble.
- Contrast. Web: text/primary on all fills; time text/tertiary 4.85:1 on user-bg; incoming sender #9A5B00 5.4:1; outgoing sender #006223 7.2:1. Assistant sender is text/action: In light, text/action #00B140 on white is 2.85:1, below 4.5:1 for text; in dark it is lime #BAFF29 (13:1 on bg/surface #222222). Android: Same tokens as web via EqualTheme.colors.
- State. Web: Side and fill show who sent it; only the first bubble of a group has a sender line, so follow-ups carry no sender for screen readers. Locked bubbles hide the text and read "Locked. Unlock Equal Unlimited to see this." Android: Same; LockedContent uses clearAndSetSemantics with the same locked sentence.
- Motion. Web: No animation. Android: No animation.

Known accessibility gaps:
- Assistant sender line uses text/action #00B140 on bg/surface (2.85:1), below 4.5:1 in light (ChatBubble.tsx, ChatBubble.kt).
- Follow-up bubbles (first={false} / isFirstInGroup = false) have no sender in their accessible text, so a screen reader can't tell who sent them (ChatBubble.tsx, ChatBubble.kt).
- MessageList in ChatBubble.tsx is a plain div; a live call thread should be role="log" so new messages are announced.
- ChatBubble.kt does not merge the bubble (semantics(mergeDescendants = true)), so TalkBack stops on sender, message and time separately.

Example: A call thread
```tsx
<MessageList>
  <ChatBubble kind="outgoing" sender="Equal AI" time="03:21">Hi, who is this?</ChatBubble>
  <ChatBubble kind="incoming" sender="Dr Mehta Clinic" time="03:21">
    This is Priya from Dr. Mehta's clinic. Your appointment is confirmed for tomorrow.
  </ChatBubble>
  <ChatBubble kind="outgoing" sender="You" time="03:21">Yes, I'll be there at 10 AM</ChatBubble>
  <ChatBubble kind="assistant" sender="Equal AI" time="03:21">
    Hey Keshav! Here is the summary of your call
  </ChatBubble>
</MessageList>
```
```kotlin
// Compose: no MessageList; a Column with 12dp spacing gives the between-group rhythm.
Column(verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(12.dp)) {
    ChatBubble(type = ChatBubbleType.Outgoing, sender = "Equal AI", timestamp = "03:21", message = "Hi, who is this?")
    ChatBubble(type = ChatBubbleType.Incoming, sender = "Dr Mehta Clinic", timestamp = "03:21",
        message = "This is Priya from Dr. Mehta's clinic. Your appointment is confirmed for tomorrow.")
    ChatBubble(type = ChatBubbleType.Outgoing, sender = "You", timestamp = "03:21", message = "Yes, I'll be there at 10 AM")
    ChatBubble(type = ChatBubbleType.Incoming, sender = "Dr Mehta Clinic", timestamp = "03:21",
        message = "Great. Please bring your previous reports too.")
    ChatBubble(type = ChatBubbleType.Assistant, sender = "Equal AI", timestamp = "03:21",
        message = "Hey Keshav! Here is the summary of your call")
}
```

Example: Tails and grouping
```tsx
<ChatBubble kind="incoming" category="real-estate" sender="Vijay · NoBroker" time="03:21" tail>
  I have an offer on a 2BHK flat in Sector 12.
</ChatBubble>
<ChatBubble kind="incoming" category="real-estate" first={false} time="03:21">
  Are you free for a site visit this weekend?
</ChatBubble>
<ChatBubble kind="outgoing" sender="Equal AI" time="03:22" tail>
  Thanks, but Keshav is not interested right now.
</ChatBubble>
```
```kotlin
Column {
    ChatBubble(type = ChatBubbleType.Incoming, incomingCategory = EqualCategory.RealEstate,
        sender = "Vijay · NoBroker", timestamp = "03:21", tail = true,
        message = "I have an offer on a 2BHK flat in Sector 12.")
    // Follow-up in the same group: 4dp gap, no avatar, no sender line.
    ChatBubble(type = ChatBubbleType.Incoming, incomingCategory = EqualCategory.RealEstate,
        isFirstInGroup = false, timestamp = "03:21", modifier = Modifier.padding(top = 4.dp),
        message = "Are you free for a site visit this weekend?")
    ChatBubble(type = ChatBubbleType.Outgoing, sender = "Equal AI", timestamp = "03:22", tail = true,
        modifier = Modifier.padding(top = 12.dp), message = "Thanks, but Keshav is not interested right now.")
}
```

Example: Bare content
```tsx
<ChatBubble kind="assistant" bare>
  <CallSummary noRecording summary="Delivery agent will arrive between 4 and 5 PM." time="03:21" />
</ChatBubble>
```
```kotlin
// Compose: ChatBubble has no `bare` mode; lay the AI avatar beside the card yourself.
Row(horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(8.dp)) {
    AiAvatar(size = AiAvatarSize.Small)
    CallSummaryBubble(
        summary = "Delivery agent will arrive between 4 and 5 PM.",
        timestamp = "03:21",
        modifier = Modifier.width(240.dp),
    )
}
```

entries.text:
# Chat list item (`chat-list-item`)
Group: Chat

A row in the Chats list with avatar, name, date, preview, unread count and the small action chips; states come from `unread` and `selected`.

- React: `import { ChatListItem } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `ChatListItem`
- Tokens: `bg/surface`, `action-card/highlight`, `text/primary`, `text/secondary`, `text/action`, `text/tertiary`, `button/primary`, `text/on-action`
- Source: §6 Chat List Item

Do: Give unknown callers their category art and saved contacts their initials. Offer the next step as chips on the row (📞 Call Back, 🗓️ Add to Calendar) so it is one tap from the list. Use long-press to enter selection mode.

Don't: Don't set chip states yourself; the row derives them from unread and selected. Don't let the preview wrap; it is one line with an ellipsis.

Anatomy:
1. Row container: Full-width tappable row; fills green when selected. (padding 12 v / 16 start (web 0 end) · bg/surface · selected action-card/highlight · gap 16)
2. Avatar: Contact avatar or the orb for Equal AI. (48 · selected shows the check badge)
3. Name: Contact name, one line, with a verified tick for the official chat. (subheading 16/500 text/primary · verified 16 text/action, label 'Verified')
4. Date: Time or date of the last message. (micro 12/500 · text/action when unread (web also when selected), else text/tertiary · gap 8)
5. Preview: Last message or summary, blurred when locked. (body1 14/400 text/secondary · one line · locked blur 4)
6. Unread count: CountBadge at the end of the preview line; a crown-lock replaces it when locked. (20 · button/primary · gap 8)
7. Action chips: Scrolling row of SmallActionChips; state follows the row. (margin-top 8 · gap 12 · unread / read / outlined)

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: A <div role='button' tabIndex=0> with aria-selected, containing the chip <button>s. Android: combinedClickable on the Row with no role; chips are separate Role.Button nodes.
- Name. Web: All row text in order: name, 'Verified', date, preview, count; locked previews read 'Locked. Unlock Equal Unlimited to see this.' Android: Merged text of the row; LockedContent replaces the preview with the same locked message.
- Keyboard. Web: Tab to the row, Enter opens it; Space does nothing. Long-press maps to the context-menu event (right-click or the Menu key). Chips are later Tab stops. Android: TalkBack: double-tap opens, double-tap-and-hold triggers onLongClick (no custom label).
- Touch target. Web: Row is at least 72px high and full width; chips use .eq-touch. Android: Row is full width and at least 72dp; chips get 48dp.
- Contrast. Web: Name 17:1, preview text/secondary 7.5:1, read date text/tertiary 5.1:1; unread date text/action #00B140 is 2.85:1 in light (lime in dark passes). Android: Same tokens as web.
- State. Web: Unread shows the count badge as well as a green date; selected sets aria-selected (not valid on role=button) plus the avatar check and highlight fill. The row has outline: none and no focus style. Android: Unread shows the count badge; selected is drawn (fill, check 'Selected') but not set as selected semantics.
- Motion. Web: Background fades over 200ms; zeroed under prefers-reduced-motion. Android: Ripple-free; no animation.

Known accessibility gaps:
- ChatListItem.tsx: role='button' wraps the chip <button>s, which nests interactive controls; the row should be a list item with a separate open button or link.
- ChatListItem.tsx: aria-selected is not supported on role='button'; use aria-pressed, or role='option' / a checkbox in selection mode.
- ChatListItem.tsx: only Enter activates the row; Space should too.
- ChatListItem.tsx: inline outline: none removes the focus indicator and nothing replaces it.
- ChatListItem.kt: combinedClickable has no role, no onLongClickLabel (e.g. 'Select'), and the Selected state is not set in semantics.
- ChatListItem.tsx / ChatListItem.kt: unread date in text/action #00B140 on white is 2.85:1 for 12sp text in light mode.

Example: Unread and read
```tsx
<ChatListItem name="Arnav Raj" preview="You have a visitor" date="Yesterday"
  unread={5} avatar={{ category: 'na' }}
  actions={[
    { label: 'Call Back', emoji: '📞' },
    { label: 'Update Address', emoji: '✏️' },
    { label: 'Add to Calendar', emoji: '🗓️' },
  ]} />
<ChatListItem name="Amit Nanda" preview="Count me in for Sunday 8 PM 👍" date="12 July"
  avatar={{ initials: 'AN' }} actions={[{ label: 'Call Back', emoji: '📞' }]} />
```
```kotlin
ChatListItem(
    name = "Arnav Raj",
    preview = "You have a visitor",
    date = "Yesterday",
    state = ChatListItemState.Unread,
    unreadCount = 5,
    category = EqualCategory.NA,
    chips = listOf(
        ActionChipData("Call Back", "📞"),
        ActionChipData("Update Address", "✏️"),
        ActionChipData("Add to Calendar", "🗓️"),
    ),
)
ChatListItem(
    name = "Amit Nanda",
    preview = "Count me in for Sunday 8 PM 👍",
    date = "12 July",
    initials = "AN",
    chips = listOf(ActionChipData("Call Back", "📞")),
)
```

Example: Long-press to select
```tsx
<ChatListItem name="Dr Mehta Clinic" preview="Appointment confirmed for tomorrow, 10 AM"
  date="03:21" unread={2} avatar={{ category: 'others' }}
  actions={[{ label: 'Add to Calendar', emoji: '🗓️' }, { label: 'Call Back', emoji: '📞' }]}
  selected={selected} onLongPress={() => setSelected(true)} />
```
```kotlin
var selected by remember { mutableStateOf(false) }

ChatListItem(
    name = "Dr Mehta Clinic",
    preview = "Appointment confirmed for tomorrow, 10 AM",
    date = "03:21",
    state = if (selected) ChatListItemState.Selected else ChatListItemState.Unread,
    unreadCount = 2,
    category = EqualCategory.Others,
    chips = listOf(ActionChipData("Add to Calendar", "🗓️"), ActionChipData("Call Back", "📞")),
    onLongClick = { selected = true },
    onClick = { selected = false },
)
```

Example: The list
```tsx
{chats.map((c) => (
  <ChatListItem key={c.id} name={c.name} preview={c.preview} date={c.date}
    unread={c.unread} actions={c.actions}
    avatar={c.initials ? { initials: c.initials } : { category: c.category }} />
))}
```
```kotlin
val callBack = listOf(ActionChipData("Call Back", "📞"))
Column {
    ChatListItem(name = "Amit Nanda", preview = "Count me in for Sunday 8 PM 👍", date = "12 July",
        initials = "AN", chips = callBack)
    ChatListItem(name = "Vijay · NoBroker", preview = "Offer on a 2BHK flat in Sector 12", date = "10 July",
        category = EqualCategory.RealEstate, chips = callBack)
    ChatListItem(name = "Swiggy Delivery", preview = "Your order is at the gate", date = "09 July",
        category = EqualCategory.Delivery, chips = listOf(ActionChipData("Update Address", "✏️")))
    ChatListItem(name = "HDFC Bank", preview = "Pre-approved loan offer. You said not interested", date = "08 July",
        category = EqualCategory.Financial, chips = callBack)
}
```

entries.title: Chat wallpaper
entries.summary: The doodle pattern behind chat threads and the instruction setup chat, tinted by token so one tile serves light and dark.
entries.text:
# Chat wallpaper (`chat-wallpaper`)
Group: Chat

The doodle pattern behind chat threads and the instruction setup chat, tinted by token so one tile serves light and dark.

- React: `import { ChatWallpaper } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `ChatWallpaper`
- Tokens: `chat/wallpaper-bg`, `chat/wallpaper-pattern`
- Source: Flows · Chat wallpaper

Do: Use it behind chat threads and the "Setting up instruction" chat only. Give it minHeight: 100% so the pattern fills short threads.

Don't: Don't put the wallpaper behind lists or settings screens. Don't tint the pattern yourself; it reads chat/wallpaper-pattern in both themes.

Anatomy:
1. Background: Flat fill behind the thread. (chat/wallpaper-bg)
2. Doodle pattern: Tiled doodles masked and tinted by token. (360 × 750 tile · chat/wallpaper-pattern rgba(115,115,115,0.08) · web ::before mask, pointer-events none · Compose drawBehind SrcIn)
3. Content: The thread drawn on top. (children / content slot)

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: Decorative: the pattern is a CSS ::before mask with no semantics. Android: Decorative: drawn in drawBehind, no semantics node.
- Name. Web: None; the pattern should never be announced. Android: None.
- Contrast. Web: The pattern is 8% grey so it stays under text; text contrast is set by the bubbles on top. Android: Same.
- Motion. Web: Static. Android: Static.

Example: Behind a thread
```tsx
<ChatWallpaper style={{ minHeight: '100%' }}>
  <MessageList>
    <DayDivider label="Today" />
    <ChatBubble kind="outgoing" sender="Equal AI" time="03:21">Hi, who is this?</ChatBubble>
    …
  </MessageList>
</ChatWallpaper>
```
```kotlin
ChatWallpaper(Modifier.fillMaxSize()) {
    Column(
        Modifier.fillMaxWidth().padding(vertical = 16.dp),
        horizontalAlignment = Alignment.CenterHorizontally,
        verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(12.dp),
    ) {
        DayDivider("Today")
        ChatBubble(type = ChatBubbleType.Outgoing, sender = "Equal AI", timestamp = "03:21", message = "Hi, who is this?")
        ChatBubble(type = ChatBubbleType.Incoming, sender = "Dr Mehta Clinic", timestamp = "03:21",
            message = "This is Priya from Dr. Mehta's clinic. Your appointment is confirmed for tomorrow.")
    }
}
```

entries.summary: The thread card for a call the assistant couldn’t pick up. One component, three cases: we know why the caller usually calls, we know only their name, or we know nothing. Every case ends in Call back.
entries.text: # Missed call card (`missed-call`) Group: Chat The thread card for a call the assistant couldn’t pick up. One component, three cases: we know why the caller usually calls, we know only their name, or we know nothing. Every case ends in Call back. - React: `import { MissedCallCard } from '@equal/ds';` - Compose: `MissedCallCard` - Tokens: `bg/surface`, `missed-call/bg`, `missed-call/stroke`, `missed-call/icon-bg`, `missed-call/icon`, `text/primary`, `text/secondary`, `text/tertiary`, `text/action`, `stroke/subtle` Do: Pick the case from what we know: reason + art, then name only, then unknown. Never invent a reason. Show thumbs only with a reason, since they rate the reason. Call back opens the same Call Back task as everywhere else (Flows → Call Back). Don't: Don’t colour the whole card red; the warm tint says “missed”, not “error”. Don’t show caller art without a reason; the disc keeps the three cases distinct. Anatomy: 1. Card: White card holding the head, reason and Call back. (width 320 · bg/surface · radius lg (16)) 2. Head: Tinted strip that says the call was missed. (margin 6 · padding 10 / 12 · radius 12 · missed-call/bg · 1 px missed-call/stroke · gap 12) 3. Art or disc: Caller art with a missed badge (with a reason) or the red missed-call disc. (48 · badge 20 missed-call/icon-bg · phone-missed-fill 12 / 24 · missed-call/icon) 4. Title and why: "{caller} Called" or "Missed by the assistant", then why. (subheading text/primary · body2 Regular text/secondary) 5. Likely calls for: Optional reason block with bold key words and the time. (overline text/secondary · body1 Regular text/secondary · padding 4 16 6 · micro time) 6. Call back: Full-width action row. (48 high · call icon 20 · subheading · text/action · 1 px stroke/subtle top) 7. Feedback thumbs: Optional 👍 / 👎 to rate the reason. (40 circles · gap 8 · 1 px stroke/subtle · on: filled icon + text/action stroke) Accessibility: - Role. Web: Call back is a

entries.name: avatars
entries.title: Avatars
entries.summary: Every face in the app: caller category art or initials for contacts, the Equal orb for the assistant, the ringed 3D profile avatar for the user, and the robot mascot.
entries.text: # Avatars (`avatars`) Group: Display Every face in the app: caller category art or initials for contacts, the Equal orb for the assistant, the ringed 3D profile avatar for the user, and the robot mascot. - React: `import { ContactAvatar, CategoryAvatar, AiAvatar, EqualOrb, ProfileAvatar, Mascot } from '@equal/ds';` - Compose: `ContactAvatar`, `CategoryAvatar`, `InitialsAvatar`, `AiAvatar`, `EqualLogoOrb`, `ProfileAvatar`, `EqualMascot` - Tokens: `action-card/highlight`, `text/action`, `button/primary`, `text/on-action`, `bg/surface` - Source: Icons, emoji, categories, logo · §12 AI Assistant Avatar Do: Default unknown callers to `na` and incoming bubbles to `others` (the red telephone). Size ProfileAvatar by width only; its height follows so the head can rise above the ring. Use AiAvatar at 24 / 36 / 48 only. Don't: Never crop category art or the profile avatar; the circle and ring are part of the image. Don't draw your own green circle for the assistant; the orb swaps light (#00B140) and dark (lime) files by theme. Don't use initials for business callers; they get their category art. Anatomy: 1. ContactAvatar: image or disc: Category art for unknown callers, or a tinted disc with initials for saved contacts. (48 list · 36 header · 96 contact info · circle · 6 tones contact-avatar/*-bg) 2. ContactAvatar: initials: First two letters, uppercased. (Medium, 37.5% of size (18 at 48) · contact-avatar/*-text) 3. ContactAvatar: saved badge: Person badge marking a known contact. (36% of size · contact-avatar/badge-bg + badge-icon · bottom-right, offset 10%) 4. ContactAvatar: selected check: Green tick that replaces the saved badge in selection mode. (web 18, Compose 22 incl. 2dp bg/surface ring · button/primary · check 12 text/on-action) 5. AiAvatar / EqualOrb: The Equal orb for the assistant; light and dark files swap with the theme. (24 / 36 / 48 (FAB 58) · image drawn at size / 0.8, glow overflows) 6. ProfileAvatar: The user's 3D character, gold ring when paid. (width 72 default · height ≈ 1.12 × width · free = bust art) 7. Mascot: Robot for the assistant toggle card. (40 default · dimmed = greyscale at 70%) Accessibility: - Role. Web: EqualOrb, Mascot and the saved badge are role='img'; CategoryAvatar and ProfileAvatar are ; the initials disc is plain text. Android: Image with contentDescription; InitialsAvatar is text plus a 'Saved contact' badge node. - Name. Web: Orb 'Equal AI', Mascot 'Equal assistant', ProfileAvatar 'Your profile', CategoryAvatar the category label, saved badge 'Saved contact'. Pass label/alt = '' when a visible name sits beside it. Android: Same defaults via contentDescription; pass null when the row already names the person. SelectedCheckBadge reads 'Selected'. - Contrast. Web: The six initials tones are 4.6–6.5:1 in light and 4.7–8.7:1 in dark. The selected check is white on #00B140 (2.85:1) in light. Android: Same tokens as web. - State. Web: Selected adds a tick shape, not only colour, but the tick has no text alternative. Mascot dimmed is visual only; the toggle beside it states on or off. Android: Selected is announced as 'Selected' via the check's contentDescription. - Motion. Web: Mascot filter and opacity fade over 200ms; zeroed under prefers-reduced-motion. Android: None. Known accessibility gaps: - Avatar.tsx: ContactAvatar's selected check icon is aria-hidden with no label, so selection is not announced on web (Compose says 'Selected'). - Avatar.tsx: default labels ('Your profile', 'Equal AI', category names) are announced even when the avatar sits next to a visible name; components that embed it (e.g. BottomNav) should pass an empty label. Example: Profile avatar: free vs paid ```tsx ``` ```kotlin Row(horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(24.dp)) { ProfileAvatar(variant = ProfileAvatarVariant.Male, width = 70.dp, tier = PlanTier.Free) ProfileAvatar(variant = ProfileAvatarVariant.Male, width = 70.dp, tier = PlanTier.Paid) } ``` Example: Caller categories ```tsx ``` ```kotlin Row(horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(12.dp)) { CategoryAvatar(category = EqualCategory.NA, size = 48.dp) CategoryAvatar(category = EqualCategory.Delivery, size = 48.dp) CategoryAvatar(category = EqualCategory.RealEstate, size = 48.dp) } ``` Example: Contact avatar ```tsx ``` ```kotlin Row(horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(16.dp), verticalAlignment = Alignment.CenterVertically) { ContactAvatar(size = 48.dp) ContactAvatar(size = 48.dp, category = EqualCategory.Others) ContactAvatar(size = 48.dp, initials = "AN") ContactAvatar(size = 48.dp, initials = "AN", selected = true) ContactAvatar(size = 36.dp, category = EqualCategory.Career) } ``` Example: Saved-contact colours ```tsx // tone picked from the initials // blue · green · purple · orange · pink · teal ``` ```kotlin Row(horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(14.dp), verticalAlignment = Alignment.CenterVertically) { // The tone is picked from the initials by default; pass tone to choose. listOf("AN", "AR", "KS", "PR", "VJ", "MS").zip(ContactTone.entries).forEach { (initials, tone) -> InitialsAvatar(initials = initials, size = 48.dp, tone = tone) } } ``` Example: Assistant, user and mascot ```tsx ``` ```kotlin Row(horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(20.dp), verticalAlignment = Alignment.Bottom) { AiAvatar(size = AiAvatarSize.Small) AiAvatar(size = AiAvatarSize.Medium) AiAvatar(size = AiAvatarSize.Large) EqualLogoOrb(size = 58.dp) ProfileAvatar(variant = ProfileAvatarVariant.Male, width = 70.dp) ProfileAvatar(variant = ProfileAvatarVariant.Female, width = 70.dp) EqualMascot(size = 40.dp) EqualMascot(size = 40.dp, dimmed = true) } ```

entries.title: Badges
entries.summary: Small uppercase markers: NEW on settings rows, unread counts, the NEW FEATURE pill on announcements, and the gold UNLIMITED plan marker.
entries.text:
# Badges (`badges`)
Group: Display

Small uppercase markers: NEW on settings rows, unread counts, the NEW FEATURE pill on announcements, and the gold UNLIMITED plan marker.

- React: `import { NewBadge, CountBadge, FeatureBadge, PlanBadge } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `NewBadge`, `CountBadge`, `FeatureBadge`, `PlanBadge`
- Tokens: `button/primary`, `text/on-action`, `bg/surface`, `badge/new-feature-stroke`, `text/secondary`, `gradient/gold`, `text/on-dark`
- Source: §20 Badge

Do: Keep badge text to one or two words; badges never wrap. Pass normal-case strings; the components uppercase badge text in the string (rule 5). Use CountBadge for unread messages only; it hides itself at zero.

Don't: Don't use NewBadge for counts or statuses; it means "new" and nothing else. Don't recolour PlanBadge; the gold gradient marks the plan everywhere (top bar, profile).

Anatomy:
1. NewBadge: container: Small rectangle that marks something new. (16 high · padding h6 · radius/xs 4 · solid button/primary · soft action-card/highlight)
2. NewBadge: label: One word, uppercased in the string. (badge 10/500 · solid text/on-action · soft text/action)
3. CountBadge: circle: Unread count on a green circle. (20 min width / height (16 in nav) · padding h5 for 2+ digits · radius full · button/primary · badgeCount 10/500 text/on-action · web 99+, ring adds 1.5 bg/surface)
4. FeatureBadge: pill: 'NEW FEATURE' pill with a star. (24 high · padding 8/10 · radius full · bg/surface · 1px badge/new-feature-stroke · ⭐ 11 · gap 6 · badge text/secondary)
5. PlanBadge: tag: Plan marker beside the logo (UNLIMITED, PLAN EXPIRED). (16 high · padding h6 · radius 4 · paid gradient/gold + text/on-dark · expired plan-badge/expired-bg #D0302F + white)

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: Plain <span> text; none are interactive. Android: Plain Box/Row with text; no semantics added.
- Name. Web: Read as their text ('NEW', 'UNLIMITED'). CountBadge sets aria-label '{n} unread' on a span with no role, which most screen readers ignore, so they read the bare number. Android: Read as the text; CountBadge reads just the number, with no 'unread'.
- Contrast. Web: Solid NEW white on #00B140 2.85:1 and soft text/action on #DCFFE4 2.6:1 fail 4.5:1 at 10sp; PlanBadge white on gradient/gold is 2.2–4.3:1; expired white on #D0302F 5.1:1; FeatureBadge text/secondary 7.5:1. Dark: black on lime passes. Android: Same tokens as web.
- State. Web: Badges carry state in words or numbers, not colour alone; CountBadge renders nothing at 0. Android: Same; CountBadge caps at max+ (default 99).

Known accessibility gaps:
- Badge.tsx: CountBadge puts aria-label on a span with no role, which is not reliably announced; give it role='img' or visually hidden '{n} unread' text.
- Badges.kt: CountBadge has no semantics, so TalkBack reads a bare number with no 'unread'.
- Badge.css / Badges.kt: NewBadge solid (white on #00B140, 2.85:1) and soft (text/action on #DCFFE4, 2.6:1) fail 4.5:1 for 10sp text in light mode.
- Badge.css / Badges.kt: PlanBadge white text on gradient/gold is 2.2–4.3:1 in both themes.
- Badges.kt: FeatureBadge EmojiGlyph is not hidden, so TalkBack reads 'star' before the label (web hides it).

Example: All badges
```tsx
<NewBadge />
<NewBadge tone="soft" />
<CountBadge count={5} />
<CountBadge count={12} />
<CountBadge count={140} />   {/* renders 99+ */}
<FeatureBadge />
<PlanBadge />
```
```kotlin
Row(horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(16.dp), verticalAlignment = Alignment.CenterVertically) {
    NewBadge()
    // Compose: no tone = "soft"; NewBadge has the solid fill only.
    CountBadge(count = 5)
    CountBadge(count = 12)
    CountBadge(count = 140) // renders 99+
    FeatureBadge()
    PlanBadge()
}
```

Example: In context
```tsx
<TopBar />                                  {/* PlanBadge */}
<SettingsRow icon="instructions" label="Instructions" isNew
  description="Tell assistant how you'd like it to help" />   {/* NewBadge */}
<ChatListItem name="Arnav Raj" preview="You have a visitor"
  date="Yesterday" unread={5} />             {/* CountBadge */}
```
```kotlin
Column {
    TopBar() // PlanBadge
    RowGroup(inset = 0.dp) {
        SettingsRow(
            label = "Instructions",
            description = "Tell assistant how you'd like it to help",
            leadingIcon = EqualIcons.Instructions,
            showNewBadge = true, // NewBadge
        )
    }
    ChatListItem(
        name = "Arnav Raj",
        preview = "You have a visitor",
        date = "Yesterday",
        state = ChatListItemState.Unread,
        unreadCount = 5, // CountBadge
    )
}
```

entries.summary: Plays illustrative animations shipped as Lottie JSON: mascot moments, celebrations, typing. The same file plays on web and Android.
entries.text:
# Lottie animation (`lottie`)
Group: Display

Plays illustrative animations shipped as Lottie JSON: mascot moments, celebrations, typing. The same file plays on web and Android.

- React: `import { Lottie } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `EqualLottie`
- Tokens: `text/action`
- Source: Motion · Animations

Do: Use Lottie for illustrative motion; keep micro-interactions (press, toggles, sheets) in code on the motion tokens. Export from After Effects with Bodymovin, shapes only (no images or text layers), 60 fps, under ~100 KB. Tint single-colour animations with `text/action` so they follow the theme.

Don't: Don't rebuild an animation by hand in code when a Lottie file exists. Don't autoplay looping animations behind text people are reading.

Anatomy:
1. Box: Fixed-size container the player draws into. (width / height 120 default · flex-shrink 0)
2. Animation: Lottie JSON from assets/lottie/, rendered as SVG. (lottie_light svg renderer (web) · LottieAnimation (Compose) · loop and autoplay default true)
3. Tint: Optional single colour for every fill and stroke. (--eq-lottie-tint (web) · LottieProperty.COLOR / STROKE_COLOR (Compose) · e.g. text/action)

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: With label: role="img"; without: aria-hidden="true". Android: With contentDescription: semantics contentDescription; without: no semantics.
- Name. Web: label prop, e.g. "Equal AI is typing". Omit for decorative motion. Android: contentDescription param.
- Keyboard. Web: Not interactive; no pause control. Android: Not interactive.
- Contrast. Web: Tint with text/action to follow the theme; meaningful animations need 3:1 against their background. Android: Same with EqualTheme.colors.textAction.
- State. Web: No state. Android: No state.
- Motion. Web: Under prefers-reduced-motion it does not autoplay or loop and shows the first frame (read once on mount). Otherwise it loops forever with no pause control. Android: When Remove animations (animator scale 0) is on it shows frame 0 and does not play; otherwise it repeats forever.

Known accessibility gaps:
- loop defaults to true with no pause or stop control, so looping animations over 5 s can't be paused (WCAG 2.2.2) unless reduced motion is on (Lottie.tsx, EqualLottie.kt).

Example: Typing dots
```tsx
// assets/lottie/typing-dots.json
<Lottie name="typing-dots" width={120} height={40} tint="var(--eq-text-action)" label="Equal AI is typing" />
```
```kotlin
// res/raw/lottie_typing_dots.json (copied from assets/lottie/ by `npm run assets`)
EqualLottie(
    rawRes = R.raw.lottie_typing_dots,
    width = 120.dp,
    height = 40.dp,
    tint = EqualTheme.colors.textAction,
    contentDescription = "Equal AI is typing",
)
```

Example: Original colours, play once
```tsx
<Lottie name="typing-dots" width={120} height={40} loop={false} />
```
```kotlin
EqualLottie(rawRes = R.raw.lottie_typing_dots, width = 120.dp, height = 40.dp, iterations = 1)
```

entries.title: Address
entries.summary: Saved address cards with an Edit / Delete overflow, and the add/edit form (label chips, address lines, city, pincode, guiding direction, Save).
entries.text:
# Address (`address`)
Group: Flows

Saved address cards with an Edit / Delete overflow, and the add/edit form (label chips, address lines, city, pincode, guiding direction, Save).

- React: `import { AddressCard, AddressForm, formatAddress } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `AddressCard`, `AddressForm`
- Tokens: `bg/surface`, `text/primary`, `text/secondary`, `text/tertiary`, `text/danger`, `chip/selected-bg`, `button/primary`
- Source: Flows · Addresses

Do: Use formatAddress so every card reads "line1, line2, City- pincode". Open the form in a titled BottomSheet ("Edit Address" / "Add Address"). Route Delete address through the trash confirm sheet.

Don't: Don't show Edit as a separate button; it lives in the ⋮ menu. Don't accept a pincode that isn't six digits; the form blocks Save.

Anatomy:
1. AddressCard: card: Card for one saved address. (bg/surface · radius 16 · padding 14/16 · 1dp stroke/subtle in dark)
2. AddressCard: label: Home, Work or a custom name. (subheading · text/primary)
3. AddressCard: address: Full address built by formatAddress. (captionWrap · text/secondary · 4 above)
4. AddressCard: overflow: ⋮ menu with Edit and Delete address. (OverflowMenu 32 · icon 20 · menu min width 168)
5. AddressForm: label chips: LABEL* overline above Home / Work / Other chips. (overline text/tertiary · SegmentedChips 36 high)
6. AddressForm: fields: Two address lines, then City and Pincode side by side. (TextField radius 12 · bodyLarge · min 48 · Pincode is digits only, 6 max, tabular)
7. AddressForm: guiding direction: Optional free-text field. (TextField with label + '(Optional)')
8. AddressForm: Save: Commit. Disabled until line 1, city and a 6-digit pincode are filled. (Button lg block · 45 high)

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: The card is a div. The chips are radios inside a radiogroup. The fields are textarea/input elements. Save is a button. Android: Chips use selectable(Role.RadioButton) inside selectableGroup(). Fields are BasicTextField. Save is Role.Button.
- Name. Web: The overflow is named '{label} options'. Fields use aria-label: 'Address line 1', 'Address line 2', 'City', 'Pincode'. The chip group has no name, because the LABEL* text is not linked. Android: Overflow contentDescription is '{label} options'. Fields use contentDescription with the same strings.
- Keyboard. Web: Tab through the chips (no arrow keys), the fields and Save. Pincode has inputMode numeric. The overflow menu closes on Escape. Android: TalkBack: swipe through the fields; Pincode opens the number keyboard. Double-tap Save.
- Touch target. Web: Chips are 36 tall with no eq-touch. Fields are at least 48. Save is 45 with no eq-touch. The overflow gets 48 through eq-touch. Android: Chips are 36dp with minimumInteractiveComponentSize (48). Save gets 48. The overflow trigger is 32dp with no minimum.
- Contrast. Web: Address text/secondary 7.5:1. Overlines text/tertiary 5.1:1. Error text/danger 6.2:1. Save is white on green, 2.85:1 in light. The selected chip is 12.6:1. Android: Same tokens.
- State. Web: Chips use aria-checked. Save uses native disabled. The pincode error shows as red text but is not linked: no aria-invalid or aria-describedby. Android: Chips are selected. Save is enabled = false. The pincode error is not exposed with semantics { error() }.
- Motion. Web: Chip colour transitions over duration-base, 0ms under reduced motion. Android: None.

Known accessibility gaps:
- SegmentedChips in Inputs.tsx (AddressForm): the radiogroup has no accessible name, there is no arrow-key navigation, and the 36px chips have no eq-touch.
- TextField in Inputs.tsx: the pincode error is not linked to the input (no aria-invalid / aria-describedby). EqualTextField in Inputs.kt does not set semantics { error() }.
- AddressForm in Flows.tsx: Save is an lg Button, 45px tall with no eq-touch, and native disabled hides it from Tab with no reason given.
- OverflowMenu in Flows.kt (AddressCard): the 32dp trigger has no minimumInteractiveComponentSize.
- Primary buttons put text/on-action white on button/primary #00B140 in light mode: 2.85:1, below AA 4.5:1 for 14sp text (Button.css / Buttons.kt). Dark (black on lime) is 17.4:1.

Example: Saved addresses
```tsx
{addresses.map((a) => (
  <AddressCard key={a.id} label={a.label} address={formatAddress(a)}
    onEdit={() => edit(a)} onDelete={() => confirmDelete(a)} />
))}
```
```kotlin
var addresses by remember { mutableStateOf(SampleAddresses) }
Column(verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(12.dp)) {
    addresses.forEach { a ->
        AddressCard(
            label = a.label,
            address = formatAddress(a),
            onEdit = {},
            onDelete = { addresses = addresses - a },
        )
    }
}
```

Example: Long address
```tsx
<AddressCard label="Work"
  address="Flat 4B, Block C, Skyline Towers, Phase 2, HITECH city, MG Road, Opposite City Center Mall, Banjara Hills, Hyderabad- 500034"
  onEdit={edit} />
```
```kotlin
AddressCard(
    label = "Work",
    address = "Flat 4B, Block C, Skyline Towers, Phase 2, HITECH city, MG Road, Opposite City Center Mall, Banjara Hills, Hyderabad- 500034",
    onEdit = {},
)
```

Example: Edit address form
```tsx
<AddressForm
  initial={{ label: 'Home', line1: 'House no. 4, Tony Street', line2: 'Financial District', city: 'Hyderabad', pincode: '500032' }}
  onSave={(address) => save(address)} />
```
```kotlin
AddressForm(
    // Compose: SavedAddress needs an id (web takes a Partial)
    initial = SavedAddress(
        id = "a1",
        label = "Home",
        line1 = "House no. 4, Tony Street",
        line2 = "Financial District",
        city = "Hyderabad",
        pincode = "500032",
    ),
    onSave = {},
)
```
