entries.title: Call Handling
entries.summary: Pieces of the Call Handling setup and the known-call notification: radio choice cards, contact pickers with an A–Z index, the setup takeover, permission sheets, the done wash, the Android ongoing-call notification and the ongoing-call strip.
entries.text:
# Call Handling (`call-handling`) Group: Flows Pieces of the Call Handling setup and the known-call notification: radio choice cards, contact pickers with an A–Z index, the setup takeover, permission sheets, the done wash, the Android ongoing-call notification and the ongoing-call strip. - React: `import { CallQuestion, ChoiceCard, InfoNote, ContactPick, ContactCheckRow, AlphabetIndex, SetupPrompt, SetupDone, PermissionSheet, CallNotification, OngoingCallBar } from '@equal/ds';` - Compose: `CallQuestion`, `ChoiceCard`, `SuggestedTag`, `InfoNote`, `ContactPick`, `ContactCheckRow`, `AlphabetIndex`, `SetupPrompt`, `SetupDone`, `PermissionSheet`, `CallNotification`, `OngoingCallBar` - Tokens: `choice/selected-bg`, `gradient/choice-stroke`, `info-note/bg`, `initials-disc/bg`, `gradient/setup-done`, `gradient/setup-prompt`, `ongoing-bar/bg`, `ongoing-bar/text` - Source: Known Calls (new users) · Known-call notifications Props of `ChoiceCard`: - `icon`: `IconName`. Leading icon. - `title`: `string`. Option. - `description`: `string`. What it means. - `selected?`: `boolean`. Green outline + tint. - `suggested?`: `boolean`. ⭐ Suggested tag. - `disabled?`: `boolean`. Dimmed (e.g. no permission). - `onSelect?`: `() => void`. Choose. Props of `CallNotification`: - `name`: `string`. Caller. - `state`: `'answering' | 'summary' | 'expanded' | 'connecting'`. Stage of the call. - `category?`: `Category` = 'home-services'. Avatar art. - `elapsed?`: `string` = '00:06'. Timer. - `summary?`: `string`. What the caller wants. - `replies?`: `string[]`. Quick replies (expanded). Props of `PermissionSheet`: - `art`: `AssetName`. 3D art. - `title`: `string`. Ask. - `body`: `ReactNode`. Why. - `cta`: `string`. Action. - `secondary?`: `string`. Underlined text action (e.g. Skip, answer everyone). - `onClose?`: `() => void`. Floating close. Do: Ask for a permission only at the step that needs it, and say why in one line. Keep the notification to who, what they want and one tap to act; Takeover always comes first. Don't: Don't style the notification beyond Android's shell; the system draws it. Don't make the user pick contacts before they've chosen All calls. Anatomy: 1. CallQuestion: Hero art and the setup question. (280 × 208 art or 300 Lottie · title headline Bold (h1) · subtitle title Regular text/secondary) 2. ChoiceCard: Radio card for one call-handling option. (radius 20 · padding 18/18/18/20 · gap 16 · icon 28 · title subheading + description body1 text/secondary · 24 radio · selected: choice/selected-bg + 2dp gradient/choice-stroke · disabled 45%) 3. SuggestedTag + InfoNote: Suggested tag on a card, and the note that asks for a permission. (tag ⭐ + caption text/secondary pill · note radius 16, info-note/bg, padding 16, info 18 + subheading, body1, underlined text/action link with chevron) 4. ContactPick: Suggested contact to add or remove. (76 wide · 56 initials disc initials-disc/bg · 22 +/× badge text/secondary · name body2) 5. ContactCheckRow + AlphabetIndex: Contact row with a checkbox, and the A–Z jump index. (52 disc · name title Medium · phone body1 tabular · 26 checkbox · index letters 11/14 Medium, gap 1) 6. PermissionSheet: Ask-once permission sheet. (sheet/bg · radius 32 top · padding 32/20/24 · 110 art · headline title · title Regular body text/secondary · block lg CTA · 44 close top-right) 7. CallNotification: Android ongoing-call notification while the assistant answers. (radius 24 bg/surface · app line caption + 'Ongoing' text/action + timer pill · 40 avatar · name subheading · summary body1, 1–2 lines · 44 answer ring or 48 app tile · 34 reply chips) 8. SetupPrompt / SetupDone / OngoingCallBar: Setup takeover, done screen and the in-chat call strip. (gradient/setup-prompt takeover + Start · gradient/setup-done wash + Done · bar 44 high, ongoing-bar/bg, lime 'Ongoing call - 02:34' subheading) Accessibility: - Role. Web: ChoiceCard is a button role=radio with aria-checked (the caller adds role=radiogroup); ContactCheckRow uses a role=checkbox; AlphabetIndex is a nav of buttons; PermissionSheet and SetupPrompt are role=dialog; InfoNote is role=note; CallNotification and OngoingCallBar are role=status. Android: ChoiceCard is selectable(Role.RadioButton) (wrap in selectableGroup); the checkbox is toggleable(Role.Checkbox); ContactPick is Role.Button; sheets set paneTitle; CallNotification and OngoingCallBar are polite live regions. - Name. Web: ChoiceCard reads title, Suggested and description; ContactPick 'Add Mom' / 'Remove Vijay Cousin'; checkbox 'Select Arnav Raj'; 'Answer the call'; close 'Close'; notification 'Equal AI is answering Mom'. Android: Same strings via contentDescription; index letters use onClickLabel 'Jump to A'. - Keyboard. Web: Each ChoiceCard is its own Tab stop; arrow keys don't move between radios. PermissionSheet and SetupPrompt don't move or trap focus and ignore Escape. Android: TalkBack reads 'Only unknown numbers, selected, radio button'; double-tap selects. System Back is not handled by the sheets. - Touch target. Web: AlphabetIndex letters are about 14 px tall; notification replies 34 px and the answer button 44 px have no eq-touch; the checkbox is 26 × 40; Button lg is 45 px. Android: AlphabetIndex letters, ReplyChip (34dp), the answer ring (44dp) and UnderlinedLink (36dp) have no minimum size; ChoiceCard, ContactPick, the checkbox and buttons meet 48dp. - Contrast. Web: The selected radio and choice stroke use button/primary green, 2.85:1 on white (under 3:1); the InfoNote link is 2.5:1 on info-note/bg; note text 15:1; ongoing bar lime on #262626 12.6:1; primary buttons are white on green 2.85:1. Dark uses lime with black content. Android: Same tokens and ratios as web. - State. Web: Selected uses aria-checked plus the radio dot and outline; disabled uses the disabled attribute plus 45% opacity; checked uses aria-checked. The notification and ongoing bar are live regions, so each timer tick is announced. Android: selected/enabled on selectable, toggleable state on the checkbox; the live regions also announce every timer change. - Motion. Web: SetupPrompt fades in and PermissionSheet slides up; both stop under prefers-reduced-motion. The CallQuestion Lottie shows its first frame. Android: SetupPrompt and PermissionSheet start visible under rememberReduceMotion; EqualLottie doesn't play. Known accessibility gaps: - AlphabetIndex (CallHandling.tsx and CallHandling.kt) letters are about 14 px/dp tall, far below 48. - CallNotification reply chips (34) and answer button (44) have no touch extension in CallHandling.tsx or CallHandling.kt; UnderlinedLink in CallHandling.kt is 36dp. - ContactCheckRow uses Checkbox (Checkbox.tsx) at 26 × 40 px with no eq-touch, and the row itself isn't clickable. - ChoiceCard in CallHandling.tsx has role=radio but no roving tabindex or arrow-key handling. - PermissionSheet and SetupPrompt in CallHandling.tsx are role=dialog with no focus move, focus trap or Escape. - OngoingCallBar and CallNotification (both platforms) are live regions around a ticking timer, so every second is announced. - Selected radio (button/primary) is 2.85:1 and the InfoNote link (text/action on info-note/bg) 2.5:1 in light theme. Example: Choice cards ```tsx
setMode('all')} /> setMode('unknown')} />
``` ```kotlin var mode by remember { mutableStateOf(CallMode.All) } Column(Modifier.selectableGroup(), verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(16.dp)) { ChoiceCard( icon = EqualIcons.Globe, title = "All calls, except a few", description = "I answer everyone. You pick who I skip.", selected = mode == CallMode.All, onSelect = { mode = CallMode.All }, ) ChoiceCard( icon = EqualIcons.Call, title = "Only unknown numbers", description = "I answer numbers that are not saved in your phone.", selected = mode == CallMode.Unknown, onSelect = { mode = CallMode.Unknown }, ) InfoNote( title = "Contact access needed", body = "Without it, the assistant can’t handle all calls.", link = "Give contacts permission", onLink = { /* ask for READ_CONTACTS */ }, ) } ``` Example: Contact pickers ```tsx ``` ```kotlin var picked by remember { mutableStateOf(true) } Column { Row(horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(8.dp)) { ContactPick(initials = "SU", name = "Mom", onClick = { /* add */ }) ContactPick(initials = "VC", name = "Vijay Cousin", onClick = { /* remove */ }, mark = ContactPickMark.Remove) } Box(Modifier.fillMaxWidth()) { ContactCheckRow(initials = "AR", name = "Arnav Raj", phone = "+91 8986461540", checked = picked, onCheckedChange = { picked = it }) AlphabetIndex(Modifier.align(Alignment.CenterEnd).padding(end = 2.dp), onPick = { /* jump to letter */ }) } } ``` Example: Permission sheet ```tsx ``` ```kotlin // Overlay: fills the screen (scrim + sheet); pass inline = true to draw only the sheet PermissionSheet( art = EqualAssets.PermissionContacts, title = "Allow contacts permission", body = "I need your contact list to know who is calling.", cta = "Allow", onAllow = { /* request READ_CONTACTS */ }, onClose = { /* hide the sheet */ }, ) ``` Example: Call notification ```tsx ``` ```kotlin // Design reference + in-app preview. On device, build the same content into an ongoing // NotificationCompat (CATEGORY_CALL, custom RemoteViews); the system draws the shell. Column(verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(12.dp)) { CallNotification(name = "Mom", state = CallNotificationState.Answering) CallNotification( name = "Mom", state = CallNotificationState.Expanded, category = EqualCategory.HomeServices, summary = SampleCallSummary, replies = listOf("Takeover", "I’ll bring them all", "I’ll call back to get more"), onReply = { /* say it (it == "Takeover": pick up) */ }, onAnswer = { /* pick up */ }, ) CallNotification(name = "Mom", state = CallNotificationState.Connecting) } ``` Example: Ongoing call bar ```tsx ``` ```kotlin OngoingCallBar(elapsed = "02:34") ```

entries.name: gender-selector
entries.title: Gender selector
entries.summary: The two-card Male / Female picker in Personal Details; the choice sets the profile avatar across the app.
entries.text:
# Gender selector (`gender-selector`)
Group: Flows

The two-card Male / Female picker in Personal Details; the choice sets the profile avatar across the app.

- React: `import { GenderSelector } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `GenderSelector`
- Tokens: `bg/surface`, `button/primary`, `gradient/gender-selected`, `text/primary`
- Source: Flows · Profile

Do: Update the profile avatar (hero and bottom nav) as soon as the user picks. Place it under a GENDER overline, below the Name field.

Don't: Don't crop the bust art; if it is missing the card falls back to the ringed avatar. Don't add a third card or a text input here.

Anatomy:
1. Group: Two-column grid of cards. (2 columns · gap 12)
2. Card: One option, Male or Female. (120 high · radius 16 · bg/surface · 2dp transparent border (stroke/dark in dark))
3. Watermark: Faint ♂ or ♀ in the bottom-left corner. (96 · text/primary at 5% · clipped)
4. Label: 'Male' or 'Female'. (subheading · text/primary · 12 from the top)
5. Art: Bust for free users; gold-ringed avatar for paid users. (bust 60×56 · paid avatar 52 · bottom centre)
6. Selected state: Green outline and tinted fill on the chosen card. (gradient/gender-selected · 2dp button/primary border)

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: role="radiogroup" with aria-label 'Gender'. Each card is a button with role="radio". The watermark is aria-hidden. Android: The Row has selectableGroup(). Each card is selectable(role = Role.RadioButton).
- Name. Web: Each radio is named by its text, 'Male' or 'Female'. With tier paid, or when the bust is missing, ProfileAvatar adds alt 'Your profile', so the name becomes 'Male Your profile'. Android: The card merges its text. ProfileAvatar passes contentDescription null, but the ♂/♀ watermark text is not hidden and is read too.
- Keyboard. Web: Each radio is its own Tab stop, with Enter/Space to select. Arrow keys do nothing, unlike a native radio group. Android: TalkBack: swipe between the two cards, double-tap to select. TalkBack reads 'selected / not selected'.
- Touch target. Web: Cards are 120 tall and half the width. Android: Cards are 120dp tall and weighted to half the width.
- Contrast. Web: Label 18.9:1. The selected 2dp border is button/primary #00B140 on white: 2.85:1, under the 3:1 needed for a state indicator. In dark it is lime (#BAFF29), which passes. Android: Same tokens.
- State. Web: aria-checked. Visually, only the border and tint change; there is no check mark. Android: selected = true on the card. Visually, only the border and tint change.
- Motion. Web: Press scale (eq-pressable), 0ms under reduced motion. Android: None.

Known accessibility gaps:
- GenderSelector in Flows.tsx: with tier paid, or when the bust asset is missing, ProfileAvatar's default alt 'Your profile' joins each radio's name ('Male Your profile'). Pass label="".
- GenderSelector in Flows.tsx: each radio is a separate Tab stop with no arrow-key roving, which a radiogroup is expected to have.
- GenderCard in Flows.kt: the ♂/♀ watermark BasicText is not cleared from semantics, so TalkBack reads it as part of the option.
- GenderSelector (Flows.css / Flows.kt): selection is shown only by a #00B140 border (2.85:1 on white in light) and a tint, with no check mark.

Example: Free vs paid
```tsx
<GenderSelector value={gender} onChange={setGender} tier="free" />
<GenderSelector value={gender} onChange={setGender} tier="paid" />
```
```kotlin
var gender by remember { mutableStateOf(Gender.Male) }
Column(verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(16.dp)) {
    GenderSelector(value = gender, onValueChange = { gender = it }, tier = PlanTier.Free)
    GenderSelector(value = gender, onValueChange = { gender = it }, tier = PlanTier.Paid)
}
```

Example: Interactive
```tsx
const [gender, setGender] = useState<Gender>('male');

<GenderSelector value={gender} onChange={setGender} />
<ProfileAvatar variant={gender} size={56} />
```
```kotlin
var gender by remember { mutableStateOf(Gender.Male) }
GenderSelector(value = gender, onValueChange = { gender = it })
ProfileAvatar(
    variant = if (gender == Gender.Male) ProfileAvatarVariant.Male else ProfileAvatarVariant.Female,
    width = 56.dp,
)
```

Example: In Personal Details
```tsx
<AppBar title="Personal Details" onBack={goBack} />
<TextField label="Name" value={name} onChange={setName}
  helper="Your AI will call you 'Keshav'" />
<SectionHeader inset={0}>Gender</SectionHeader>
<GenderSelector value={gender} onChange={setGender} />
```
```kotlin
var name by remember { mutableStateOf("Keshav") }
var gender by remember { mutableStateOf(Gender.Female) }
EqualAppBar(title = "Personal Details", onBackClick = {})
EqualTextField(
    value = name,
    onValueChange = { name = it },
    label = "Name",
    helper = AnnotatedString("Your AI will call you '$name'"),
)
SectionHeader(title = "Gender", inset = 0.dp)
GenderSelector(value = gender, onValueChange = { gender = it })
```

entries.name: instruction-cards
entries.title: Instruction cards
entries.summary: The pieces of the Instructions flow: recommended and preset cards on the hub, preset and active instruction cards with When / Do rows, and the preview shown in the setup chat.
entries.text:
# Instruction cards (`instruction-cards`)
Group: Flows

The pieces of the Instructions flow: recommended and preset cards on the hub, preset and active instruction cards with When / Do rows, and the preview shown in the setup chat.

- React: `import { RecommendedCard, SuggestionsComingCard, PresetCard, PresetInstructionCard, InstructionCard, WhenDoRow, InstructionPreview } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `RecommendedCard`, `SuggestionsComingCard`, `PresetCard`, `PresetInstructionCard`, `InstructionCard`, `WhenDoRow`, `InstructionPreview`
- Tokens: `bg/surface`, `chip/when-bg`, `chip/do-bg`, `preset/tint-red`, `preset/tint-green`, `preset/tint-orange`, `gradient/suggestion-card`, `text/primary`, `text/secondary`, `text/tertiary`, `text/action`, `button/primary`
- Source: Flows · Instructions · Instruction Card

Do: Write When as the situation and Do as the assistant's behaviour, in plain first person ("say I am not interested"). Use sentence-case When / Do on presets and uppercase WHEN / DO on active instructions (`upper`). Confirm with 👍 Confirm (unread) next to ✍️ Edit (read) under the preview. Show SuggestionsComingCard once every recommendation is applied.

Don't: Don't delete an instruction straight from the ⋮ menu; confirm first. Don't use Material icons on preset or recommended cards; they lead with emoji. Don't put two filled buttons on a preset instruction; Apply is the only commit.

Anatomy:
1. RecommendedCard: Horizontal card with an emoji, + add, title and description. (188 wide · min 114 · radius 16 · 1dp stroke/subtle · emoji 26 · add 30 circle icon-button/bg, add 20 text/action)
2. SuggestionsComingCard: Shown once every recommendation is added. (gradient/suggestion-card · radius 16 · orb 18 + caption · bodyLarge · illustration 112)
3. PresetCard: Tappable preset with an emoji in a tinted circle and a chevron. (flow card · emoji 16 in 26 circle (preset/tint-*) · chevron 22 text/placeholder · subheading + captionWrap)
4. PresetInstructionCard: Preset instruction with Apply, which becomes an 'Applied' pill. (title subheading (h3) · Button sm 24 · Applied pill 24 action-card/highlight + check 16 text/action)
5. WhenDoRow: When / Do line: a flat chip on presets, a fading pill on active instructions. (preset chip 26 high, min 42, chip/when-bg / chip/do-bg · active pill 51×24 gradient/when-chip / do-chip · text 13/18)
6. InstructionCard: Active instruction: bold title + ⋮, source pill, divider, WHEN and DO. (radius 16 · 1dp stroke/subtle · padding 17 · title 17/20 Bold · source pill 24 high)
7. InstructionPreview: Preview in the setup chat, with an optional ✅ reaction. (white frame radius 16 · padding 8 · max 280 · reaction 32 circle, shadow/raised)

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: RecommendedCard is a div with an add <button>. PresetCard is a <button>. Instruction titles are h3. The overflow is a button with aria-expanded. Emoji are aria-hidden. Android: Add, PresetCard and Apply are Role.Button. The overflow is a clickable Box. Titles have no heading(). EmojiGlyph text is not hidden.
- Name. Web: Add is 'Add {title}'. PresetCard is named by its title and description. The overflow is 'Instruction options' on every card. The ✅ reaction has aria-label 'Confirmed' on a span with no role. Android: Add has onClickLabel and contentDescription 'Add {title}'. Overflow: 'Instruction options'. Emoji are read by their Unicode names.
- Keyboard. Web: Tab to add, the preset cards, Apply and ⋮, then Enter/Space. When Apply becomes the 'Applied' span, focus is lost. Android: TalkBack: swipe through the cards, double-tap to act. Back closes the overflow popup.
- Touch target. Web: Add (30) uses eq-touch for 48. The sm Apply button uses eq-touch. The overflow gets 48 through IconButton. Android: Add is a 30dp Box and the overflow a 32dp Box, both with no minimum size. Apply (sm) gets 48 from EqualButton.
- Contrast. Web: Titles 18.9:1, descriptions text/secondary 7.5:1. Below 3:1 in light: the add icon on icon-button/bg (2.55:1), the Applied text on its highlight (2.64:1), and the chevron in text/placeholder (2.32:1). The preset When/Do chip label is 4.43:1 in dark. Android: Same tokens. In dark, add and Applied are lime on dark tints, above 10:1.
- State. Web: Applied is shown by the check icon and the 'Applied' text. The change is not announced. Android: Same visuals. The change is not announced.
- Motion. Web: Press scale only, 0ms under reduced motion. Android: None.

Known accessibility gaps:
- RecommendedCard add (30dp) and OverflowMenu (32dp) in Flows.kt have no minimumInteractiveComponentSize.
- PresetInstructionCard in Flows.tsx: Apply is replaced by a non-focusable 'Applied' span, so keyboard focus is lost and the change is not announced (no live region on web or Android).
- InstructionPreview in Flows.tsx: the reaction's aria-label 'Confirmed' is on a span with no role, so it is not announced. In Flows.kt the ✅ EmojiGlyph is read as a raw emoji name.
- EmojiGlyph in Foundation.kt (used in RecommendedCard, PresetCard and the source pill) is not hidden from TalkBack, so emoji names are read aloud.
- InstructionCard (Flows.tsx / Flows.kt): every overflow button is labelled 'Instruction options', without the instruction title, so they can't be told apart in a list.
- Contrast below 3:1 in light: the add icon text/action on icon-button/bg (2.55:1), the Applied pill text/action on action-card/highlight (2.64:1), and the PresetCard chevron text/placeholder (2.32:1). The preset When/Do chip label is text/tertiary on chip/when-bg at 4.43:1 in dark.

Example: Recommended for you
```tsx
<RecommendedCard emoji="🚫" title="Decline sales & spam"
  description="Politely declines sales and insurance calls." onAdd={add} />
<RecommendedCard emoji="💬" title="Take a message"
  description="Takes their name, number and message." onAdd={add} />

{allApplied && <SuggestionsComingCard />}
```
```kotlin
var added by remember { mutableStateOf(setOf<String>()) }
if (added.size < 2) {
    Row(horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(12.dp)) {
        if ("decline" !in added) {
            RecommendedCard(
                emoji = "🚫",
                title = "Decline sales & spam",
                description = "Politely declines sales and insurance calls.",
                onAdd = { added = added + "decline" },
            )
        }
        if ("message" !in added) {
            RecommendedCard(
                emoji = "💬",
                title = "Take a message",
                description = "Takes their name, number and message.",
                onAdd = { added = added + "message" },
            )
        }
    }
} else {
    SuggestionsComingCard()
}
```

Example: Browse presets

  description="Decline spam, hold the line on loan and payments call, close wrong call" onClick={open} />

```

Example: Preset instructions

  applied={applied} onApply={apply} />
```

Example: Active instructions

  id: 'decline-sales',

entries.name: checkbox
entries.title: Checkbox
entries.summary: A coded checkbox with an optional label, used for multi-select such as "Select All" in chat-list selection mode.
entries.text:
# Checkbox (`checkbox`)
Group: Inputs

A coded checkbox with an optional label, used for multi-select such as "Select All" in chat-list selection mode.

- React: `import { Checkbox } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `EqualCheckbox`
- Tokens: `button/primary`, `text/secondary`, `text/primary`
- Source: §5 Chat Header · Selection mode

Do: Use for multi-select lists; the whole label is the tap target. Use bodyLarge labels in headers ("Select All") and body1 in dense lists.

Don't: Don't use a checkbox for an instant on/off setting; that is a Switch. Don't replace the coded box with an image; checkboxes are coded, never images.

Anatomy:
1. Box: The Material checkbox glyph that shows checked or blank. (Web 22 default · Compose 18 · checked button/primary · unchecked web text/secondary, Compose text/tertiary)
2. Label: Optional text beside the box; part of the same tap target. (gap 12 · bodyLarge 16/400 or body1 14/400 · text/primary)

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: <button role='checkbox'> with aria-checked; the icon is aria-hidden. Android: toggleable(role = Role.Checkbox) when onCheckedChange is set; with null the row (e.g. SelectionChatHeader Select All) owns it.
- Name. Web: The visible label inside the button; with no label pass ariaLabel (e.g. 'Select Arnav Raj'). Android: contentDescription parameter when nothing beside it names it; otherwise the parent row's merged text.
- Keyboard. Web: Tab to focus, Space or Enter toggles. Android: TalkBack: swipe to focus, double-tap to toggle; announces 'checked' or 'not checked'.
- Touch target. Web: minHeight 40 and no .eq-touch: a labelled checkbox is 40px high, an icon-only one is 22 × 40. Android: minimumInteractiveComponentSize() gives 48dp around the 18dp glyph.
- Contrast. Web: Unchecked text/secondary on white is 7.5:1; checked button/primary #00B140 is 2.85:1 in light (below 3:1), lime in dark passes. Android: Unchecked text/tertiary #6E6E6E is 5.1:1 on white; checked uses the same #00B140.
- State. Web: aria-checked; the glyph changes from an empty box to a filled box with a tick, so state is not colour alone. There is no disabled prop. Android: toggleableState from toggleable; the glyph changes shape. No enabled parameter.

Known accessibility gaps:
- Checkbox.tsx: no eq-touch and only minHeight 40, so the hit area is 40px high (22 × 40 with no label).
- Checkbox.tsx / EqualSwitch.kt (EqualCheckbox): no disabled / enabled support on either platform.
- Checkbox.tsx / EqualSwitch.kt: checked glyph button/primary #00B140 on white is 2.85:1 in light mode, below 3:1.

Example: Interactive
```tsx
const [all, setAll] = useState(false);

<Checkbox checked={all} onChange={setAll} label="Select All" />
<Checkbox checked={a} onChange={setA} label="Loan Offers" labelVariant="body1" />
```
```kotlin
var all by remember { mutableStateOf(false) }
var loanOffers by remember { mutableStateOf(false) }

// Compose: no label / labelVariant params; put an EqualText beside the box.
Row(horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(8.dp), verticalAlignment = Alignment.CenterVertically) {
    EqualCheckbox(checked = all, onCheckedChange = { all = it })
    EqualText(text = "Select All", style = EqualTheme.type.bodyLarge, color = EqualTheme.colors.textPrimary)
}
Row(horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(8.dp), verticalAlignment = Alignment.CenterVertically) {
    EqualCheckbox(checked = loanOffers, onCheckedChange = { loanOffers = it })
    EqualText(text = "Loan Offers", style = EqualTheme.type.body1, color = EqualTheme.colors.textPrimary)
}
```

Example: Sizes and bare
```tsx
<Checkbox checked size={18} />
<Checkbox checked={false} size={18} />
<Checkbox checked />
<Checkbox checked={false} />
```
```kotlin
Row(horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(20.dp)) {
    EqualCheckbox(checked = true, onCheckedChange = {}, size = 18.dp)
    EqualCheckbox(checked = false, onCheckedChange = {}, size = 18.dp)
    // Compose: default size is 18.dp (web defaults to 22), so pass 22.dp explicitly.
    EqualCheckbox(checked = true, onCheckedChange = {}, size = 22.dp)
    EqualCheckbox(checked = false, onCheckedChange = {}, size = 22.dp)
}
```

Example: In the selection header
```tsx
<SelectionHeader count={selected.length} allSelected={all}
  onSelectAll={(v) => setSelected(v ? ids : [])} />
```
```kotlin
val ids = listOf("arnav", "amit", "priya")
var selected by remember { mutableStateOf(setOf<String>()) }

SelectionChatHeader(
    selectedCount = selected.size,
    allSelected = selected.size == ids.size,
    onSelectAllChange = { all -> selected = if (all) ids.toSet() else emptySet() },
    onBackClick = {},
    onMarkReadClick = {},
    onDeleteClick = {},
)
```

entries.name: composer
entries.title: Composer
entries.summary: The message input bar with a send button that stays disabled until there is text, used at the bottom of a chat and in the AI panel.
entries.text:
# Composer (`composer`)
Group: Inputs

The message input bar with a send button that stays disabled until there is text, used at the bottom of a chat and in the AI panel.

- React: `import { Composer } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `VoiceInputBar`
- Tokens: `bg/surface`, `stroke/subtle`, `action/stroke/unread`, `shadow/focusRing`, `gradient/send-disabled`, `gradient/fab`, `shadow/fab`, `text/tertiary`, `text/primary`
- Source: §15 Voice Input Bar (Composer)

Do: Pin the composer to the bottom of the chat or AI panel. Leave send disabled on empty input; the component does this for you.

Don't: Don't add attachment or emoji buttons inside the bar; the spec is input + send only. Don't change the send glyph; it is the coded send icon rotated −35°.

Anatomy:
1. Input: Pill text field where the user types a message. (45 high · radius full · padding h20 · bg/surface · 1px stroke/subtle · focus action/stroke/unread + shadow/focusRing · body1 14/400)
2. Placeholder: Hint shown while empty. (web 'Type a message...' · Compose 'Type a message' · text/tertiary)
3. Send button: Circle that sends the message; enabled only when there is text. (45 circle · gap 10 · disabled gradient/send-disabled · active gradient/fab + shadow/fab)
4. Send icon: Paper-plane glyph rotated −35°. (send 20 · active text/on-action · disabled text/on-dark)

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: <form> with a native <input> and a <button type='submit'>. Android: BasicTextField plus a Box with clickable(role = Role.Button).
- Name. Web: Input aria-label 'Message'; send button aria-label 'Send'. Android: Input has no contentDescription (placeholder only); send uses sendContentDescription ('Send') as both onClickLabel and icon description.
- Keyboard. Web: Enter submits the form; Tab moves to Send, which is skipped while disabled. Android: IME action Send calls onSend when there is text; TalkBack double-tap on the send button.
- Touch target. Web: Send is 45px with no .eq-touch. Android: Send is a 45dp Box without minimumInteractiveComponentSize.
- Contrast. Web: Text 17:1, placeholder text/tertiary 5.1:1. Active send icon is white on #86E63B→#00B140 (1.6–2.85:1) in light; dark is black on lime (about 17:1). Android: Same tokens as web.
- State. Web: Send uses the native disabled attribute until there is text; the fill also changes. Android: clickable(enabled = canSend) exposes disabled; enabled = false on the bar disables both.
- Motion. Web: Border, ring and send shadow fade over 200ms; press scale on send; zeroed under prefers-reduced-motion. Android: Press scale on send via eqPressFeedback, following the system animator scale.

Known accessibility gaps:
- Composer.tsx: the 45px send button has no eq-touch, so its hit area is below 48px.
- Composer.kt: SendButton is 45dp without minimumInteractiveComponentSize().
- Composer.kt: VoiceInputBar's BasicTextField has no contentDescription; the name relies on the placeholder (web uses aria-label 'Message').
- Composer.css / Composer.kt: active send icon is white on gradient/fab (#86E63B → #00B140), 1.6–2.85:1 in light mode, below 3:1.

Example: Interactive
```tsx
<Composer onSend={(text) => setSent((s) => [...s, text])} />
```
```kotlin
val sent = remember { mutableStateListOf<String>() }
var text by remember { mutableStateOf("") }

// Compose: always controlled; clear the value yourself after send.
VoiceInputBar(
    value = text,
    onValueChange = { text = it },
    onSend = {
        sent += text.trim()
        text = ""
    },
)
```

Example: States
```tsx
<Composer />
<Composer forceFocus />
<Composer value="Sure, I'll be there!" onChange={setText} />
```
```kotlin
var text by remember { mutableStateOf("Sure, I'll be there!") }

Column(verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(16.dp)) {
    VoiceInputBar(value = "", onValueChange = {}, onSend = {})
    // Compose: no forceFocus; the focused look appears when the field has focus.
    VoiceInputBar(value = text, onValueChange = { text = it }, onSend = {})
}
```

entries.name: search
entries.title: Search
entries.summary: The search screen’s pieces: the outlined search bar with back inside, section labels with Clear all, recent searches as avatar tiles, message hits with the match in bold, loading dots and the three illustration states.
entries.text:
# Search (`search`)
Group: Inputs

The search screen’s pieces: the outlined search bar with back inside, section labels with Clear all, recent searches as avatar tiles, message hits with the match in bold, loading dots and the three illustration states.

- React: `import { SearchBar, SearchSection, RecentSearches, MessageResult, LoadingDots, SearchState } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `SearchBar`, `SearchSection`, `RecentSearches`, `MessageResult`, `LoadingDots`, `SearchState`
- Tokens: `button/primary`, `bg/surface`, `text/tertiary`, `text/primary`
- Source: Search

Props of `SearchBar`:
- `value`: `string`. Query.
- `onChange?`: `(v: string) => void`. Typing.
- `onBack?`: `() => void`. Back arrow inside the bar.
- `placeholder?`: `string` = 'Search for names'. Hint.

Props of `MessageResult`:
- `name`: `string`. Who.
- `time`: `string`. When.
- `text`: `string`. The message line.
- `query`: `string`. Bolded wherever it appears.

Props of `SearchState`:
- `art`: `AssetName`. Illustration.
- `title`: `string`. Headline.
- `body`: `string`. One line of help.
- `size?`: `number` = 160. Art size.

Do: Show chats first and messages after; chats come back fastest. Bold the match in message hits so people see why each one showed up.

Don't: Don't show a spinner for the whole screen; load each section in place with the dots. Don't reuse the no-results art for errors; offline has its own.

Anatomy:
1. SearchBar: Pill search field with back inside and clear once there is a query. (52 high · margin 8/16 · radius full · bg/surface · 1.5dp button/primary outline · back 40 (48 touch) · bodyLarge input, placeholder text/tertiary, caret text/action · clear × 18 text/tertiary)
2. SearchSection: Section label with optional Clear all. (overline uppercase text/tertiary · padding 14/16/8 · Clear all caption pill bg/surface, padding 4/12)
3. RecentSearches: Recent searches as avatar tiles. (72 wide tiles · gap 14 · 52 avatar · caption name truncated)
4. MessageResult: A message hit with the match in bold. (padding 10/16 · name subheading + time micro text/tertiary · line body1, match Bold text/primary · 1dp stroke/subtle between hits)
5. LoadingDots: Three dots that pulse while a section loads. (9 dots · gap 8 · button/primary · pulse 1s, staggered 0.15s · padding 24)
6. SearchState: Illustration state: start, no internet, no results. (art 160 (100–120 in use) · title title Medium (h2 on web) · body body1 text/secondary, max 280)

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: Input is a plain text input (not type=search); back, clear, Clear all, tiles and hits are buttons; LoadingDots is role=status; SearchState title is h2; section labels are plain text. Android: BasicTextField with contentDescription; back and clear are Role.Button; LoadingDots is a polite live region; section labels and SearchState titles are plain text, not heading().
- Name. Web: Input named by its placeholder ('Search for names'); 'Back'; 'Clear search'; 'Clear all'; tiles by avatar alt plus label (e.g. 'Career Amit Nanda'); hits by name, time and line. Android: Same strings; recent tiles have onClickLabel 'Search Amit Nanda'.
- Keyboard. Web: Tab: back, input, clear; Enter/Space on buttons. The input has autoFocus when asked. Android: TalkBack: swipe to the field and double-tap to edit; double-tap tiles and hits.
- Touch target. Web: Back and clear use eq-touch (48); Clear all eq-touch; tiles 72 wide; hits full width. Android: Back, clear and Clear all use minimumInteractiveComponentSize; tiles and hits are large rows.
- Contrast. Web: Placeholder and section labels text/tertiary 5.1:1 on white; highlight Bold text/primary. The green bar outline and loading dots (button/primary) are 2.85:1 in light; lime in dark. Android: Same tokens and ratios as web.
- State. Web: The match is shown by weight (Bold), not colour. Loading is announced via role=status 'Loading'. Result counts are not announced. Android: Loading announced by the live region; matches bolded.
- Motion. Web: LoadingDots pulse; stopped under prefers-reduced-motion (dots stay solid). Android: LoadingDots stop under rememberReduceMotion.

Known accessibility gaps:
- SearchSection labels and SearchState titles in Search.kt are not marked heading(), and web SearchSection is plain text, so results can't be skimmed by heading.
- SearchBar outline and LoadingDots use button/primary at 2.85:1 in light theme, under 3:1 for UI parts.
- RecentSearches tiles in Search.tsx include the CategoryAvatar alt in the button name ('Career Amit Nanda'); the avatar should be decorative there.

Example: Search bar
```tsx
<SearchBar value={q} onChange={setQ} onBack={goBack} autoFocus />
```
```kotlin
var q by remember { mutableStateOf("") }
SearchBar(value = q, onValueChange = { q = it }, onBack = {}, autoFocus = true)
```

Example: Recent searches
```tsx
<SearchSection title="Recent searches" onClear={clearRecent} />
<RecentSearches items={recent} onPick={setQ} />
```
```kotlin
var q by remember { mutableStateOf("") }
var recent by remember {
    mutableStateOf(
        listOf(
            RecentSearch("Amit Nanda", EqualCategory.Career),
            RecentSearch("Shankar", EqualCategory.Ride),
            RecentSearch("DSR Builder", EqualCategory.Financial),
        ),
    )
}
Column {
    SearchBar(value = q, onValueChange = { q = it })
    SearchSection(title = "Recent searches", onClear = { recent = emptyList() })
    RecentSearches(items = recent, onPick = { q = it })
}
```

Example: Message results
```tsx
<MessageResult name="Santosh Anna" time="3:02 PM" text={line} query={q} onClick={openMessage} />
```
```kotlin
val q = "Sa"
Column {
    SearchSection(title = "Messages")
    MessageResult(name = "Santosh Anna", time = "3:02 PM", text = "Caller said that they’ll call you in the evening", query = q, onClick = {})
    EqualDivider()
    MessageResult(name = "Amit Nanda", time = "3:02 PM", text = "Same address, near Gachibowli", query = q, onClick = {})
}
```

Example: States
```tsx
<SearchState art="illustration-search" title="Search across your calls" body="…" />
<SearchState art="illustration-no-internet" title="No internet connection" body="…" />
<SearchState art="illustration-no-results" title="No results found" body="…" />
<LoadingDots />
```
```kotlin
Column {
    // Compose: SearchState takes an EqualAssets illustration and a size in dp
    SearchStateView(art = EqualAssets.IllustrationSearch, size = 170.dp, title = "Search across your calls", body = "Look for names, phone numbers, categories, keywords")
    SearchStateView(art = EqualAssets.IllustrationNoInternet, size = 130.dp, title = "No internet connection", body = "We could not connect to a stable internet. Check your connection and try again.")
    SearchStateView(art = EqualAssets.IllustrationNoResults, size = 150.dp, title = "No results found", body = "Couldn’t find anything matching. Try a different name, number, category or keyword")
    LoadingDots()
}
```

entries.name: search-field
entries.title: Search field
entries.summary: A pill search input with a leading search icon and a clear button, used to filter chats.
entries.text:
# Search field (`search-field`)
Group: Inputs

A pill search input with a leading search icon and a clear button, used to filter chats.

- React: `import { SearchField } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `SearchField`
- Tokens: `bg/surface`, `text/tertiary`, `text/primary`, `text/placeholder`
- Source: Surfaces from the Typography screen inventory · Search Field

Do: Say what is being searched in the placeholder ("Search chats"). Show an EmptyState with the query in it when nothing matches.

Don't: Don't add a separate search button; results filter as you type. Don't use it as a general form field; use TextField.

Anatomy:
1. Container: Full-width pill that holds the search input. (48 high · radius full · bg/surface · web 1px stroke/subtle border, focus action/stroke/unread + shadow/focusRing · padding 16 start / 14 end)
2. Search icon: Leading magnifier that marks the field as search. (search 20 · text/tertiary · gap web 10, Compose 8 · decorative)
3. Input / placeholder: The query text, or 'Search for names' while empty. (bodyLarge 16/400 · text/primary · placeholder web text/tertiary, Compose text/placeholder)
4. Clear button: Web only: appears once there is text and empties the field. (close 18 · text/tertiary · .eq-touch 48 hit area · aria-label 'Clear')

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: Native <input> inside a <label>; with onActivate it becomes a readOnly input that hands off to the search screen. Android: BasicTextField when editable; with onActivate a Row with clickable(role = Role.Button).
- Name. Web: aria-label is the placeholder ('Search for names'); the clear button is 'Clear'. Android: No contentDescription; the name relies on the placeholder drawn in the decoration box. The onActivate row uses onClickLabel = placeholder plus the visible text.
- Keyboard. Web: Tab to the input, type; Tab again reaches Clear. With onActivate, focusing the input blurs it at once and calls onActivate. Android: TalkBack: double-tap to edit; the onActivate variant is a button, double-tap opens search.
- Touch target. Web: Container 48px high; Clear gets 48px via .eq-touch. Android: 48dp high, full width.
- Contrast. Web: Text 17:1; placeholder and icon text/tertiary on white 5.1:1 (dark #999999 on #222222 5.6:1). The 1px stroke/subtle border is 1.2:1. Android: Placeholder uses text/placeholder #AAAAAA (2.3:1 on white), lower than web.
- State. Web: Clear appears only when there is a value; focus shows a green border and ring. Android: No clear control or focus styling.
- Motion. Web: Border and ring fade over 200ms; zeroed under prefers-reduced-motion. Android: None.

Known accessibility gaps:
- Inputs.tsx: with onActivate the field is a readOnly input that blurs itself on focus, so keyboard and screen-reader users lose focus; it should be a <button> styled as the field.
- Inputs.kt: the editable SearchField has no contentDescription and no clear button; the name relies on placeholder text in the decoration box.
- Inputs.kt: SearchField placeholder uses text/placeholder #AAAAAA (2.3:1 on white) where web uses text/tertiary (5.1:1).

Example: Empty
```tsx
const [q, setQ] = useState('');

<SearchField value={q} onChange={setQ} />
```
```kotlin
var q by remember { mutableStateOf("") }

// Compose: the default placeholder is "Search", so pass "Search chats".
SearchField(value = q, onValueChange = { q = it }, placeholder = "Search chats")
```

Example: With a query
```tsx
<SearchField value="Amit" onChange={setQ} />
```
```kotlin
var q by remember { mutableStateOf("Amit") }

// Compose: no built-in clear (X) button; clear by setting the value to "".
SearchField(value = q, onValueChange = { q = it }, placeholder = "Search chats")
```

Example: Filtering the chat list
```tsx
<SearchField value={q} onChange={setQ} />
{results.length === 0
  ? <EmptyState title="No chats found" body={`Nothing matches "\${q}". Try a name or number.`} />
  : results.map((c) => <ChatListItem key={c.id} {...c} />)}
```
```kotlin
val chats = listOf("Arnav Raj", "Amit Kumar", "Priya Nair")
var q by remember { mutableStateOf("") }
val results = chats.filter { it.contains(q, ignoreCase = true) }

SearchField(value = q, onValueChange = { q = it }, placeholder = "Search chats")
if (results.isEmpty()) {
    EmptyState(title = "No chats found", body = "Nothing matches \"$q\". Try a name or number.")
} else {
    results.forEach { name ->
        ChatListItem(name = name, preview = "You have a visitor", date = "Yesterday")
    }
}
```

entries.text:
# Segmented chips (`segmented-chips`)
Group: Inputs

A single-select row of pill chips for a short, fixed set of options, like the Home / Work / Other address label.

- React: `import { SegmentedChips } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `SegmentedChips`
- Tokens: `chip/selected-bg`, `chip/selected-text`, `stroke/medium`, `text/secondary`
- Source: Surfaces from the Typography screen inventory · Segmented Label Chips

Do: Use for two to four short options where exactly one is always selected. Declare options `as const` so value and onChange are typed to the union.

Don't: Don't use it for multi-select; use checkboxes. Don't use it for long labels that would wrap; the chips wrap as a row, not the text.

Anatomy:
1. Group: Row of mutually exclusive chips (Home / Work / Other). (gap 8 · wraps on web)
2. Chip: One option pill. (36 high · padding h16 · radius full · 1px stroke/medium · bg/surface)
3. Label: The option name. (button 14/500 · text/secondary)
4. Selected chip: The chosen option, filled dark. (fill + border chip/selected-bg (#333333 light, #F7F7F7 dark) · label chip/selected-text)

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: role='radiogroup' on the row and <button role='radio'> per chip. Android: selectableGroup() on the Row and selectable(role = Role.RadioButton) per chip.
- Name. Web: Each chip is named by its label; the group has no accessible name. Android: Each chip by its text; the group has no label.
- Keyboard. Web: Every chip is its own Tab stop and Enter/Space selects; arrow keys do nothing. Android: TalkBack: swipe between options, double-tap to select; announces 'selected' and position in the group.
- Touch target. Web: 36px high with no .eq-touch, so the hit area is under 48px. Android: minimumInteractiveComponentSize() gives 48dp around the 36dp chip.
- Contrast. Web: Unselected text/secondary on white 7.5:1; selected white on #333333 12.6:1 (dark #111111 on #F7F7F7). The stroke/medium border is 1.3:1. Android: Same tokens as web.
- State. Web: aria-checked on the selected radio; selection is a full fill swap, not just a hue change. Android: selected = true is exposed by selectable.
- Motion. Web: Fill, colour and border fade over 200ms, plus press scale; zeroed under prefers-reduced-motion. Android: No animation.

Known accessibility gaps:
- Inputs.tsx: SegmentedChips radios have no arrow-key handling or roving tabindex; each chip is a separate Tab stop.
- Inputs.tsx / Inputs.kt: the radiogroup / selectableGroup has no accessible name and no prop to set one.
- Inputs.css: .eq-seg is 36px high with no eq-touch, so the web hit area is under 48px.

Example: Address label
```tsx
const LABELS = ['Home', 'Work', 'Other'] as const;
const [label, setLabel] = useState<(typeof LABELS)[number]>('Home');

<SegmentedChips options={LABELS} value={label} onChange={setLabel} />
```
```kotlin
val labels = listOf("Home", "Work", "Other")
var selected by remember { mutableStateOf(0) }

SegmentedChips(options = labels, selectedIndex = selected, onSelectedIndexChange = { selected = it })
```

Example: Any string union
```tsx
const SPEEDS = ['Slow', 'Normal', 'Fast'] as const;

<SegmentedChips options={SPEEDS} value={v} onChange={setV} />
```
```kotlin
val speeds = listOf("Slow", "Normal", "Fast")
var selected by remember { mutableStateOf(1) }

// Compose: options are a List<String> addressed by index, not a typed union.
SegmentedChips(options = speeds, selectedIndex = selected, onSelectedIndexChange = { selected = it })
```

entries.name: switch
entries.title: Switch
entries.summary: A controlled on/off toggle (40 × 24 track) for settings that take effect immediately, such as the assistant or promotional-call muting.
entries.text:
# Switch (`switch`)
Group: Inputs

A controlled on/off toggle (40 × 24 track) for settings that take effect immediately, such as the assistant or promotional-call muting.

- React: `import { Switch } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `EqualSwitch`
- Tokens: `button/primary`, `button/disabled`, `brand/white`, `shadow/raised`
- Source: §3 Assistant Availability Toggle · Switch

Do: Use a Switch when the change applies instantly (Mute Promotional Calls, Get updates on WhatsApp). Put the visible label in the row beside it and pass the same text as `label`. Confirm with a sheet when turning something off has consequences, as WhatsApp Updates does ("Turn off WhatsApp updates?").

Don't: Don't use a Switch for a choice that needs a Save button; use Checkbox or SegmentedChips. Don't recolour the track; on is button/primary and off is button/disabled in both themes.

Anatomy:
1. Track: The pill that shows on or off and takes the tap. (40 × 24 · radius full · on button/primary · off button/disabled)
2. Thumb: The circle that slides to the on side. (18 circle · inset 3 · travel 16 · shadow/raised · on text/on-action (white in light, black on lime in dark) · off brand/white)

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: <button role='switch'> with aria-checked. Android: toggleable(role = Role.Switch) when onCheckedChange is set; with null the parent row (AssistantToggleCard, ToggleRow) owns the semantics.
- Name. Web: Required `label` prop set as aria-label; it should match the visible row label (e.g. 'AI Assistant'). Android: No contentDescription parameter: the name comes from the parent row's merged text. Use onCheckedChange = null inside a labelled row.
- Keyboard. Web: Tab to focus, Space or Enter toggles; disabled removes it from the tab order. Android: TalkBack: swipe to focus, double-tap to toggle; it announces 'on' or 'off'.
- Touch target. Web: .eq-touch gives a 48px hit area around the 40 × 24 track. Android: minimumInteractiveComponentSize() on the toggleable gives 48dp; a parent row usually supplies a larger target.
- Contrast. Web: On track #00B140 on white is 2.85:1 and off track #DDDDDD is 1.36:1, both below 3:1; dark lime on #222222 passes, off #444444 is 1.63:1. Thumb position also shows state. Android: Same tokens as web.
- State. Web: aria-checked true/false; the thumb moves right as well as changing colour, so state is not colour alone. Disabled uses the disabled attribute and 50% opacity. Android: toggleableState is announced; enabled = false sets disabled semantics but draws no visual change.
- Motion. Web: Track and thumb animate over motion.switchToggle (500ms ease-in-out); base.css zeroes it under prefers-reduced-motion. Android: Thumb offset and track colour tween over 500ms, set to 0ms when rememberReduceMotion() is true.

Known accessibility gaps:
- Switch.css / EqualSwitch.kt: off track button/disabled #DDDDDD on white is 1.36:1 (dark #444444 on #222222 is 1.63:1) and on track #00B140 on white is 2.85:1, below the 3:1 non-text minimum.
- EqualSwitch.kt: no contentDescription parameter, so a standalone switch with onCheckedChange has no accessible name.
- EqualSwitch.kt: enabled = false changes nothing visually (web dims to 50%).

Example: Interactive
```tsx
const [on, setOn] = useState(true);

<Switch checked={on} onChange={setOn} label="AI Assistant" />
```
```kotlin
var on by remember { mutableStateOf(true) }

// Compose: no label param; set the accessible label with semantics.
EqualSwitch(
    checked = on,
    onCheckedChange = { on = it },
    modifier = Modifier.semantics { contentDescription = "AI Assistant" },
)
```

Example: States
```tsx
<Switch checked label="On" />
<Switch checked={false} label="Off" />
<Switch checked disabled label="On, disabled" />
<Switch checked={false} disabled label="Off, disabled" />
```
```kotlin
Row(horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(20.dp)) {
    EqualSwitch(checked = true, onCheckedChange = {})
    EqualSwitch(checked = false, onCheckedChange = {})
    EqualSwitch(checked = true, onCheckedChange = {}, enabled = false)
    EqualSwitch(checked = false, onCheckedChange = {}, enabled = false)
}
```

Example: In context
```tsx
<RowGroup>
  <ToggleRow label="Mute Promotional Calls" wrap
    description="Equal AI Assistant can identify Promotional Calls and automatically mute them"
    checked={mute} onChange={setMute} />
</RowGroup>
```
```kotlin
var mute by remember { mutableStateOf(true) }

RowGroup {
    ToggleRow(
        label = "Mute Promotional Calls",
        description = "Equal AI Assistant can identify Promotional Calls and automatically mute them",
        descriptionWraps = true,
        checked = mute,
        onCheckedChange = { mute = it },
    )
}
```

entries.name: text-field
entries.title: Text field
entries.summary: A borderless white form field with an uppercase overline label, bodyLarge value, helper and error text, used in the Personal Details and Address forms.
entries.text:
# Text field (`text-field`)
Group: Inputs

A borderless white form field with an uppercase overline label, bodyLarge value, helper and error text, used in the Personal Details and Address forms.

- React: `import { TextField } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `EqualTextField`
- Tokens: `bg/surface`, `stroke/medium`, `action/stroke/unread`, `shadow/focusRing`, `text/primary`, `text/placeholder`, `text/tertiary`, `text/secondary`, `text/danger`
- Source: Surfaces from the Typography screen inventory · Text Field

Do: Write the overline label in the string's natural case; the component uppercases it (rule 5). Use `pill` for single short values (Name) and `rounded` for address lines. Add `className="eq-tnum"` on numeric fields; postal codes use tabular figures (rule 6).

Don't: Don't add a border in light mode; fields are borderless white on bg/primary. Don't put instructions in the placeholder that the user needs after typing; use `helper`. Don't show both helper and error; the error replaces the helper.

Anatomy:
1. Label: Uppercase overline that names the field, with * when required. (overline 11/500 · text/tertiary · margin-bottom 8)
2. Optional marker: '(Optional)' after the label for fields the user may skip. (caption Regular 12/400 · text/tertiary · gap 6)
3. Input container: The surface the user types into. (min height 48 · radius/md 12 · padding 12/14 · bg/surface · border transparent in light, stroke/subtle in dark · focus action/stroke/unread + shadow/focusRing · error text/danger)
4. Value / placeholder: The entered text, or a hint while empty. (bodyLarge 16/400 · text/primary · placeholder text/placeholder · multiline 2 rows)
5. Helper or error: One line below the field: guidance, or the error that replaces it. (captionWrap 12/400 · margin-top 6 · helper text/secondary · error text/danger)

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: Native <input> or <textarea> (textbox). Android: BasicTextField (editable text node).
- Name. Web: A <label htmlFor> wraps the overline, but aria-label={label} overrides it, so the name is the raw label without the * or '(Optional)'. Fields without a label need aria-label. Android: contentDescription ?: label is set in semantics on the field; pass contentDescription when a group shares one label.
- Keyboard. Web: Tab to focus, type; textarea accepts Enter for new lines. Android: TalkBack: double-tap to edit; keyboardOptions sets the IME type and action.
- Touch target. Web: Input min height 48px, full width. Android: heightIn(min = 48.dp), full width.
- Contrast. Web: Value text/primary passes (17:1); label text/tertiary on bg/primary is 4.8:1; placeholder #AAAAAA is 2.3:1. In light the field edge is white on #F7F7F7 (1.07:1) and the focus border #9DDDB4 is 1.6:1. Android: Same tokens; dark mode adds a stroke/subtle border (1.2:1 on #222222).
- State. Web: Error shows a red border plus error text, so it is not colour alone, but the input gets no aria-invalid and the text is not linked with aria-describedby; `required` is not passed to the input. Android: enabled maps to disabled semantics; error is only drawn text, with no semantics { error() }.
- Motion. Web: Border and focus ring fade over 200ms; zeroed under prefers-reduced-motion. Android: No animation; border colour switches instantly.

Known accessibility gaps:
- Inputs.tsx: error and helper text are not linked to the input (no aria-describedby) and errors set no aria-invalid.
- Inputs.kt: EqualTextField does not expose error in semantics (semantics { error(...) }), so TalkBack does not announce it on focus.
- Inputs.tsx: `required` is destructured and never reaches the input (no required / aria-required), and aria-label={label} hides the visible '*'.
- Inputs.tsx: the multiline textarea ignores ...rest, so disabled, required and aria-* props are dropped.
- Inputs.css / Inputs.kt: in light mode the field has a transparent border, so its edge is white on #F7F7F7 (1.07:1), below 3:1.
- Inputs.css / Inputs.kt: focus border action/stroke/unread #9DDDB4 (1.6:1) plus a 12% ring is a weak focus indicator.
- Inputs.css / Inputs.kt: placeholder text/placeholder #AAAAAA on white is 2.3:1.

Example: Name
```tsx
const [name, setName] = useState('Keshav');

<TextField label="Name" value={name} onChange={setName}
  placeholder="Your name" helper="Your AI will call you 'Keshav'" />
```
```kotlin
var name by remember { mutableStateOf("Keshav") }

EqualTextField(
    value = name,
    onValueChange = { name = it },
    label = "Name",
    placeholder = "Your name",
    helper = AnnotatedString("Your AI will call you 'Keshav'"),
)
```

Example: Optional label
```tsx
<TextField label="Guiding direction" optional value={v} onChange={setV}
  placeholder="e.g. Near City Center Mall" />
```
```kotlin
var direction by remember { mutableStateOf("") }

EqualTextField(
    value = direction,
    onValueChange = { direction = it },
    label = "Guiding direction",
    optional = true,
    placeholder = "e.g. Near City Center Mall",
)
```

Example: Multiline and grouped
```tsx
<TextField aria-label="Address line 1" placeholder="Flat, house no., building"
  value={l1} onChange={setL1} multiline />
<TextField aria-label="Address line 2" placeholder="Street, area, landmark"
  value={l2} onChange={setL2} multiline />
```
```kotlin
var line1 by remember { mutableStateOf("") }
var line2 by remember { mutableStateOf("") }

// Fields that share one ADDRESS label omit `label` and pass contentDescription instead.
EqualTextField(
    value = line1,
    onValueChange = { line1 = it },
    contentDescription = "Address line 1",
    placeholder = "Flat, house no., building",
    multiline = true,
)
EqualTextField(
    value = line2,
    onValueChange = { line2 = it },
    contentDescription = "Address line 2",
    placeholder = "Street, area, landmark",
    multiline = true,
)
```

Example: Error
```tsx
<TextField aria-label="Pincode" placeholder="Pincode" value={pin}
  onChange={(v) => setPin(v.replace(/\D/g, '').slice(0, 6))}
  inputMode="numeric" className="eq-tnum" align="center"
  error={/^\d{6}$/.test(pin) ? undefined : 'Enter a 6-digit pincode'} />
```
```kotlin
var pin by remember { mutableStateOf("") }

EqualTextField(
    value = pin,
    onValueChange = { pin = it.filter(Char::isDigit).take(6) },
    contentDescription = "Pincode",
    placeholder = "Pincode",
    keyboardOptions = KeyboardOptions(keyboardType = KeyboardType.Number),
    tabular = true,
    align = TextFieldAlign.Center,
    error = if (pin.length == 6) null else "Enter a 6-digit pincode",
)
```

entries.name: call-history
entries.title: Call history
entries.summary: The Contact Info call-history card (radius 16; outlined in dark) and its rows: direction icon, call type, meta line and time.
entries.text:
# Call history (`call-history`)
Group: Lists & rows

The Contact Info call-history card (radius 16; outlined in dark) and its rows: direction icon, call type, meta line and time.

- React: `import { CallHistoryList, CallHistoryRow } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `CallHistoryList`, `CallHistoryRow`
- Tokens: `bg/surface`, `stroke/subtle`, `stroke/medium`, `text/primary`, `text/secondary`, `text/tertiary`, `text/danger`
- Source: Contact Info · Call history

Do: Separate date and duration in `meta` with " • " ("Today • 30 Sec."). Group rows in a CallHistoryList under a `SectionHeader size="label"` CALL HISTORY header (inset 22).

Don't: Don't colour the "Missed Call" label red; only the icon uses text/danger. Don't pass your own label; the direction sets it.

Anatomy:
1. List card: Rounded card that holds the call rows. (inset 22 · radius 16 · bg/surface · dividers stroke/subtle (stroke/medium in dark) · dark adds a 1dp stroke/subtle outline)
2. Direction icon: Incoming, outgoing or missed arrow. Only the missed icon is red. (24dp · text/primary, text/danger when missed)
3. Call type: Label set by the direction: Incoming Call, Outgoing Call or Missed Call. (bodyLarge, line height 20 · text/primary)
4. Meta line: Date and duration, e.g. 'Today • 30 Sec.'. (11/14 Regular · text/tertiary)
5. Time: Time of the call. (body1 · text/secondary · tabular)
6. Trailing: Optional content after the time, e.g. a play button. (web: any node (e.g. IconButton 32/20) · Compose: onCallClick adds a 48dp call-back button in text/action)

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: Rows are plain divs inside a div; there is no list role. The icon is aria-hidden. Android: Rows are plain Rows. The icon has contentDescription null. The rows are not merged or marked as list items.
- Name. Web: Each row reads as its text: call type, meta, time. Direction comes from the 'Missed Call' text, not the icon. Android: TalkBack reads the label, meta and time as three separate items. The call button is 'Call back'.
- Keyboard. Web: Rows are not focusable. A trailing IconButton is reached with Tab. Android: TalkBack: swipe through the texts. Double-tap 'Call back' when it is shown.
- Touch target. Web: Rows are at least 63 tall. A trailing IconButton at size 32 gets 48 through eq-touch. Android: Rows are at least 63dp. PlainIconButton is 48dp with minimumInteractiveComponentSize.
- Contrast. Web: Type text/primary 18.9:1, meta text/tertiary 5.1:1, time text/secondary 7.5:1, missed icon text/danger 6.2:1. In dark: 14.9, 5.6, 8.3 and 5.6:1. Android: Same tokens and ratios.
- State. Web: Missed is said in the label, so red is not the only signal. Android: Same: the label says 'Missed Call'.
- Motion. Web: None. Android: None.

Known accessibility gaps:
- CallHistoryList and CallHistoryRow in Profile.tsx have no list/listitem semantics, so screen readers don't announce the number of calls.
- CallHistoryRow in Rows.kt doesn't merge descendants, so TalkBack stops on the call type, meta and time separately for every row.

Example: Directions
```tsx
<SectionHeader size="label" inset={22}>Call history</SectionHeader>
<CallHistoryList>
  <CallHistoryRow direction="incoming" meta="Today • 30 Sec." time="02:30 PM" />
  <CallHistoryRow direction="missed" meta="Yesterday" time="11:04 AM" />
  <CallHistoryRow direction="outgoing" meta="12 July • 2 Min." time="06:15 PM" />
</CallHistoryList>
```
```kotlin
SectionHeader(title = "Call history", size = SectionHeaderSize.Label, inset = 22.dp)
CallHistoryList {
    CallHistoryRow(CallDirection.Incoming, meta = "Today • 30 Sec.", time = "02:30 PM")
    CallHistoryRow(CallDirection.Missed, meta = "Yesterday", time = "11:04 AM")
    CallHistoryRow(CallDirection.Outgoing, meta = "12 July • 2 Min.", time = "06:15 PM")
}
```

Example: With trailing
```tsx
<CallHistoryRow direction="incoming" meta="Today • 2 Min." time="03:21 PM"
  trailing={<IconButton icon="play" label="Play recording" size={32} iconSize={20} />} />
```
```kotlin
CallHistoryList {
    // Compose: no custom trailing slot; onCallClick adds the only trailing button (call back, not play)
    CallHistoryRow(CallDirection.Incoming, meta = "Today • 2 Min.", time = "03:21 PM", onCallClick = {})
}
```

entries.name: empty-state
entries.title: Empty state
entries.summary: A centred illustration, title, body and optional action for empty lists and no-results, plus IllustrationHeader for the art at the top of settings detail screens.
entries.text: # Empty state (`empty-state`) Group: Lists & rows A centred illustration, title, body and optional action for empty lists and no-results, plus IllustrationHeader for the art at the top of settings detail screens. - React: `import { EmptyState, IllustrationHeader } from '@equal/ds';` - Compose: `EmptyState`, `IllustrationHeader` - Tokens: `text/primary`, `text/tertiary`, `button/primary` - Source: Surfaces from the Typography screen inventory · Empty / Error State Do: Say what the feature does for the user in the title ("Never explain your address again"). Put the query back in no-results copy and suggest what to try. Don't: Don't crop or recolour the 3D illustrations. Don't show an action when the list fills from elsewhere; if the add button is pinned below, leave it off. Anatomy: 1. Container: Centred column that fills the empty list area. (full width · padding 32 web / 24 Compose · centred) 2. Illustration: Optional 3D illustration on top. (96dp · decorative) 3. Title: Says what the feature does or what is missing. (subheading · text/primary · 16 below the art) 4. Body: Explains the empty state or suggests what to try. (captionWrap · text/tertiary · max 260 web · 4 above) 5. Action: Optional filled button. (Button md 36 · 20 above web / 16 Compose) 6. IllustrationHeader: Large centred art at the top of a settings detail screen. (160dp by default · padding 8 top, 16 bottom) Accessibility: - Role. Web: The title is an h2 and the body a p. Illustrations are , so they are decorative. Android: The title is plain text with no heading(). EqualAssetImage has contentDescription null by default, so the art is skipped. - Name. Web: The action button is named by actionLabel. Android: The button is named by actionLabel. - Keyboard. Web: Only the action is focusable: Tab, then Enter/Space. Android: TalkBack: swipe title → body → button, double-tap to act. - Touch target. Web: The md Button is 36px tall with no eq-touch. Android: EqualButton applies minimumInteractiveComponentSize (48dp). - Contrast. Web: Title text/primary 18.9:1 and body text/tertiary 5.1:1 on bg/surface (4.8:1 on bg/primary). The primary button is 2.85:1 in light and fails; dark is black on lime. Android: Same tokens. - State. Web: A no-results state is not announced when it appears; it has no live region. Android: Same: no liveRegion. - Motion. Web: None. Android: None. Known accessibility gaps: - EmptyState in Dialog.tsx: the md action Button is 36px tall with no eq-touch, so its hit height is 36. - EmptyState in Overlays.kt: the title has no heading() semantics. - No-results EmptyState (Dialog.tsx / Overlays.kt) is not announced when it replaces the list. Wrap it in role="status" / liveRegion when it follows a search. - Primary buttons put text/on-action white on button/primary #00B140 in light mode: 2.85:1, below AA 4.5:1 for 14sp text (Button.css / Buttons.kt). Dark (black on lime) is 17.4:1. Example: Addresses empty ```tsx ``` ```kotlin EmptyState( title = "Never explain your address again", body = "Save frequently used addresses, and your assistant will use them to handle delivery, pickup calls, etc. more naturally.", // Compose: the illustration is a slot, not an asset name illustration = { EqualAssetImage(EqualAssets.IllustrationAddressesEmpty, 96.dp) }, actionLabel = "Add new Address", onActionClick = {}, ) ``` Example: No results ```tsx ``` ```kotlin val query = "Priya" EmptyState(title = "No chats found", body = "Nothing matches \"$query\". Try a name or number.") ``` Example: Illustration header ```tsx ``` ```kotlin IllustrationHeader(asset = EqualAssets.IllustrationSilentMode) RowGroup { ToggleRow( label = "Mute Promotional Calls", description = "Equal AI Assistant can identify Promotional Calls and automatically mute them", descriptionWraps = true, checked = true, onCheckedChange = {}, ) } ```

entries.name: settings-row
entries.title: Settings row
entries.summary: The dense settings row (icon, subheading label, caption description, chevron or switch), grouped into rounded cards with RowGroup.
entries.text: # Settings row (`settings-row`) Group: Lists & rows The dense settings row (icon, subheading label, caption description, chevron or switch), grouped into rounded cards with RowGroup. - React: `import { SettingsRow, ToggleRow, RowGroup } from '@equal/ds';` - Compose: `SettingsRow`, `ToggleRow`, `RowGroup` - Tokens: `bg/surface`, `stroke/subtle`, `text/primary`, `text/tertiary`, `text/placeholder`, `button/primary` - Source: You tab · Settings row Do: Group related rows under a SectionHeader with matching inset. Use `wrap` for descriptions longer than one line so they switch to Regular (rule 3). Use ToggleRow for instant settings and a chevron row for anything that opens a screen. Don't: Don't mix a chevron and a switch on one row. Don't truncate a description that matters; set `wrap`. Anatomy: 1. Row container: Full-width row. It becomes a button when it has onClick. (min height 64 · padding 12/12/12/16 · gap 12 · bg/surface) 2. Leading icon: Optional icon for the setting. (24dp · text/primary) 3. Label: Name of the setting, with an optional NEW badge after it. (subheading · text/primary · truncates · badge gap 8) 4. Description: Secondary line; with wrap it can span several lines. (caption Regular (captionWrap when wrap) · text/tertiary) 5. (track 40×24 · thumb 18 · on button/primary, off button/disabled · thumb text/on-action when on) 7. RowGroup: card: Rounded card that groups rows, with dividers between them.
