entries.name: plan-banner
entries.title: Plan banner
entries.summary: The amber "Reactivate your current Plan…" strip for lapsed plans, under the plan card in Settings or at the top of a chat; plus the plan card link label (Manage plan / Restore Plan / Reactivate plan).
entries.text:
# Plan banner (`plan-banner`)
Group: Monetization

The amber "Reactivate your current Plan…" strip for lapsed plans, under the plan card in Settings or at the top of a chat; plus the plan card link label (Manage plan / Restore Plan / Reactivate plan).

- React: `import { PlanBanner, PlanCard } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `PlanBanner`
- Tokens: `plan-banner/bg`, `plan-banner/text`
- Source: Monetization Flow · lapsed plan

Props of `PlanBanner`:
- `children`: `ReactNode`. Message.
- `attached?`: `boolean`. Hangs under the plan card.
- `onClick?`: `() => void`. Makes the strip tappable.

Do: Use it only when the plan has lapsed or autopay is off.

Don't: Don't use red; it is a nudge, not an error.

Anatomy:
1. Strip: Amber strip that nudges a lapsed plan. (plan-banner/bg · padding 8/12 · gap 8 · attached: inset 8, pulled 14 up under PlanCard, top padding 20, radius 14 bottom only)
2. Info icon: Marks the strip as a notice. (info-fill 16 · plan-banner/text · decorative)
3. Message: What to do, e.g. 'Reactivate your current Plan to use Equal Unlimited'. (caption · plan-banner/text)

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: role=status when static; with onClick it becomes a div role=button with tabIndex 0. Android: Plain text when static; with onClick the Row is clickable(Role.Button). No live region.
- Name. Web: The message text; the icon is aria-hidden. Android: The message text; the icon has contentDescription null.
- Keyboard. Web: When tappable it takes focus but has no key handler, so Enter/Space do nothing. It should be a <button> or handle both keys. Android: TalkBack: swipe to the strip, double-tap to reactivate.
- Touch target. Web: About 32 px tall (44 attached) when tappable; should be at least 48 px. Android: About 32dp tall (44 attached) with no minimum size; should be at least 48dp.
- Contrast. Web: plan-banner/text on plan-banner/bg is 6.0:1 light, 9.0:1 dark. Android: Same tokens: 6.0:1 light, 9.0:1 dark.
- State. Web: The lapsed plan is stated in the text; amber is supporting, never the only signal. Android: Same: the text carries the meaning.

Known accessibility gaps:
- PlanBanner in Monetization.tsx with onClick is a div role=button with no onKeyDown, so Enter/Space don't activate it.
- PlanBanner (Monetization.tsx and Monetization.kt) is about 32 px/dp tall when tappable, below the 48 target.

Example: Under the plan card
```tsx
<PlanCard onManage={reactivate} actionLabel="Reactivate plan" />
<PlanBanner attached>Reactivate your current Plan to use Equal Unlimited</PlanBanner>
```
```kotlin
Column {
    PlanCard(onManageClick = { /* reactivate */ }, manageLabel = "Reactivate plan")
    PlanBanner(text = "Reactivate your current Plan to use Equal Unlimited", attached = true)
}
```

Example: At the top of a chat
```tsx
<PlanBanner onClick={reactivate}>Reactivate your current Plan to keep using Equal Unlimited</PlanBanner>
```
```kotlin
PlanBanner(text = "Reactivate your current Plan to keep using Equal Unlimited", onClick = { /* reactivate */ })
```

entries.name: plan-expiry-banner
entries.title: Plan expiry banner
entries.summary: The strip under the home header as a plan runs out: amber while days remain, red on the last day and after it ends, always with Renew Now.
entries.text:
# Plan expiry banner (`plan-expiry-banner`)
Group: Monetization

The strip under the home header as a plan runs out: amber while days remain, red on the last day and after it ends, always with Renew Now.

- React: `import { PlanExpiryBanner } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `PlanExpiryBanner`
- Tokens: `expiry-banner/warning-bg`, `expiry-banner/warning-text`, `expiry-banner/danger-bg`, `expiry-banner/danger-text`
- Source: Monetization value · Home Screen

Props of `PlanExpiryBanner`:
- `expiry`: `{ state: 'expiring', days } | { state: 'today' } | { state: 'expired', date }`. Where the plan stands; picks the tone and copy.
- `onRenew?`: `() => void`. Renew Now.

Do: Show it full width directly under the home header. Use amber while days remain, red from the last day.

Don't: Don't show it while the plan is comfortably active. Don't stack it with the Reactivate plan banner.

Anatomy:
1. Strip: Full-width strip under the home header as the plan runs out. (min 44 high · padding 6/12 · gap 10 · expiry-banner/warning-bg (days left) or expiry-banner/danger-bg (today, expired))
2. Icon disc: Info icon in a soft disc of the text colour. (info-fill 20 · 3dp padding · circle of the text colour at 12% · decorative)
3. Message: Where the plan stands, with the key part in Bold. (body2 · 'Your Plan Expires in 2 Days' / 'Expires Today' / 'Expired on 30th July' · expiry-banner/*-text)
4. Renew Now: Text action that opens renewal. (button token Bold · underlined, offset 3 · same text colour · 48 touch target)

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: The strip is role=status with a native button inside. Android: The message has liveRegion Polite; Renew Now is clickable(Role.Button).
- Name. Web: Message text, e.g. 'Your Plan Expires in 2 Days'; button 'Renew Now'; icon aria-hidden. Android: Message text and 'Renew Now'; icon contentDescription null.
- Keyboard. Web: Tab to Renew Now, Enter/Space activates. Android: TalkBack reads the message, then 'Renew Now, Button'; double-tap renews.
- Touch target. Web: Renew Now uses eq-touch for a 48 px hit area around the text. Android: Renew Now uses minimumInteractiveComponentSize (48dp).
- Contrast. Web: Warning text 7.1:1 light / 9.0:1 dark; danger text 8.9:1 light / 7.7:1 dark. The link is marked by underline and Bold, not colour. Android: Same tokens and ratios as web.
- State. Web: Amber vs red always comes with the words 'Expires in N Days', 'Today' or 'Expired on'; the live region announces it when it appears. Android: Same; the polite live region announces the message.
- Motion. Web: No animation. Android: No animation.

Example: States
```tsx
<PlanExpiryBanner expiry={{ state: 'expiring', days: 2 }} onRenew={renew} />
<PlanExpiryBanner expiry={{ state: 'today' }} onRenew={renew} />
<PlanExpiryBanner expiry={{ state: 'expired', date: '30th July' }} onRenew={renew} />
```
```kotlin
Column(verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(12.dp)) {
    PlanExpiryBanner(expiry = PlanExpiry.Expiring(days = 2), onRenew = { /* open PaywallScreen */ })
    PlanExpiryBanner(expiry = PlanExpiry.Today, onRenew = { /* open PaywallScreen */ })
    PlanExpiryBanner(expiry = PlanExpiry.Expired(date = "30th July"), onRenew = { /* open PaywallScreen */ })
}
```

entries.name: social-proof
entries.title: Social proof
entries.summary: The subscription page proof block: a big gold stat, the rating pill and a testimonial carousel.
entries.text:
# Social proof (`social-proof`)
Group: Monetization

The subscription page proof block: a big gold stat, the rating pill and a testimonial carousel.

- React: `import { StatBlock, RatingPill, TestimonialCarousel } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `StatBlock`, `RatingPill`, `TestimonialCarousel`
- Tokens: `gradient/gold-text`, `text/gold`, `paywall/card-stroke`
- Source: Monetization Flow · Why people choose

Props of `StatBlock`:
- `value`: `string`. "400k+".
- `label`: `string`. Under it.

Props of `RatingPill`:
- `rating`: `number`. 4.5
- `outOf?`: `number` = 5. Scale.

Props of `TestimonialCarousel`:
- `items`: `{ quote; name; avatar? }[]`. Cards (240 wide), with page dots.

Do: Use real numbers and real reviews only.

Don't: Don't invent testimonials for production.

Anatomy:
1. Panel: SocialProof: gold-washed block with the section label. (radius 28 bottom · bg/surface → paywall/card-bg (30%) wash · padding 24/16/20 · gap 16 · DividerLabel 'Why people choose' over 'EQUAL UNLIMITED' title Bold text/gold)
2. StatBlock: Big gold stat with its label. (value 52/56 Bold -0.04em gradient/gold-text · label body2 text/primary)
3. RatingPill: Rating out of five. (36 high · padding 0 14 · radius 10 · bg/surface · 1dp paywall/card-stroke · gold star 20 · 'Rated' body2 · rating body2 Bold · '/5' body1 text/tertiary)
4. TestimonialCarousel: card: One review card in a sideways scroller. (240 wide · gap 12 · radius 16 · bg/surface · 1dp stroke/subtle · padding 14 · quote body1 text/secondary · avatar 36 + name body2)
5. TestimonialCarousel: dots: Page dots under the cards. (6dp · gap 6 · stroke/medium, current text/gold · decorative)

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: Cards are figure with blockquote and figcaption; the track is a plain scrolling div; dots are aria-hidden. Android: Cards are Columns in a LazyRow; RatingPill is cleared to one description; dots are cleared.
- Name. Web: Stat reads '400k+ People never miss a call'; rating reads 'Rated 4.5 /5' as separate spans; star alt is empty. Android: Rating reads 'Rated 4.5 out of 5'; star has no description.
- Keyboard. Web: The track has no tabIndex and no buttons, so keyboard users can't scroll to later testimonials. Android: TalkBack swipes card by card and scrolls the LazyRow.
- Contrast. Web: Gold stat gradient is 3.5–7.3:1 on white (52 px, large text); 'EQUAL UNLIMITED' text/gold 5.9:1 on paywall/card-bg; quotes text/secondary 7.5:1; '/5' text/tertiary 5.1:1. Gold-on-light passes; dark uses the light gold tokens. Android: Same tokens and ratios as web.
- State. Web: Current page is shown only by the gold dot, which is hidden from assistive tech; no position is announced. Android: Dots are cleared; no page position is announced.
- Motion. Web: Scroll snapping only; no animation. Android: Snap fling only; no animation.

Known accessibility gaps:
- TestimonialCarousel track in Monetization.tsx is not focusable and has no controls, so keyboard users can't reach later testimonials.
- StatBlock in Monetization.tsx paints text with background-clip and color: transparent, so it disappears in forced-colors / high-contrast mode.
- DividerLabel 'Why people choose' (Monetization.tsx and Monetization.kt) is not a heading.

Example: Stat and rating
```tsx
<StatBlock value="400k+" label="People never miss a call" />
<RatingPill rating={4.5} />
```
```kotlin
Column(horizontalAlignment = Alignment.CenterHorizontally, verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(16.dp)) {
    StatBlock(value = "400k+", label = "People never miss a call")
    RatingPill(rating = 4.5f)
}
```

Example: Testimonials
```tsx
<TestimonialCarousel items={[{ quote, name, avatar: <ProfileAvatar variant="female" size={36} /> }, …]} />
```
```kotlin
val avatar = @Composable { asset: EqualAssets -> EqualAssetImage(asset, size = 36.dp, modifier = Modifier.clip(CircleShape)) }
TestimonialCarousel(
    items = listOf(
        Testimonial(
            quote = "As a freelancer, client calls and spam used to mix together. Now I get proper summaries.",
            name = "keerthana",
            avatar = { avatar(EqualAssets.AvatarTestimonial1) },
        ),
        Testimonial(
            quote = "It is a very useful app for screening the unknown calls. This is a must download.",
            name = "Arnav Raj",
            avatar = { avatar(EqualAssets.AvatarTestimonial2) },
        ),
        Testimonial(
            quote = "My parents get loan and insurance calls all day. Equal answers them, and I just read the summary.",
            name = "Riya Kapoor",
            avatar = { avatar(EqualAssets.AvatarTestimonial3) },
        ),
    ),
)
```

entries.name: value-card
entries.title: Value card & sheet
entries.summary: What Unlimited saved you: calls handled, the perks, the expiry chip and the current plan. Inside the sheet that rises after a call near the end of a plan, and on the plan page (circuit pattern, no perks). For free users the QuotaCard counts the week’s calls instead.
entries.text:
# Value card & sheet (`value-card`)
Group: Monetization

What Unlimited saved you: calls handled, the perks, the expiry chip and the current plan. Inside the sheet that rises after a call near the end of a plan, and on the plan page (circuit pattern, no perks). For free users the QuotaCard counts the week’s calls instead.

- React: `import { ValueCard, QuotaCard, ValueSheet, ExpiryChip, PremiumIcon } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `ValueCard`, `QuotaCard`, `ValueSheet`, `ExpiryChip`, `PremiumIcon`
- Tokens: `premium-icon/start`, `premium-icon/end`, `gradient/value-card`, `value-card/stroke`, `value-card/perks-bg`, `value-card/ring`, `expiry-chip/warning-bg`, `expiry-chip/danger-bg`, `expiry-chip/active-bg`
- Source: Monetization value · Value Bottom Sheet Once Called

Props of `ValueCard`:
- `calls`: `number`. Calls the assistant handled.
- `expiry`: `PlanExpiry`. active (until) · expiring (days) · today · expired (date).
- `title?`: `string | null` = 'What Unlimited saved you'. In-card heading; null on the plan page.
- `perks?`: `ValuePerk[] | null` = defaultValuePerks. The three rows; null hides them.
- `price?`: `number` = 39. Current price.
- `was?`: `number` = 49. Struck list price.
- `pattern?`: `'rings' | 'circuit'` = circuit when perks is null. Rings (sheet) or the gold circuit lines (plan page).

Props of `PremiumIcon`:
- `name`: `IconName`. A filled Material Symbol (the -fill icons, timer, person, call-log).
- `size?`: `number` = 16. dp.

Props of `QuotaCard`:
- `quota`: `{ used: number; limit: number; resetsInDays: number }`. This week; used ≥ limit shows Limit Reached.
- `perks?`: `ValuePerk[] | null` = quotaPerks. What Unlimited adds.
- `price?`: `number` = 149. Price.
- `was?`: `number` = 249. Struck list price.

Props of `ValueSheet`:
- `expiry?`: `PlanExpiry`. Paid plan state.
- `quota?`: `Quota`. Free plan: show the QuotaCard (CTA Get Equal AI Unlimited).
- `calls?`: `number` = 20. Calls handled.
- `variant?`: `'card' | 'flush'` = 'card'. Inset card or the card as the sheet (experiment).
- `cta?`: `string` = 'Renew your Equal AI'. Gold CTA.
- `onRenew?`: `() => void`. CTA.
- `onClose?`: `() => void`. The floating close and the scrim.

Do: Show the sheet once, after the assistant handles a call in the last days of a plan. Lead with the number; the user should see what they get before the ask. Perk icons are filled Material Symbols at 16 dp in the premium gold gradient (PremiumIcon), never outlined or flat-tinted. Light cards sit on the premium-glow art; dark cards use the coded black-gold gradient.

Don't: Don't show the sheet on every call or app open. Don't use it for users who never subscribed; they get the paywall.

Anatomy:
1. Container: ValueCard: the gold card that shows what Unlimited did before asking for renewal. (radius 20 · 1dp value-card/stroke · light rings: bg/surface + premium-glow art · dark: gradient/value-card + value-card/ring rings · circuit: paywall/card-bg → bg/surface + gold circuit · padding 18/14 · gap 14)
2. Title: In-card heading, hidden on the plan page. (DividerLabel · subheading Medium uppercase · paywall/divider hairlines · inset 16)
3. Stat: Calls the assistant handled. (count 48/52 Bold -0.04em tabular text/primary · 'Calls Handled' title Medium over 'by your Assistant' body1 · gap 12)
4. Perks: Three things Unlimited did, each with a gold icon. (inset 16 · radius 14 · value-card/perks-bg · 1dp value-card/stroke · rows padding 10/12 · PremiumIcon 16 (premium-icon/start → end) + body2)
5. Date row + ExpiryChip: When the plan ends, with a tinted chip. (paywall/divider rules · label body1 · chip 30 high, radius 6, padding 0 8, 18 Bold tabular · active text/gold on expiry-chip/active-bg · warning/danger expiry-chip tokens)
6. Plan row: Current plan and its price. ('Current Plan' caption text/secondary over plan title SemiBold · ₹price subheading Bold · struck ₹was and period caption text/secondary)
7. ValueSheet: close and CTA: The sheet around the card: floating close and the gold renew button. (panel sheet/bg radius 24 top · 44 neutral close 16 above, centred (48 touch) · block gold CTA 'Renew your Equal AI', padding 16 · flush: card is the top, CTA on bg/surface)
8. QuotaCard: head and bar: Free plan: calls left this week and a gold bar. ('6 out of 30' 30/36 Bold + 'Calls Left' 18 Medium · 10dp bar, paywall/divider track, gradient/cta-gold fill · 'Limit Reached' replaces both at the limit)

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: ValueCard and QuotaCard are <section aria-label>; perks are a ul; the quota bar is role=progressbar with min, max and now; ValueSheet is role=dialog (aria-modal in overlay). Android: The stat row uses clearAndSetSemantics; the quota bar sets progressBarRangeInfo; the sheet panel sets paneTitle.
- Name. Web: Section label is the title or 'N out of M calls left' / 'Limit reached'; bar 'Calls handled this week'; close 'Close'; CTA by its text. PremiumIcon is aria-hidden. Android: Stat reads '20 Calls Handled by your Assistant'; bar 'Calls handled this week'; close 'Close'; scrim onClickLabel 'Close'. PremiumIcon has no description.
- Keyboard. Web: Tab reaches Close then the CTA; the scrim click closes. No Escape key and no focus trap. Android: TalkBack: swipe through the card, then the CTA; Close sits above the panel. System Back is not handled by the component.
- Touch target. Web: Close is 44 px with eq-touch (48); the gold CTA is a 45 px lg button with no extension. Android: Close is a 44dp circle in a 48dp box; EqualButton enforces 48dp.
- Contrast. Web: Text is text/primary or text/secondary (7.5:1). ExpiryChip: active 5.3:1 light / 7.3:1 dark, warning 6.6 / 9.7, danger 5.6 / 7.2. Gold CTA white label runs 6.2:1 to 3.1:1 across gradient/cta-gold. PremiumIcon is decorative (2.2:1 at its light stop). Light cards sit on premium-glow art, dark on the black-gold gradient. Android: Same tokens and ratios as web.
- State. Web: Expiry tone always comes with words ('Plan Expires in', 'Today', 'Expired on'). The quota bar exposes its value; at the limit the bar is replaced by 'Limit Reached'. The struck ₹was is an <s>, which screen readers usually don't announce. Android: Same wording carries the tone. The struck ₹was is a LineThrough span with no description, so it reads as a second price.
- Motion. Web: Sheet slides up (motion.slow); gold CTA sheen and glow; all stop under prefers-reduced-motion. Android: Gold CTA sheen/glow stop under rememberReduceMotion; the ValueSheet slide-up does not check it.

Known accessibility gaps:
- ValueSheet in Monetization.tsx is role=dialog with no Escape to close and no focus trap.
- ValueCard/QuotaCard plan row: the struck ₹was (<s> in Monetization.tsx, LineThrough span in PlanValue.kt) has no 'was' text, so screen readers read '₹39 ₹49 /Monthly'.
- ValueSheet in PlanValue.kt always plays the slide-up and fade; it does not check rememberReduceMotion.
- The gold CTA (Button lg, Button.css) is 45 px tall on web with no touch extension.

Example: Sheet
```tsx
<ValueSheet expiry={{ state: 'expiring', days: 3 }} onRenew={renew} onClose={close} />
```
```kotlin
// Overlay: fills the screen (scrim + sheet); pass inline = true to draw only the panel
ValueSheet(
    expiry = PlanExpiry.Expiring(days = 3),
    onRenew = { /* open PaywallScreen(cta = "Get Equal AI Unlimited") */ },
    onClose = { /* hide the sheet */ },
)
```

Example: Flush sheet (experiment)
```tsx
<ValueSheet variant="flush" expiry={{ state: 'today' }} onRenew={renew} onClose={close} />
```
```kotlin
ValueSheet(
    expiry = PlanExpiry.Today,
    variant = ValueSheetVariant.Flush,
    onRenew = { /* open PaywallScreen(cta = "Get Equal AI Unlimited") */ },
    onClose = { /* hide the sheet */ },
)
```

Example: On the plan page
```tsx
<DividerLabel>What Unlimited Saved You</DividerLabel>
<ValueCard calls={20} title={null} perks={null} expiry={{ state: 'expired', date: '30th July' }} />
```
```kotlin
Column(verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(16.dp)) {
    DividerLabel(text = "What Unlimited Saved You")
    ValueCard(calls = 20, title = null, perks = null, expiry = PlanExpiry.Expired(date = "30th July"))
}
```

Example: Quota: calls left
```tsx
<QuotaCard quota={{ used: 24, limit: 30, resetsInDays: 4 }} />
```
```kotlin
// Free plan: "6 out of 30 Calls Left" with the gold progress bar
QuotaCard(quota = Quota(used = 24, limit = 30, resetsInDays = 4))
```

Example: Quota: limit reached
```tsx
<QuotaCard quota={{ used: 30, limit: 30, resetsInDays: 2 }} />
// in the sheet: <ValueSheet quota={{ used: 30, limit: 30, resetsInDays: 2 }} onRenew={openPaywall} onClose={close} />
```
```kotlin
QuotaCard(quota = Quota(used = 30, limit = 30, resetsInDays = 2))
// in the sheet: ValueSheet(quota = Quota(used = 30, limit = 30, resetsInDays = 2), onRenew = openPaywall, onClose = close)
```

Example: Expiry chips
```tsx
<ExpiryChip tone="active">25th Jun ’26</ExpiryChip>
<ExpiryChip tone="warning">03 Days</ExpiryChip>
<ExpiryChip tone="danger">Today</ExpiryChip>
```
```kotlin
Row(horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(10.dp)) {
    ExpiryChip(text = "25th Jun ’26", tone = ExpiryTone.Active)
    ExpiryChip(text = "03 Days", tone = ExpiryTone.Warning)
    ExpiryChip(text = "Today", tone = ExpiryTone.Danger)
}
```

entries.name: app-bar
entries.title: App bar
entries.summary: The standard screen header with back, a subheading title and trailing actions, plus the uppercase section header that labels groups of rows.
entries.text:
# App bar (`app-bar`)
Group: Navigation

The standard screen header with back, a subheading title and trailing actions, plus the uppercase section header that labels groups of rows.

- React: `import { AppBar, SectionHeader } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `EqualAppBar`, `SectionHeader`
- Tokens: `bg/primary`, `bg/surface`, `shadow/header`, `text/primary`, `text/tertiary`
- Source: Surfaces from the Typography screen inventory · App Bar, Section Header

Do: Centre the title in flow screens (Personal Details, Your Addresses, Contact Info). Keep SectionHeader side inset equal to the RowGroup inset below it (20 on the You tab).

Don't: Don't write section headers in capitals in source; pass normal text and let the component uppercase it. Don't put a filled Button in the app bar; trailing actions are icon or text buttons.

Anatomy:
1. Container: Header surface at the top of a screen. (center 56 high · start 64 high · bg/primary default, bg/surface or transparent · elevated adds shadow/header)
2. Status bar: Optional mock status bar on the same background. (52 high · statusBar prop)
3. Back button: Ghost icon button that goes back. (arrow-back 24 · web 40 + eq-touch, Compose 48 · padding 4 start / 8 end)
4. Title: Screen name, one line, centred by default. (subheading 16/500 · text/primary · ellipsis · centre uses equal side columns)
5. Trailing actions: Optional actions at the end. (`trailing` / `actions` slot)
6. SectionHeader: Uppercase region label with an optional action. (overline 11/500 text/tertiary · padding 24 top / 12 bottom / inset 20 · label size 13 text/secondary, 30 / 18)

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: <header> landmark with the title as <h1>; SectionHeader is plain text, not a heading. Android: Column/Row with plain text; the title has no heading() semantics.
- Name. Web: Back is IconButton label 'Back'; the h1 text names the screen. Android: PlainIconButton contentDescription 'Back'.
- Keyboard. Web: Tab reaches Back, then trailing actions; screen-reader users can jump to the h1. Android: TalkBack: swipe through Back, title and actions; headings navigation does not find the title.
- Touch target. Web: Back is 40px with .eq-touch for 48px. Android: PlainIconButton is 48dp with minimumInteractiveComponentSize(); the SectionHeader action is clickable text with no minimum size.
- Contrast. Web: Title text/primary 17:1; SectionHeader text/tertiary on bg/primary 4.8:1, label size text/secondary 7:1. Android: Same tokens; a SectionHeader action in text/action #00B140 is 2.85:1 on white.

Known accessibility gaps:
- ChatHeader.kt: EqualAppBar's title has no semantics { heading() } (web uses <h1>).
- AppBar.tsx / Rows.kt: SectionHeader is not exposed as a heading (web span, Compose plain text).
- Rows.kt: the SectionHeader action is a clickable EqualText with no minimumInteractiveComponentSize, so its target is about 16dp high, and its text/action label is 2.85:1 in light.

Example: Centred (flows)
```tsx
<AppBar title="Personal Details" onBack={goBack} />
```
```kotlin
EqualAppBar(title = "Personal Details", onBackClick = {})
```

Example: Start-aligned, elevated, with trailing
```tsx
<AppBar title="Active Instructions" align="start" surface="surface" elevated
  onBack={goBack} trailing={<TextButton leadingIcon="add">Add</TextButton>} />
```
```kotlin
EqualAppBar(
    title = "Active Instructions",
    onBackClick = {},
    align = AppBarAlign.Start,
    background = EqualTheme.colors.bgSurface,
    elevated = true,
) {
    EqualTextButton(text = "Add", onClick = {}, leadingIcon = EqualIcons.Add)
}
```

Example: Section headers
```tsx
<SectionHeader>Your assistant</SectionHeader>
<SectionHeader qualifier="(Optional)">Guiding direction</SectionHeader>
<SectionHeader action={<TextButton size="small">Clear all</TextButton>}>
  Recommended for you
</SectionHeader>
```
```kotlin
// Pass normal text; SectionHeader uppercases it.
SectionHeader(title = "Your assistant")
// Compose: no `qualifier` slot; it is appended to the title (and uppercased with it).
SectionHeader(title = "Guiding direction (Optional)")
SectionHeader(title = "Recommended for you", actionLabel = "Clear all", onActionClick = {})
```

entries.name: bottom-nav
entries.title: Bottom nav
entries.summary: The floating two-tab pill (Chats, You) with an unread count, beside the Equal orb FAB that opens the assistant.
entries.text:
# Bottom nav (`bottom-nav`)
Group: Navigation

The floating two-tab pill (Chats, You) with an unread count, beside the Equal orb FAB that opens the assistant.

- React: `import { BottomNav, Fab } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `BottomNavBar`, `EqualFab`
- Tokens: `bg/surface`, `shadow/nav`, `nav/selected-bg`, `text/action`, `text/tertiary`, `text/secondary`, `button/primary`, `text/on-action`
- Source: §4 Tab Bar (Bottom Navigation)

Do: Float the nav over content and leave ~104dp bottom padding so the last row is reachable. Pass the user's gender as `avatar` so the You tab matches the profile avatar.

Don't: Don't add a third tab; the pill is Chats and You. Don't replace the FAB orb with an icon; the orb carries its own glow.

Anatomy:
1. Pill container: Floating surface that holds the two tabs. (padding 8 · radius full · bg/surface · shadow/nav)
2. Tab item: One destination capsule; the selected one is filled. (web 84 × 56, Compose 99 × 52 · radius full · selected nav/selected-bg)
3. Icon: Chats bubble (filled when selected) or the user's ProfileAvatar. (24 · selected text/action · unselected text/secondary · avatar lifted 3)
4. Count badge: Unread count on the Chats icon. (16 · 1.5 bg/surface ring · button/primary · web 99+, Compose 9+)
5. Label: Tab name under the icon. (caption 12/500 · gap 2 · selected text/action · unselected text/tertiary)
6. Fab: The Equal orb button beside the pill that opens the assistant. (58 · gap 16 · orb image carries its glow)

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: <nav aria-label='Main'> with <button> items; the current one has aria-current='page'. Fab is a <button>. Android: selectable(role = Role.Tab) per item; EqualFab is clickable(role = Role.Button). The row has no selectableGroup().
- Name. Web: Item text plus contents: 'Chats' plus the count digits, and 'Your profile You' because ProfileAvatar keeps its alt. Fab aria-label 'Talk to Equal AI'. Android: Merged text: the count then 'Chats'; the You avatar has contentDescription = null. Fab 'Ask Equal AI'.
- Keyboard. Web: Tab through Chats, You, Fab; Enter or Space activates. Android: TalkBack: swipe between tabs, announces 'selected' and 'tab'; double-tap to switch.
- Touch target. Web: Items 84 × 56, Fab 58. Android: Items 99 × 52, Fab 58.
- Contrast. Web: Unselected label text/tertiary on white 5.1:1; selected text/action #00B140 on #F1FAF3 is 2.7:1 in light; dark lime on #272C1E 11.9:1. Android: Same tokens as web.
- State. Web: aria-current='page'; selection also fills the capsule and switches the chat icon to filled, not colour alone. Android: selected semantics from selectable; the capsule fill and icon change too.
- Motion. Web: Capsule fill and colour fade over 200ms; Fab press scale; zeroed under prefers-reduced-motion. Android: Fab press scale via eqPressFeedback; tab switch is instant.

Known accessibility gaps:
- BottomNav.tsx: the You tab's name includes ProfileAvatar's alt, so it reads 'Your profile You'; pass an empty label.
- BottomNav.tsx / BottomNavBar.kt: the Chats count is read as a bare number (web aria-label on a role-less span is ignored; Compose NavCountBadge has no semantics); it should say 'N unread'.
- BottomNav.css / BottomNavBar.kt: selected label text/action #00B140 on nav/selected-bg #F1FAF3 is 2.7:1 in light mode.
- BottomNavBar.kt: the tab Row has no selectableGroup(), so TalkBack does not announce the tab count or position.
- BottomNav.tsx / BottomNavBar.kt: Fab names differ ('Talk to Equal AI' on web, 'Ask Equal AI' on Android).

Example: Interactive
```tsx
const [tab, setTab] = useState<NavTab>('chats');

<BottomNav active={tab} onChange={setTab} unread={7} />
```
```kotlin
var tab by remember { mutableStateOf(EqualTab.Chats) }

BottomNavBar(
    selectedTab = tab,
    onTabSelected = { tab = it },
    onFabClick = {},
    chatsBadgeCount = 7,
)
```

Example: You active, female avatar, no FAB
```tsx
<BottomNav active="you" avatar="female" showFab={false} />
```
```kotlin
// Compose: BottomNavBar always draws the FAB; there is no showFab = false.
BottomNavBar(
    selectedTab = EqualTab.You,
    onTabSelected = {},
    onFabClick = {},
    avatar = ProfileAvatarVariant.Female,
)
```

Example: FAB on its own
```tsx
<Fab onClick={openAssistant} />
```
```kotlin
EqualFab(onClick = {})
```

entries.name: chat-header
entries.title: Chat header
entries.summary: Headers for the chat surfaces: the in-conversation header (with the Takeover pill on a live call), the chat-list selection header, and the home header with the assistant toggle.
entries.text:
# Chat header (`chat-header`)
Group: Navigation

Headers for the chat surfaces: the in-conversation header (with the Takeover pill on a live call), the chat-list selection header, and the home header with the assistant toggle.

- React: `import { ChatHeader, TakeoverPill, SelectionHeader, HomeHeader } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `ChatHeader`, `TakeoverPill`, `SelectionChatHeader`, `HomeHeader`
- Tokens: `bg/surface`, `bg/primary`, `shadow/header`, `gradient/takeover`, `action/stroke/unread`, `shadow/glass`, `text/action`, `text/primary`, `text/tertiary`, `button/danger`
- Source: §5 Chat Header (In-Conversation)

Do: Show the phone number as the subtitle normally and a status line ("You have a visitor") during a live call. During a live call show only the Takeover pill; the call and more buttons go away. Route selection-mode Delete through the delete confirm sheet.

Don't: Don't show Takeover alongside the call button; that is two actions for the same intent. Don't truncate the phone number with custom styles; it is tabular and one line.

Anatomy:
1. Container: White header at the top of a conversation. (64 high · bg/surface · shadow/header · padding web 4/8, Compose h12)
2. Back button: Goes back to the chat list. (arrow-back 24 · web 36 + eq-touch, Compose 48)
3. Avatar: Contact or category avatar, or the orb for Equal AI's own chat. (36 · ContactAvatar or AiAvatar)
4. Name and subtitle: Who the chat is with, and a phone number or status line. (name subheading 16/500 text/primary · subtitle caption Regular 12/400 text/tertiary, tabular for numbers · gap 12 after avatar)
5. Trailing actions: Call and More options, or the Takeover pill on a live call. (call + more-vert 24 · web 36 + eq-touch, Compose 48)
6. TakeoverPill: Glass pill that takes over a live call. (34 high · padding h14 · gradient/takeover · 1px action/stroke/unread · shadow/glass · call-filled 18 + button text/action)
7. SelectionHeader: Selection-mode bar: count, Mark read, Delete, then Select All. (row 64 · 'N Selected' subheading · Mark read 26 high pill · delete button/danger · Select All row 40 with checkbox)
8. HomeHeader: Status bar, TopBar and the assistant toggle card on bg/primary. (bg/primary · shadow/header · toggle card padding 0 12 12)

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: <header> with IconButtons; the name is a <div>, not a heading. Takeover and Mark read are <button>s. Android: Row with PlainIconButtons (Role.Button); name is plain text with no heading().
- Name. Web: 'Back', 'Call', 'More options'; Takeover and Mark read use visible text; selection back is 'Exit selection'; the home toggle switch is 'AI Assistant'. Android: 'Back', 'Call', 'More options', 'Delete'; Takeover and Mark read by text; selection back is 'Back'.
- Keyboard. Web: Tab order: Back, Call, More (or Takeover); in selection mode Back, Mark read, Delete, Select All. Android: TalkBack: swipe in the same order; the Select All row is one checkbox node.
- Touch target. Web: 36px buttons get 48px via .eq-touch, but with a 4px gap their hit areas overlap by 8px; Takeover and Mark read use .eq-touch; Select All is 40px high. Android: Icon buttons 48dp; TakeoverPill and MarkReadPill use minimumInteractiveComponentSize(); the Select All row is 40dp high with none.
- Contrast. Web: Name 17:1, subtitle text/tertiary 5.1:1; Takeover text/action on gradient/takeover is about 2.6:1 in light, lime on #2F3423 in dark passes; delete #C50000 6.2:1. Android: Same tokens as web.
- State. Web: Live call is shown by Takeover replacing Call and More; the selection count is text but is not announced when it changes. Android: Select All exposes checked state via toggleable(Role.Checkbox); the count is plain text with no live region.
- Motion. Web: Press scale on buttons and pills; zeroed under prefers-reduced-motion. Android: eqPressFeedback on pills, following the system animator scale.

Known accessibility gaps:
- ChatHeader.tsx / ChatHeader.kt: the contact name is not a heading (web div, Compose text without heading()).
- ChatHeader.tsx / ChatHeader.kt: the 'N Selected' count is not a live region, so changes are not announced.
- ChatHeader.kt: the SelectionChatHeader Select All row is 40dp high with no minimumInteractiveComponentSize; on web the Checkbox is also 40px.
- ChatHeader.tsx: 36px icon buttons 4px apart with eq-touch give 48px hit areas that overlap by 8px.
- ChatHeader.css / ChatHeader.kt: TakeoverPill text/action on gradient/takeover is about 2.6:1 in light mode.

Example: Default
```tsx
<ChatHeader name="Amit Nanda" subtitle="+91 98717 46113"
  avatar={{ initials: 'AN' }} onBack={goBack} onCall={call} onMore={openInfo} />
```
```kotlin
ChatHeader(
    name = "Amit Nanda",
    subtitle = "+91 98717 46113",
    initials = "AN",
    onBackClick = {},
    onCallClick = {},
    onMoreClick = {},
)
```

Example: Live call
```tsx
<ChatHeader name="Arnav Raj" subtitle="You have a visitor" live
  onBack={goBack} onTakeover={takeover} />
```
```kotlin
ChatHeader(
    name = "Arnav Raj",
    subtitle = "You have a visitor",
    subtitleIsPhone = false,
    variant = ChatHeaderVariant.LiveCall,
    onBackClick = {},
    onTakeoverClick = {},
)
```

Example: Selection mode
```tsx
<SelectionHeader count={1} allSelected={false}
  onSelectAll={selectAll} onBack={exit} onMarkRead={markRead} onDelete={confirmDelete} />
```
```kotlin
var allSelected by remember { mutableStateOf(false) }

SelectionChatHeader(
    selectedCount = if (allSelected) 3 else 1,
    allSelected = allSelected,
    onSelectAllChange = { allSelected = it },
    onBackClick = {},
    onMarkReadClick = {},
    onDeleteClick = {},
)
```

Example: Home
```tsx
const [on, setOn] = useState(true);

<HomeHeader assistantOn={on} onAssistantChange={setOn} />
```
```kotlin
var on by remember { mutableStateOf(true) }

HomeHeader(assistantOn = on, onAssistantChange = { on = it })
```

Example: Takeover pill
```tsx
<TakeoverPill onClick={takeover} />
```
```kotlin
TakeoverPill(onClick = {})
```

entries.name: status-bar
entries.title: Status bar
entries.summary: The Material 3 Android status bar (52dp: Roboto time; wifi, triangle signal and an upright battery) for mocks, flows and screen demos.
entries.text:
# Status bar (`status-bar`)
Group: Navigation

The Material 3 Android status bar (52dp: Roboto time; wifi, triangle signal and an upright battery) for mocks, flows and screen demos.

- React: `import { StatusBar } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `StatusBar`
- Tokens: `bg/primary`, `text/primary`
- Source: §1 Status Bar

Do: Use it only in mocks and flow demos; the app draws edge-to-edge and pads with `WindowInsets.statusBars`. Match `background` to the surface beneath (bg/surface under white headers).

Don't: Don't add carrier names or extra icons; the Material 3 bar is time + wifi + signal + battery.

Anatomy:
1. Container: Full-width strip at the top of a mock screen. (52 high · padding h24 · bg/primary default (match the header))
2. Time: Clock text on the left. (Roboto Medium 14/20 · tracking 0.1 · tabular · text/primary)
3. System icons: Wifi, signal and battery on the right. (18 each · gap 4 · order wifi, signal, battery · text/primary)

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: Plain <div>; the icons are aria-hidden, but the time text is exposed. Android: Row with BasicText time and icons with contentDescription = null.
- Name. Web: None needed: it is a mock of system chrome and should be hidden (aria-hidden='true') so the fake '12:30' is not read. Android: Should be hidden (clearAndSetSemantics {}) in catalog screens; real apps draw under the system bar with WindowInsets.statusBars.
- Contrast. Web: text/primary on bg/primary is 17.6:1 in light, #F7F7F7 on #141414 in dark; a custom `color` must keep 4.5:1. Android: Same tokens; the `color` parameter must keep 4.5:1 on `background`.

Known accessibility gaps:
- StatusBar.tsx: the mock bar is not aria-hidden, so screen readers read the fake time '12:30'.
- HomeChrome.kt: StatusBar's time text is exposed to TalkBack; wrap it in clearAndSetSemantics {}.

Example: Default
```tsx
<StatusBar />
```
```kotlin
StatusBar()
```

Example: On a white header
```tsx
<StatusBar time="9:41" background="var(--eq-bg-surface)" />
<AppBar title="Contact Info" surface="surface" onBack={goBack} />
```
```kotlin
Column {
    StatusBar(time = "9:41", background = EqualTheme.colors.bgSurface)
    EqualAppBar(title = "Contact Info", onBackClick = {}, background = EqualTheme.colors.bgSurface)
}
```

entries.name: top-bar
entries.title: Top bar
entries.summary: The Chats home bar: the vector Equal AI logo with the plan marker, plus the logo and mark on their own.
entries.text:
# Top bar (`top-bar`)
Group: Navigation

The Chats home bar: the vector Equal AI logo with the plan marker, plus the logo and mark on their own.

- React: `import { TopBar, EqualLogo, EqualMark } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `TopBar`, `EqualLogo`, `EqualMark`
- Tokens: `text/action`, `gradient/gold`, `text/on-dark`
- Source: §2 Top Bar (Logo + Availability Status)

Do: Use the vector logo in text/action so it is #00B140 in light and lime in dark. Keep the logo 20dp high in the top bar.

Don't: Don't use a raster logo; the logo is coded as vector paths. Don't stretch or recolour the lockup outside text/action.

Anatomy:
1. Container: Home bar holding the logo, plan marker and trailing actions. (56 high · padding h16 · gap 8 · transparent on bg/primary)
2. EqualLogo: Six-dot mark plus 'equal ai' wordmark. (20 high · 113:24 aspect · text/action (#00B140 light, lime dark))
3. PlanBadge: Plan marker after the logo. (16 high · radius 4 · gradient/gold + text/on-dark, or expired #D0302F + white)
4. Trailing slot: Optional actions at the end, e.g. search. (pushed right by a flex spacer)
5. EqualMark: The six-dot mark alone. (width 23 default · 488:428 aspect)

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: Plain <div>; EqualLogo is an <svg role='img'>; EqualMark is aria-hidden unless given a title. Android: Row; EqualLogo is an Image; EqualMark contentDescription defaults to null.
- Name. Web: Logo reads 'Equal AI', then the badge text ('UNLIMITED' or 'PLAN EXPIRED'). Trailing buttons need their own labels. Android: EqualLogo contentDescription 'Equal AI', then the PlanBadge text.
- Keyboard. Web: Nothing focusable except what you put in `trailing`. Android: TalkBack: logo and badge are read in order; trailing actions are focusable.
- Contrast. Web: The logo is exempt as a logotype. PlanBadge white on gradient/gold is 2.2–4.3:1 (fails); the expired badge is 5.1:1. Android: Same tokens as web.
- State. Web: Plan state is in the badge text, not colour alone. Android: Same.

Known accessibility gaps:
- TopBar.tsx / HomeChrome.kt: the PlanBadge it renders has white text on gradient/gold at 2.2–4.3:1, below 4.5:1.

Example: Default
```tsx
<TopBar />
```
```kotlin
TopBar()
```

Example: Without a plan, with a trailing action
```tsx
<TopBar plan={null} trailing={<IconButton icon="search" label="Search chats" />} />
```
```kotlin
TopBar(planLabel = null) {
    EqualIconButton(icon = EqualIcons.Search, contentDescription = "Search chats", onClick = {})
}
```

Example: Logo and mark
```tsx
<EqualLogo height={20} />
<EqualLogo height={20} variant="wordmark" />
<EqualMark width={23} />
```
```kotlin
Row(horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(24.dp), verticalAlignment = Alignment.CenterVertically) {
    EqualLogo(height = 20.dp)
    EqualLogo(height = 20.dp, variant = EqualLogoVariant.WORDMARK)
    EqualMark(width = 23.dp, color = EqualTheme.colors.textAction)
}
```

entries.name: bottom-sheet
entries.title: Bottom sheet
entries.summary: Sheets that rise over the current screen: the standard sheet with a floating close or title row, the centred confirm content for destructive actions, and the full-height sheet for the instruction setup chat.
entries.text:
# Bottom sheet (`bottom-sheet`) Group: Overlays Sheets that rise over the current screen: the standard sheet with a floating close or title row, the centred confirm content for destructive actions, and the full-height sheet for the instruction setup chat. - React: `import { BottomSheet, ConfirmSheetContent, FullSheet } from '@equal/ds';` - Compose: `EqualBottomSheet`, `ConfirmSheetContent`, `FullSheet` - Tokens: `scrim`, `sheet/bg`, `bg/surface`, `shadow/raised`, `text/secondary`, `text/primary`, `button/danger`, `text/on-danger`, `chat/wallpaper-bg` - Source: §17 Bottom Sheet Do: Name the thing being deleted in the title and put its number in `subject` ("Delete chat with Amit Nanda", "(+91 9871746113)"). State the consequence in the body ("This action cannot be undone."). Render overlays inside a positioned container such as PhoneFrame; use mode="inline" in docs. Don't: Don't put a Cancel button next to the confirm; the close button and scrim are the revise path. Don't use a sheet for a quick yes/no that needs no context; use a Dialog. Don't show both a title row and the floating close. Anatomy: 1. Scrim: Dims the screen. Tapping it closes the sheet. (scrim · fades over duration-slow) 2. Sheet container: Panel anchored to the bottom that holds the content and scrolls when tall. (sheet/bg · radius 32 top (24 with a title) · padding 24/24/28 web, 24 Compose · max height 92%) 3. Close button: Floating close in the top-right corner, shown when there is no title. (IconButton neutral 44 · bg/surface · shadow/raised · close 22 text/secondary · inset 16 web / 12 Compose) 4. Title row: Optional row: close (X) on the left and a centred title. It replaces the floating close. (grid 40 / 1fr / 40 · subheading · centred · close ghost 40 (48 in Compose)) 5. ConfirmSheetContent: illustration: Centred 3D illustration above the confirm text. (72dp · illustration-trash by default) 6. ConfirmSheetContent: title, subject, body: Names the thing affected, then the consequence. (title token text/primary · subject body1 text/secondary tabular · body body1 text/secondary, 12 above) 7. ConfirmSheetContent: confirm button: One full-width commit, danger with the trash icon when destructive. (Button lg block · 45 high · 28 above · button/danger + text/on-danger) 8. FullSheet: header and body: Full-height variant: orb, title and close over the chat wallpaper, with an optional pinned footer. (top 72 · radius 24 top · header padding 14/14/14/16 · orb 32 · 1dp stroke/subtle below · chat/wallpaper-bg) Accessibility: - Role. Web: The sheet is role="dialog" with aria-modal in overlay mode. A title renders as an h2, and so does the ConfirmSheetContent title. FullSheet is a section with role="dialog" and aria-modal. Android: EqualBottomSheet and FullSheet are plain Boxes with no paneTitle or dialog semantics. The scrim is a Role.Button with onClickLabel 'Dismiss'. - Name. Web: aria-label is the title, or the label prop (default 'Sheet'). Close buttons are labelled 'Close'. Android: Close icons have contentDescription 'Close'. The sheet itself has no name, so TalkBack does not announce it when it opens. - Keyboard. Web: Escape and a scrim click call onClose. Focus is not moved into the sheet, trapped, or returned to the trigger. Android: TalkBack: swipe to the close button and double-tap. There is no BackHandler, so system Back does not close the sheet, and content behind the scrim stays in the swipe order. - Touch target. Web: Close IconButtons (44 or 40) use eq-touch for a 48px area. The lg confirm button is 45px with no eq-touch. Android: EqualIconButton and PlainIconButton apply minimumInteractiveComponentSize (48dp), and so does the 45dp confirm button. - Contrast. Web: Body text/secondary on sheet/bg is 7.1:1 in light and 7.6:1 in dark. Danger text/on-danger on button/danger is 6.2:1 light and 7.3:1 dark. A non-destructive primary confirm is white on green, 2.85:1 in light. Android: Same tokens and ratios. In dark the primary confirm is black on lime. - State. Web: The closed overlay gets aria-hidden plus visibility:hidden, so it leaves the tab order. A closed FullSheet only gets aria-hidden and pointer-events:none. Android: Visibility comes from AnimatedVisibility. No open/closed state is exposed to accessibility services. - Motion. Web: The sheet slides up and the scrim fades over duration-slow. The base.css reduced-motion rule sets these transitions to 0ms. Android: Scrim fade 200ms, slide 320ms standard (FullSheet 320ms both). Not gated on rememberReduceMotion(). Known accessibility gaps: - BottomSheet.tsx and FullSheet in Flows.tsx: focus is not moved into the dialog, not trapped, and not returned to the trigger on close, and the page behind is not made inert. - FullSheet in Flows.tsx: when closed, the panel is only aria-hidden and pointer-events:none, so its Close button can still be reached with Tab. Add visibility:hidden or inert. - EqualBottomSheet (BottomSheet.kt) and FullSheet (Flows.kt) have no BackHandler and no paneTitle, and the content behind the scrim stays reachable by TalkBack. - EqualBottomSheet and FullSheet animations are not gated on rememberReduceMotion() (BottomSheet.kt, Flows.kt). - The ConfirmSheetContent title is not marked as a heading in Compose (BottomSheet.kt). - The ConfirmSheetContent lg Button is 45px tall on web with no eq-touch, so it is under 48 (BottomSheet.tsx). - Primary buttons put text/on-action white on button/primary #00B140 in light mode: 2.85:1, below AA 4.5:1 for 14sp text (Button.css / Buttons.kt). Dark (black on lime) is 17.4:1. Example: Delete confirm (inline) ```tsx Delete chat with
Amit Nanda} subject="(+91 9871746113)" body="All past conversations will be deleted. This action cannot be undone." confirmLabel="Delete" destructive /> ``` ```kotlin // Compose: no inline mode; the sheet always draws over its parent with the scrim EqualBottomSheet(visible = true, onDismissRequest = {}) { ConfirmSheetContent( title = "Delete chat with\nAmit Nanda", phone = "(+91 9871746113)", body = "All past conversations will be deleted. entries.name: context-menu
entries.title: Context menu
entries.summary: The long-press menu of icon + label items, and OverflowMenu, the ⋮ button that opens one anchored to a card.
entries.text:
# Context menu (`context-menu`)
Group: Overlays

The long-press menu of icon + label items, and OverflowMenu, the ⋮ button that opens one anchored to a card.

- React: `import { ContextMenu, OverflowMenu } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `ContextMenu`, `ContextMenuPopup`, `OverflowMenu`
- Tokens: `bg/surface`, `shadow/card`, `stroke/subtle`, `text/primary`, `text/tertiary`, `text/danger`
- Source: §18 Context Menu (Long-press)

Do: Put the destructive item last and mark it `danger`. Name the object in destructive labels ("Delete instruction", "Delete address").

Don't: Don't put more than four or five items in a menu. Don't delete straight from the menu; open the confirm sheet.

Anatomy:
1. Container: Floating surface that holds the menu items. (bg/surface · radius 12 · shadow/card · min width 131 (168 in OverflowMenu))
2. Item: One full-width row per action. (40 high · padding 0 16 0 12 web, h12 Compose · gap 10)
3. Item icon: Leading glyph for the action. (16dp · text/tertiary (text/danger when danger))
4. Item label: Verb naming the action, e.g. 'Delete instruction'. (body1 · text/primary (text/danger when danger))
5. Divider: Hairline between items. (1dp · stroke/subtle)
6. OverflowMenu: trigger: The ⋮ button that opens the menu anchored to a card. (IconButton 32 · more-vert 20 · menu 30 below, 6 in from the right)

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: The container is role="menu" and each item is a button with role="menuitem". The ⋮ trigger is a button with aria-expanded. Android: Items are clickable Rows with Role.Button. OverflowMenu opens a focusable Popup. The trigger is a clickable Box with Role.Button.
- Name. Web: Items are named by their visible label (icons are aria-hidden). The trigger's aria-label defaults to 'More options'; AddressCard passes '{label} options', and InstructionCard passes 'Instruction options'. Android: Item labels are their text. The trigger contentDescription defaults to 'More options' and uses the same strings.
- Keyboard. Web: Enter or Space on ⋮ toggles the menu. Escape or a click outside closes it. Focus stays on the trigger, and items are reached with Tab; there is no Arrow/Home/End handling. Android: The Popup is focusable, so Back or a tap outside dismisses it. TalkBack: swipe through the items, double-tap to select. The menu closes before onSelect runs.
- Touch target. Web: Items are 40px tall with no eq-touch. The 32px trigger gets 48 through IconButton's eq-touch. Android: Items are 40dp tall. The OverflowMenu trigger is a 32dp Box with no minimumInteractiveComponentSize.
- Contrast. Web: Labels text/primary 18.9:1. Icons text/tertiary 5.1:1. Danger text/danger 6.2:1 in light and 5.6:1 in dark. Android: Same tokens and ratios.
- State. Web: Open state is aria-expanded on the trigger. Danger items are marked by colour and by the explicit verb ('Delete …'). Android: Open and closed are not exposed; there is no stateDescription on the trigger. Danger items use colour plus the verb.
- Motion. Web: The menu appears without animation. Android: The Popup appears without animation.

Known accessibility gaps:
- ContextMenu.tsx and ContextMenu.kt: items are 40 tall, below the 48 minimum target.
- OverflowMenu in Flows.tsx: focus is not moved into the menu on open, and there is no Arrow/Home/End navigation or aria-haspopup="menu", all of which role=menu implies.
- OverflowMenu in Flows.kt: the 32dp trigger has no minimumInteractiveComponentSize, and it exposes no expanded/collapsed state.

Example: Chat long-press
```tsx
<ContextMenu items={[
  { label: 'Mark as read', icon: 'done-all' },
  { label: 'Call back', icon: 'call' },
  { label: 'Delete chat', icon: 'delete', danger: true },
]} />
```
```kotlin
ContextMenu(
    items = listOf(
        ContextMenuItem("Mark as read", EqualIcons.DoneAll, onClick = {}),
        ContextMenuItem("Call back", EqualIcons.Call, onClick = {}),
        ContextMenuItem("Delete chat", EqualIcons.Delete, onClick = {}, destructive = true),
    ),
)
```

Example: Overflow menu
```tsx
<OverflowMenu items={[
  { label: 'Edit', icon: 'edit', onSelect: edit },
  { label: 'Delete instruction', icon: 'delete', danger: true, onSelect: confirmDelete },
]} />
```
```kotlin
OverflowMenu(
    items = listOf(
        ContextMenuItem("Edit", EqualIcons.Edit, onClick = {}),
        ContextMenuItem("Delete instruction", EqualIcons.Delete, onClick = {}, destructive = true),
    ),
)
```

entries.name: dialog
entries.title: Dialog
entries.summary: A centred decision dialog with a text cancel and one filled commit, plus the inverse-surface Snackbar that confirms an action afterwards.
entries.text:
# Dialog (`dialog`)
Group: Overlays

A centred decision dialog with a text cancel and one filled commit, plus the inverse-surface Snackbar that confirms an action afterwards.

- React: `import { Dialog, Snackbar } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `EqualDialog`, `EqualDialogContent`, `EqualSnackbar`
- Tokens: `bg/surface`, `shadow/nav`, `scrim`, `text/primary`, `text/secondary`, `text/tertiary`, `button/primary`, `button/danger`, `button/secondary`
- Source: Surfaces from the Typography screen inventory · Dialog, Snackbar/Toast

Do: Commit is filled and cancel is a text action, right-aligned (rule 4). Reuse the verb from the control: Turn off → "Turn off" button → "Call learning turned off" snackbar. Offer Undo on the snackbar for reversible deletes.

Don't: Don't write "OK" / "Yes" as the commit; name the action. Don't stack a snackbar on an open dialog.

Anatomy:
1. Scrim: Dims the screen behind the dialog. Tapping it cancels. (scrim · web overlay covers the nearest positioned ancestor · Compose uses a platform Dialog window)
2. Container: Centred surface that holds the decision. (312 wide (max 100% - 48) · bg/surface · radius 24 · padding 24 · shadow/nav (web))
3. Title: The question, e.g. 'Turn off Call Learning?'. (title token · text/primary)
4. Subject: Optional line naming what the dialog applies to. (caption · text/tertiary · 2 above (web))
5. Body: States the consequence. (body1 · text/secondary · 12 above web / 8 Compose)
6. Actions: Right-aligned text cancel and a filled commit (danger when destructive). (TextButton neutral text/secondary + Button md 36 · gap 20 web / 8 Compose · 24 above)
7. Snackbar: Inverse toast confirming the action afterwards, with an optional text action such as Undo. (bg text/primary · message body1 bg/surface · radius 12 · padding 12/16 · action button/secondary web, text/action Compose)

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: The box is role="alertdialog" and the title is an h2. Snackbar is role="status". Android: EqualDialog uses a platform Dialog window. The title is plain text with no heading(). EqualSnackbar is a plain Row.
- Name. Web: aria-label is the title. The body is not linked with aria-describedby. Button names come from their visible labels. Android: TalkBack reads the dialog content in order. Button labels come from their text.
- Keyboard. Web: Buttons are reachable with Tab. There is no Escape handler, focus is not moved into the dialog or trapped, and it is not returned on close. Android: The platform Dialog takes focus, and Back calls onDismissRequest. TalkBack: swipe between title, body and buttons, double-tap to activate.
- Touch target. Web: TextButton uses eq-touch (48). The md commit Button is 36px tall with no eq-touch. The Snackbar action uses eq-touch. Android: EqualButton and EqualTextButton apply minimumInteractiveComponentSize. The Snackbar action is clickable text with no minimum size.
- Contrast. Web: Body text/secondary 7.5:1 and subject text/tertiary 5.1:1 on bg/surface. The primary commit is 2.85:1 in light and fails, while danger is 6.2:1. The Snackbar action is lime on #111 in light (15.7:1) but green on #F7F7F7 in dark (2.66:1, fails). Android: Same dialog tokens. The Snackbar action uses text/action: green on #111 is 6.6:1 in light, but lime on #F7F7F7 is 1.13:1 in dark, which fails.
- State. Web: Destructive is shown by the danger fill and the verb in the label ('Delete'), not by colour alone. Android: Same: danger variant plus a named verb.
- Motion. Web: The dialog and snackbar have no animation. Android: The platform Dialog window uses the system animation, which follows the system animation scale.

Known accessibility gaps:
- Dialog.tsx: no Escape to cancel, no aria-modal, no focus move, trap or return, and the body is not linked via aria-describedby.
- The commit Button in Dialog.tsx is md (36px) with no eq-touch, so its hit height is 36.
- EqualDialogContent (Overlays.kt): the title has no heading() semantics.
- EqualSnackbar (Overlays.kt) has no liveRegion, so TalkBack does not announce it, and its action text has no 48dp minimum target.
- Snackbar action in dark mode fails contrast: button/secondary on text/primary is 2.66:1 (Dialog.tsx), and text/action lime on #F7F7F7 is 1.13:1 (Overlays.kt).
- Primary buttons put text/on-action white on button/primary #00B140 in light mode: 2.85:1, below AA 4.5:1 for 14sp text (Button.css / Buttons.kt). Dark (black on lime) is 17.4:1.

Example: Inline
```tsx
<Dialog open mode="inline" title="Turn off Call Learning?" subject="Call learning"
  body="Your assistant will stop learning from new calls. What it already knows stays until you clear it."
  confirmLabel="Turn off" />
```
```kotlin
// EqualDialogContent is the dialog surface without the window, for inline use
EqualDialogContent(
    title = "Turn off Call Learning?",
    subject = "Call learning",
    body = "Your assistant will stop learning from new calls. What it already knows stays until you clear it.",
    confirmLabel = "Turn off",
    onConfirm = {},
    onDismiss = {},
)
```

Example: Destructive
```tsx
<Dialog open mode="inline" destructive title="Delete address?" subject="Work"
  body="Your assistant will no longer share this address with delivery partners."
  confirmLabel="Delete" />
```
```kotlin
EqualDialogContent(
    title = "Delete address?",
    subject = "Work",
    body = "Your assistant will no longer share this address with delivery partners.",
    confirmLabel = "Delete",
    destructive = true,
    onConfirm = {},
    onDismiss = {},
)
```

Example: Overlay + snackbar
```tsx
<Dialog open={open} title="Turn off Call Learning?" confirmLabel="Turn off"
  onCancel={() => setOpen(false)}
  onConfirm={() => { setOpen(false); setToast('Call learning turned off'); }} />

{toast && <Snackbar message={toast} actionLabel="Undo" onAction={undo} />}
```
```kotlin
var open by remember { mutableStateOf(false) }
var toast by remember { mutableStateOf<String?>(null) }
EqualButton(text = "Turn off Call Learning", onClick = { toast = null; open = true })
if (open) {
    EqualDialog(
        onDismissRequest = { open = false },
        title = "Turn off Call Learning?",
        subject = "Call learning",
        body = "Your assistant will stop learning from new calls. What it already knows stays until you clear it.",
        confirmLabel = "Turn off",
        onConfirm = { open = false; toast = "Call learning turned off" },
    )
}
toast?.let { EqualSnackbar(message = it, actionLabel = "Undo", onActionClick = { toast = null }) }
```

Example: Snackbars
```tsx
<Snackbar message="Contact saved" />
<Snackbar message="Chat deleted" actionLabel="Undo" onAction={undo} />
```
```kotlin
Column(verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(12.dp)) {
    EqualSnackbar(message = "Contact saved")
    EqualSnackbar(message = "Chat deleted", actionLabel = "Undo", onActionClick = {})
}
```

entries.text:
# System notification (`system-notification`)
Group: Overlays

The Android heads-up notification Equal AI posts, drawn over the status bar in mocks and flows (e.g. “Equal AI Assistant is back on”).

- React: `import { SystemNotification } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `SystemNotificationPreview`
- Tokens: `component/notification/bg`, `text/primary`, `text/secondary`, `text/placeholder`
- Source: Flows: Temporarily Unavailable

Do: Keep the title under about 32 characters, so it fits on one line on a 360dp phone.

Don't: Don’t use it as an in-app toast; it stands for the OS notification.

Anatomy:
1. Shell: Rounded heads-up card. (radius 20 · padding 12 16 16 · component/notification/bg · shadow 0 8 28 / 0 1 3)
2. Header row: App name, dot and time. (micro 10 · text/primary · 3 dot text/placeholder · gap 6)
3. Orb: Equal app icon. (EqualOrb 32 · gap 10)
4. Title: Bold first line. (caption Bold · text/primary)
5. Body: Second line. (caption Regular · text/secondary)

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: role="alert" on the shell; orb is role=img. On a real device the OS draws and announces the notification. Android: No semantics beyond text; the real notification is posted with NotificationCompat.
- Name. Web: Read as app, time, "Equal AI" (orb), title and body. Android: App, time, title, body; orb contentDescription null.
- Keyboard. Web: Not interactive. Android: Not interactive in the preview.
- Contrast. Web: Title text/primary; body text/secondary 7.5:1 on white (dark 7.5:1). Android: Same tokens.
- State. Web: No state. Android: No state.
- Motion. Web: The shell has no animation; flows wrap it in .eq-heads-up (slide in), which is off under prefers-reduced-motion. Android: No animation.

Known accessibility gaps:
- role="alert" on a mock component makes screen readers interrupt as soon as a docs page or flow renders it (SystemStatus.tsx); use role="status" or none for mocks.

Example: Back on
```tsx
<SystemNotification title="Equal AI Assistant is back on"
  body="Equal AI is now handling all your unknown calls." />
```
```kotlin
// On a device, post a NotificationCompat instead; this preview is for mocks and flows
SystemNotificationPreview(
    title = "Equal AI Assistant is back on",
    body = "Equal AI is now handling all your unknown calls.",
)
```

entries.name: ai-summary-card
entries.title: AI summary card
entries.summary: The "Your AI Summary" card, prose the assistant wrote about the user, with empty, loading and ready states.
entries.text:
# AI summary card (`ai-summary-card`)
Group: You tab

The "Your AI Summary" card, prose the assistant wrote about the user, with empty, loading and ready states.

- React: `import { AiSummaryCard } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `AiSummaryCard`
- Tokens: `gradient/ai-summary`, `skeleton`, `text/primary`, `text/secondary`, `text/tertiary`
- Source: You tab · AI Summary card

Do: Write the summary in the assistant's voice, second person, short sentences. Use the loading state while the summary refreshes rather than hiding the card.

Don't: Don't show a stale summary with a spinner; use `status="loading"`. Don't use bullet lists; the summary is prose.

Anatomy:
1. Card: Soft green-tinted card for the summary. (gradient/ai-summary · radius 20 · padding 16 · min height 212 · gap 12)
2. Header: Orb and label. (orb 28 · caption · text/secondary · gap 8)
3. Body: Empty message, loading skeleton, or the summary prose. (bodyLarge text/primary · empty: Medium, centred)
4. Skeleton: Loading bars that pulse. (5 bars × 17 high · gap 4 · skeleton token · 0.95 ↔ 0.45 over 1.4s, staggered 90ms)
5. Footer: 'Last Updated: 8:06 AM' or 'Usually ready after your first few calls'. (caption Regular · text/tertiary · right-aligned)

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: A div with aria-busy while loading. The orb is role="img". The skeleton is a div with aria-label but no role. Android: A plain Column. EqualLogoOrb has contentDescription 'Equal AI'. The skeleton has no semantics.
- Name. Web: The orb reads 'Equal AI', then the label 'Your AI Summary'. 'Summary is updating' is on a div with no role, so many screen readers ignore it. Android: TalkBack reads 'Equal AI', 'Your AI Summary', the body and the footer.
- Keyboard. Web: Nothing is focusable. Android: TalkBack: swipe through the texts.
- Touch target. Web: Not interactive. Android: Not interactive.
- Contrast. Web: Body text/primary on the gradient passes. Footer text/tertiary is 4.6:1 at the #E6F7EA stop in light and 4.5:1 at #2F3423 in dark, both at the AA edge. Android: Same tokens.
- State. Web: Loading is exposed only through aria-busy; the footer text also changes to 'Last Updated'. Android: Loading is not exposed; only the footer text changes.
- Motion. Web: The skeleton pulses (eq-shimmer). Under reduced motion the base.css rule sets animation-duration to 0ms. Android: The skeleton pulse runs from rememberInfiniteTransition and does not check rememberReduceMotion().

Known accessibility gaps:
- AiSummaryCard in YouTab.tsx: the 'Summary is updating' aria-label sits on a div with no role. Use role="status" or visually hidden text so the loading state is announced.
- AiSummaryCard in YouTab.kt: the loading state has no semantics (stateDescription or contentDescription), so TalkBack can't tell it is updating.
- SummarySkeleton in YouTab.kt: the infinite pulse is not gated on rememberReduceMotion().

Example: Ready
```tsx
<AiSummaryCard summary="Your family calls you a lot. They always say it's urgent. They almost never say why." />
```
```kotlin
// Compose: status isn't inferred from summary; pass Ready explicitly
AiSummaryCard(
    status = AiSummaryStatus.Ready,
    summary = "Your family calls you a lot. They always say it's urgent. They almost never say why.",
)
```

Example: Empty
```tsx
<AiSummaryCard />
```
```kotlin
AiSummaryCard()
```

Example: Loading
```tsx
<AiSummaryCard status="loading" lastUpdated="8:06 AM" />
```
```kotlin
AiSummaryCard(status = AiSummaryStatus.Loading, lastUpdated = "8:06 AM")
```

entries.text:
# Contact info header (`contact-info-header`)
Group: You tab

The top of the Contact Info screen: a 96dp avatar, name, phone and a row of action tiles (Call, Mute, Save, Share).

- React: `import { ContactInfoHeader } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `ContactInfoHeader`
- Tokens: `bg/surface`, `stroke/subtle`, `text/action`, `text/primary`, `text/secondary`
- Source: Contact Info (Contact Info)

Do: Use the four tiles Call · Mute · Save · Share, with Material Symbols icons in text/action. Flip the Mute tile label to Unmute when the contact is muted.

Don't: Don't add more than four tiles; they share one row. Don't use emoji on the tiles; these are icon tiles, not action chips.

Anatomy:
1. Avatar: Initials avatar with the saved-contact badge, or category art for unknown callers. (96dp · initials 36sp on a tinted disc · person badge 35% of size)
2. Name: Contact or caller name. (22/28 Bold · text/primary · 10 above)
3. Phone: Phone number. (bodyLarge · text/tertiary · tabular)
4. Action tiles: Row of equal-width tiles: Call, Mute, Save, Share. (72 high · radius 8 · gap 12 · bg/surface · faint shadow, 1dp stroke/subtle in dark · 24 above)
5. Tile icon: Material Symbol for the action. (24dp · text/action)
6. Tile label: Action name; Mute flips to Unmute. (body1 · text/primary · 8 below the icon)

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: The name is an h1. Each tile is a <button>, and the icon is aria-hidden. The saved badge is role="img". Android: The name is plain text with no heading(). Tiles are clickable Columns with Role.Button that merge the icon and label.
- Name. Web: Tiles are named by their label. The category avatar's alt is the category name, and the saved badge's is 'Saved contact'. Android: Tiles are named by their label. The category avatar's contentDescription is the category label, and the saved badge's is 'Saved contact'.
- Keyboard. Web: Tab through the tiles, Enter/Space to activate. The focus ring comes from eq-reset-btn. Android: TalkBack: swipe to a tile, double-tap.
- Touch target. Web: Tiles are 72 tall and about 77 wide in the 390 frame. Android: Tiles are 72dp tall and share the row width.
- Contrast. Web: Name 18.9:1 and phone text/tertiary 5.1:1. Tile icons are text/action #00B140 on white: 2.85:1, under the 3:1 icon minimum. In dark the icons are lime on #222 (13.2:1). Android: Same tokens and ratios.
- State. Web: Mute shows its state through the label (Mute / Unmute), not through colour. Android: Same, via defaultContactInfoActions(muted).
- Motion. Web: Press scale (eq-pressable), 0ms under reduced motion. Android: eqPressFeedback on press.

Known accessibility gaps:
- ContactInfoHeader tile icons (Profile.tsx / Profile.kt): text/action #00B140 on white is 2.85:1 in light, under 3:1 for icons.
- ContactInfoHeader in Profile.kt: the name has no heading() semantics.

Example: Saved contact
```tsx
<ContactInfoHeader name="Amit Nanda" phone="+91 98717 46113" avatar={{ initials: 'AN' }}
  actions={[
    { icon: 'call', label: 'Call' },
    { icon: 'silent-mode', label: 'Mute' },
    { icon: 'person-add', label: 'Save' },
    { icon: 'share', label: 'Share' },
  ]} />
```
```kotlin
ContactInfoHeader(
    name = "Amit Nanda",
    phone = "+91 98717 46113",
    initials = "AN",
    actions = listOf(
        ContactInfoAction("Call", EqualIcons.Call, onClick = {}),
        ContactInfoAction("Mute", EqualIcons.SilentMode, onClick = {}),
        ContactInfoAction("Save", EqualIcons.PersonAdd, onClick = {}),
        ContactInfoAction("Share", EqualIcons.Share, onClick = {}),
    ),
)
```

Example: Unknown caller, with history
```tsx
<ContactInfoHeader name="Arnav Raj" phone="+91 98717 46113"
  avatar={{ category: 'career' }} actions={actions} />
<SectionHeader size="label" inset={22}>Call history</SectionHeader>
<CallHistoryList>
  <CallHistoryRow direction="incoming" meta="Today • 30 Sec." time="02:30 PM" />
  <CallHistoryRow direction="missed" meta="Yesterday" time="11:04 AM" />
</CallHistoryList>
```
```kotlin
ContactInfoHeader(
    name = "Arnav Raj",
    phone = "+91 98717 46113",
    category = EqualCategory.Career,
    // Call · Mute · Save · Share
    actions = defaultContactInfoActions(onCall = {}, onMute = {}, onSave = {}, onShare = {}),
)
SectionHeader(title = "Call history")
RowGroup {
    CallHistoryRow(direction = CallDirection.Incoming, meta = "Today • 30 Sec.", time = "02:30 PM")
    CallHistoryRow(direction = CallDirection.Missed, meta = "Yesterday", time = "11:04 AM")
}
```

entries.text:
# Plan card (`plan-card`)
Group: You tab

The dark card showing the user's current plan (Equal AI UNLIMITED, ₹149/Monthly), with a Manage plan action and an expired state.

- React: `import { PlanCard } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `PlanCard`
- Tokens: `plan-card/bg`, `plan-card/pill-stroke`, `plan-card/pattern`, `text/on-dark`, `text/on-dark-secondary`, `text/accent-gold`, `text/danger`
- Source: You tab · Plan card

Do: Show the price with the period ("₹149/Monthly"); it renders in tabular figures. Use the expired state with Manage plan so renewing is one tap.

Don't: Don't replace the coded gold pattern with an image. Don't place the plan card on a white surface; it belongs in the gold hero.

Anatomy:
1. Card: Dark card for the current plan. (plan-card/bg #2B2B2B · radius 20 · padding 14/16/16)
2. Gold pattern: Coded stepped gold lines on the right side (PlanPattern). (right 60% · plan-card/pattern · stroke 0.9 · fades 0 → 0.55 → 0.8)
3. Status pill: 'Current Plan', or 'Plan Expired' on a red fill. (24 high · radius 8 · 1dp plan-card/pill-stroke · white 4% fill · caption text/on-dark · expired: plan-card/expired-pill)
4. Manage plan: Underlined text action. (buttonSmall · text/on-dark · underline)
5. Product and tier: 'Equal AI UNLIMITED' with the tier in gold. (title · text/on-dark · tier text/accent-gold · 12 above)
6. Price: Price and period, e.g. '₹149/Monthly'. (caption Regular · text/on-dark-secondary · tabular)

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: A plain div. Manage plan is a <button>. The pattern SVG is aria-hidden. Android: A Box. Manage plan is clickable text with Role.Button. The pattern Canvas has no semantics.
- Name. Web: Manage plan is named by its label (actionLabel, default 'Manage plan'). Android: Named by manageLabel.
- Keyboard. Web: Tab to Manage plan, then Enter/Space. Android: TalkBack reads the pill, product, tier and price, then 'Manage plan, button'.
- Touch target. Web: Manage plan uses eq-touch, giving at least 48. Android: Manage plan is clickable text with no minimum size, about 16dp tall.
- Contrast. Web: text/on-dark 14.2:1, text/on-dark-secondary 6.1:1, accent-gold 6.5:1 (7.7:1 dark) on #2B2B2B. White on the expired pill is 5.1:1. The card looks the same in both themes. Android: Same tokens and ratios.
- State. Web: Expired shows as the text 'Plan Expired' as well as the red fill. Android: Same: the label changes to expiredLabel.
- Motion. Web: None. Android: None.

Known accessibility gaps:
- PlanCard in YouTab.kt: 'Manage plan' is clickable text with no minimumInteractiveComponentSize, so the target is well under 48dp.

Example: Current and expired
```tsx
<PlanCard onManage={managePlan} />
<PlanCard status="expired" onManage={managePlan} />
```
```kotlin
Column(verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(12.dp)) {
    PlanCard(onManageClick = {})
    // Compose: status="expired" is a Boolean flag
    PlanCard(expired = true, onManageClick = {})
}
```

Example: Custom tier
```tsx
<PlanCard tier="LITE" price="₹49/Monthly" />
```
```kotlin
PlanCard(tier = "LITE", price = "₹49/Monthly")
```

entries.text:
# Profile hero (`profile-hero`)
Group: You tab

The gold header at the top of the You tab (avatar, name, plan marker, edit, phone) that hosts the plan card, plus the compact ProfileHeader.

- React: `import { ProfileHero, ProfileHeader } from '@equal/ds';`
- Compose: `ProfileHero`, `ProfileHeader`
- Tokens: `gradient/profile-hero`, `gradient/gold`, `text/primary`, `text/secondary`
- Source: You tab · Profile hero

Do: Put the PlanCard inside the hero as children so it sits on the gold. Drive `avatar` from the gender chosen in Personal Details.

Don't: Don't add more actions to the hero row; edit is the only one. Don't format the phone number without tabular figures.

Anatomy:
1. Hero background: Gold gradient header with two faint arcs. In dark mode it becomes a panel with rounded bottom corners. (gradient/profile-hero · arcs r250/r290, 1.2 stroke, white 55% · padding 20 top, 12 sides · dark: radius 24 bottom, ends 56 above the bottom)
2. Avatar: ProfileAvatar: the gold-ringed avatar for paid users, the plain bust for free users. (70dp · tier paid when a plan is set)
3. Name: User's name. (headline · text/primary (light tokens in both themes) · truncates)
4. Plan badge: Plan marker, e.g. UNLIMITED. (PlanBadge · 16 high · gradient/gold · text/on-dark · badge token)
5. Edit button: Opens profile editing. (28dp · icon edit-profile 18 · text/primary web, text/secondary Compose)
6. Phone: Phone number. (body1 · text/secondary · tabular)
7. Footer slot: Holds the PlanCard so it sits on the gold. (16 below the row)
8. ProfileHeader: Compact version without the gold background. (avatar 56 · gap 16 web / 12 Compose · padding 16 web)

Accessibility:
- Role. Web: A <section>. The name is an h1, the arcs are aria-hidden, and Edit is an IconButton (<button>). Android: Plain Column. The name has no heading(). Edit is a clickable Box with Role.Button.
- Name. Web: The avatar's alt is 'Your profile', and the Edit button's aria-label is 'Edit profile'. Android: ProfileAvatar contentDescription is 'Your profile'. Edit has onClickLabel and an icon contentDescription of 'Edit profile'.
- Keyboard. Web: Tab reaches Edit, then Enter/Space. Android: TalkBack: swipe to 'Edit profile', double-tap.
- Touch target. Web: Edit is 28px with eq-touch, giving a 48 area. Android: Edit is a 28dp Box with clickable and no minimumInteractiveComponentSize, so the target is 28dp, despite the code comment.
- Contrast. Web: The content renders with light tokens in both themes (data-theme="light"): name #111 on #F8E4A2 is 14.9:1, phone text/secondary 5.9:1. The gold header stays light in dark mode. Android: The row renders under EqualTheme(darkTheme = false), so the ratios match web in both themes.
- State. Web: Plan shown as badge text, e.g. 'UNLIMITED'. Android: Plan shown as badge text.
- Motion. Web: None, apart from the eq-pressable press scale on Edit, which is 0ms under reduced motion. Android: None, apart from the press feedback.

Known accessibility gaps:
- HeroRow in YouTab.kt: the 28dp edit button has no minimumInteractiveComponentSize, so its target is 28dp, not 48.
- ProfileHero (YouTab.kt) and ProfileHeader (Profile.kt): the name has no heading() semantics, while web uses an h1.

Example: You tab hero with plan card
```tsx
<ProfileHero name="Keshav" phone="+91 98789 56749" onEdit={editProfile}>
  <PlanCard onManage={managePlan} />
</ProfileHero>
```
```kotlin
ProfileHero(name = "Keshav", phone = "+91 98789 56749", onEdit = {}) {
    PlanCard(onManageClick = {})
}
```

Example: Female avatar, no plan
```tsx
<ProfileHero name="Priya Sharma" phone="+91 99100 22114" avatar="female" plan={null} onEdit={editProfile} />
```
```kotlin
ProfileHero(
    name = "Priya Sharma",
    phone = "+91 99100 22114",
    avatar = ProfileAvatarVariant.Female,
    plan = null,
    onEdit = {},
)
```

Example: Compact header
```tsx
<ProfileHeader name="Keshav" phone="+91 98789 56749" />
```
```kotlin
ProfileHeader(name = "Keshav", phone = "+91 98789 56749")
```

What Chats shows while Equal AI is down, and how it tells you it’s back. Switch to Try it and tap “Notify me when ready” to run the whole flow.

# Flow: Instructions flow (`/flows/instructions`)

The hub, presets, the “Setting up instruction” chat and Active Instructions. Switch to Try it and apply an instruction end to end.

Source: Instructions

1. Hub: horizontal recommended cards (or “New suggestions coming…” once they’re all applied), an Active Instructions row, three presets and a pinned “Add New Instruction”.
2. Preset: the description plus instruction cards with When / Do rows and + Apply, which turns into Applied.
3. Setup chat, no input: You → Equal AI “Got it! Here’s your instruction:” → preview → ✍️ Edit / 👍 Confirm. Confirm adds ✅ and saves.
4. Setup chat, input needed: Equal AI asks each follow-up (the landmark, then the wait time); the answers are bolded in the preview → ✏️ Change something else / 👌 That’s all.
